title.rendered: Minecraft Java vs. Bedrock Edition: What’s the difference?

content.rendered:
Minecraft is all about exploring a massive world that’s made out of blocks, collecting resources, crafting items, building incredible structures, and taking on dangerous mobs. As a sandbox game, it gives you the freedom to play your way, whether you want to build an entire city or simply survive in the wild.

However, your experience depends partly on which edition you choose. Minecraft has two main editions: Java and Bedrock. Both offer the same core sandbox experience, but they differ in platform support, multiplayer, modding, controls, and graphics. If you’re wondering which one to choose, here’s everything you need to know about Minecraft Java vs. Bedrock Edition.

Minecraft Java vs. Bedrock Edition at a glance

What is the difference between Minecraft Java and Bedrock Edition?

Minecraft Java and Bedrock Edition bring the same basic sandbox experience, but each of them caters towards a different set of players.

For Java Edition, it runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux, which makes it a solid choice for anyone who wants to experiment with mods, join custom servers, slap on shaders, and explore all sorts of advanced gameplay features. Not only that, but you can also revisit older versions of Minecraft to see how the game has changed over time.

On the other hand, Bedrock Edition is available on Windows, consoles, and mobile devices, which makes cross-platform multiplayer much easier. Developer Mojang has specifically optimised this version to run across a range of hardware, and it also comes with the Minecraft Marketplace where players can purchase official add-ons, texture packs, maps, and cosmetic items.

Minecraft Java vs. Bedrock Edition: Every major difference explained

1. Supported platforms

One of the biggest differences between Minecraft Java and Bedrock Edition is platform availability.

Java Edition is designed for PC players and runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. It offers plenty of flexibility for players who want to customize their game and experiment with community-created content.

Bedrock Edition is available on Windows, Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch, and supported iOS and Android devices. This broader availability makes it easier to enjoy Minecraft on a console, computer, or phone.

If you primarily play on a console or mobile device, Bedrock is the version to choose. If you’re using a Mac or Linux computer, Java is the native edition available to you.

2. Crossplay

Both versions of Minecraft allow you to play with friends, but the way multiplayer works is different. In Java Edition, you can join all sorts of servers and explore different worlds, but everyone in your group must be playing on the same Java version.

However, Bedrock Edition allows you to team up with friends across supported devices. For instance, you can play Minecraft on your PlayStation while your friend joins the same world from an Android phone, as long as you’re both using Bedrock Edition.

3. Mods vs. add-ons

Mods have been a huge part of Minecraft Java Edition for a decade, with the community pumping out new ways to change the game. Right from bringing new mobs, items, dimensions and skins to overhauling gameplay performance and changing existing mechanics, Java Edition allows you to mod almost every single aspect of the game.

However, the Bedrock Edition doesn’t follow the same approach. What you instead get is the Minecraft Marketplace. This is where Mojang offers community-made content, including skins, texture packs, and gameplay add-onset, which can be bought with real money. Sure, there’s a lot to explore, but the selection is limited, and you have to pay.

4. Performance and FPS

Minecraft Bedrock Edition is built from the ground up to run across a wide range of platforms, which includes the likes of consoles, mobile devices, and PCs. This means it’s well optimised to run even on relatively low-end hardware, which makes it a solid choice for anyone who wants an experience without worrying about performance.

The Java edition is a more demanding version for any system. This is especially noticeable when you install multiple mods or use shaders to change up the game’s visuals. However, the performance ultimately comes down to your hardware, graphics settings, and the number of mods you’re running

5. Graphics, shaders and visual features

The two Minecraft editions have the same blocky art style, with the same textures and environments. However, the Java edition brings the freedom to change how the game looks through community-made shader packs. These can transform the way lighting, shadows, and reflections work in the game. Most of the mods are available for free and help give your world a fresh look.

Bedrock Edition also allows you to change the game’s visuals. You can easily enable the Vibrant Visuals option through the settings or even explore community-made shaders and add-onset. However, the range of customisation options is more limited compared to Java Edition.

6. Servers and realms

Minecraft Java Edition has no shortage of servers packed with different ways to experience the game. Whether you’re into RPGs, survival challenges, or competitive PVP, there’s something for everyone. If you’re looking for a place to start, check out our list of the best Minecraft servers to find one that suits your playstyle.

Bedrock Edition has no shortage of multiplayer servers either, with the added benefit of cross-platform support. However, the variety of servers and custom game modes available generally is more limited than what you’ll find in Java Edition.

Both versions also come with Minecraft Realms. For the unaware, this is a subscription service that lets you set up private worlds and invite your friends over to play.

Minecraft Java vs. Bedrock: Which edition is better for mods?

If you’re comparing Minecraft Java vs. Bedrock and modding is your top priority, the Java edition is the clear winner. Its modding community has been around for over a decade, giving players access to an endless collection of custom content. You can bring in new biomes, weapons, machines, and even gameplay systems that can’t be found in the core experience.

If that wasn’t enough, you can even bring in aspects of other game franchises into Minecraft with modding. What’s the best part about all of this? Most of these mods are generally free to download, which means you can experiment with countless ways to switch up your gameplay and have a blast.

Minecraft Java vs. Bedrock: Which is better for multiplayer?

If playing with friends is your main priority, Minecraft Bedrock Edition is without a doubt the version to purchase. Its biggest advantage is simply the fact that it is cross-platform. It doesn’t matter whether your friends are on a PC, Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch or a mobile phone; as long as they own the Bedrock edition, you can play together. Everyone gets access to the same world and multiplayer features.

What’s also great about Bedrock, particularly on consoles, is that players get access to split-screen multiplayer. This means the game can be enjoyed with friends and family on the screen without needing separate devices.

Can you switch between Minecraft Java and Bedrock Edition?

Still can’t pick between Minecraft Java and Bedrock Edition? Don’t worry, as you don’t have to choose just one. If you’re playing on PC, buying Minecraft gives you access to both editions at no additional cost. In order to switch between them, simply launch the official Minecraft Launcher and select your preferred version from the sidebar.

However, keep in mind that both editions store their game files, saved worlds, and progress separately. This means your worlds, settings, and progress won’t automatically transfer when you switch from one edition to another.

Wrapping up!

Minecraft offers two editions with the same core sandbox appeal but different strengths. Neither is universally better; the right choice depends on how you prefer to play.

Choose Java Edition if you want extensive mods, shader packs, community servers, and the flexibility to experiment with different game versions. Choose Bedrock Edition if you want to play across supported devices, use controller or touch controls, enjoy console split-screen, or access its Marketplace and official Vibrant Visuals mode on compatible hardware.

If you’re playing on a Windows PC, you can get both editions in the Java & Bedrock Edition for PC package. That gives you the flexibility to choose whichever version suits your next Minecraft adventure.

FAQs

Is Minecraft Java better than Bedrock?

Minecraft Java is suited for players who like to install mods and join custom servers. However, Minecraft Bedrock is suited for players with lower-end systems and who want to play with friends across different devices.

Can Java and Bedrock players play together?

Unfortunately, Minecraft Java and Bedrock players can’t play together as they use different multiplayer systems.

Which Minecraft edition has better performance?

Minecraft Bedrock Edition generally has better performance as it’s been optimised to run across a range of hardware and platforms.

Can you install mods on Minecraft Bedrock Edition?

You can install mods on Minecraft Bedrock Edition using add-onset, which can introduce new items, blocks, textures, and other mechanics into your world. These are available on the Minecraft Marketplace and third-party sources.

Is Minecraft Java Edition available on consoles?

No, Minecraft Java Edition is not available to play on Xbox, PlayStation or Nintendo consoles.

Do Java and Bedrock have the same updates?

Minecraft Java and Bedrock do get the same major updates. However, some features can differ and arrive at different times.

Can you convert a Java world to Bedrock?

A Java world can be converted to Bedrock Edition using third-party tools such as Chunker. However, keep in mind that the conversion might not be perfect, and modded entities or Java-specific mechanics might not transfer.

content.rendered:
Apple has unveiled a redesigned MacBook Pro with a new PROLED XDR display, tandem OLED technology, and touch support for the first time on a Mac. Alongside the new hardware, the announcement has brought a fresh collection of colorful wallpapers featuring glossy abstract shapes, metallic curves, and vibrant artwork.

If you want to give your desktop a similar look without upgrading your Mac, you’re in the right place. I’ve collected six new MacBook Pro PROLED XDR wallpapers featuring everything from the silver-and-blue design to a luminous green butterfly and flowing purple-and-green patterns. You can download your favorite design and use it on your MacBook, iMac, Windows PC, or another desktop display.

Download MacBook Pro PROLED XDR wallpapers

This collection features not only the official MacBook Pro 2026 wallpaper designed by Apple, but also several amazing wallpapers. Choose your favorites and give your desktop a fresh visual upgrade.

You may find the original wallpaper collection and previews on AppleWalls, an independent archive of Apple wallpapers.

1. Silver and blue PRO wallpaper

Let’s start with the official artwork for Apple’s new MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR display. Its flowing, metallic lines against a deep black background create a sleek, minimal look. Perfect for giving your desktop a dark, premium finish.

Download

2. Colorful abstract design

A vibrant mix of pink, orange, blue, and purple gives this wallpaper an energetic, bold appearance. It features many layers of shapes and elements, reminding me of an underwater theme. I’d choose this one if I wanted a colorful desktop that immediately catches the eye.

Download

3. Glass abstract artwork

This wallpaper combines a deep black background with glossy, sculptural shapes in red, silver, green, and electric blue. The flowing metallic curves and textured surfaces give it a unique look without making the screen feel too busy.

Download

4. Glass dolphin and microphone on the screen

A transparent, glass-like dolphin stretches across the top, while a red sphere and golden geometric form add contrast in this unusual 3D artwork. The shiny silver and blue surfaces keep the composition neat against the black background.

Download

5. Beautiful green butterfly

This nature-inspired wallpaper features a striking butterfly with luminous green wings, purple edges, and pink highlights. The textures are so elaborate that they create an ethereal feel, while the deep green background makes its bright colors pop.

Download

6. Purple and green flow wallpaper

The next abstract design combines beautiful contrasting colors to form flowing, feather-like shapes. The composition is detailed enough to create a sense of movement, making it a good choice if you prefer artistic wallpapers over simple gradients.

Download

Give your Mac a fresh look

Whether you prefer the understated silver-and-blue design or a more colorful abstract composition, these six MacBook Pro PROLED XDR wallpapers offer an easy way to refresh your desktop. Their combination of rich colors, glossy textures, and dark backgrounds makes them appealing choices for a MacBook, iMac, or Windows PC.

If you’re curious about the hardware behind the new wallpapers, read our guide to the touchscreen MacBook Pro for more details about its display and other upgrades.

mainEntity.name: Is Minecraft Java better than Bedrock?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minecraft Java is suited for players who like to install mods and join custom servers. However, Minecraft Bedrock is suited for players with lower-end systems and who want to play with friends across different devices.

mainEntity.name: Can Java and Bedrock players play together?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unfortunately, Minecraft Java and Bedrock players can't play together as they use different multiplayer systems.

mainEntity.name: Which Minecraft edition has better performance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minecraft Bedrock Edition generally has better performance as it's been optimised to run across a range of hardware and platforms.

mainEntity.name: Can you install mods on Minecraft Bedrock Edition?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can install mods on Minecraft Bedrock Edition using add-onset, which can introduce new items, blocks, textures, and other mechanics into your world. These are available on the Minecraft Marketplace and third-party sources.

mainEntity.name: Is Minecraft Java Edition available on consoles?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Minecraft Java Edition is not available to play on Xbox, PlayStation or Nintendo consoles.

mainEntity.name: Do Java and Bedrock have the same updates?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minecraft Java and Bedrock do get the same major updates. However, some features can differ and arrive at different times.

mainEntity.name: Can you convert a Java world to Bedrock?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Java world can be converted to Bedrock Edition using third-party tools such as Chunker. However, keep in mind that the conversion might not be perfect, and modded entities or Java-specific mechanics might not transfer.

title.rendered: Build a Phone Empire codes (October 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Build a Phone Empire codes on October 29, 2026

Build a Phone Empire on Roblox is a must-try for tycoon game fans! You start from a small garage and gradually turn into a massive smartphone company. From designing your phones and choosing their specifications to hiring employees and researching new technologies, there’s plenty to keep you hooked.

However, growing your business requires tons of coins and Research Points (RP), which can take time to earn. But there’s no need to worry, as here’s a list of all Build a Phone Empire codes that you can redeem for free coins and RP.

All working Build a Phone Empire codes

  • COMPANIES: 38,000 Cash and 60 RP
  • CEO: Cash and RP
  • WELCOME: 38,000 Cash and 60 RP
  • LAPTOPS: 75,000 Cash and 90 RP

As of now, these are the only active Build a Phone Empire codes available. Make sure to redeem them as soon as possible, as codes can expire without warning, leaving you unable to claim their rewards.

Expired Build a Phone Empire codes

There are currently no confirmed expired codes in the sources checked for this guide. We’ll move codes to this section when reliable reports indicate that they no longer work.

How to redeem Build a Phone Empire codes in Roblox

Now that you’re aware of the active codes, it’s also crucial to learn how to redeem them and claim your freebies. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to redeem Build a Phone Empire codes in Roblox.

  1. Fire up Build a Phone Empire on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Click on Store.
  4. Choose the Codes section.
  5. Paste a working code and hit Redeem to claim your reward.

If the code is accepted, the corresponding rewards should be credited to your account. Check your Cash and Research Points balances to confirm the rewards have been added.

Why aren’t my Build a Phone Empire codes working?

If your Build a Phone Empire codes aren’t working, double-check that you’ve entered them exactly as listed above. Keep in mind that these codes are case-sensitive, so make sure there are no extra spaces before or after them.

You can simply copy and paste the codes directly from our list. If a code still doesn’t work, it might have expired, or you may have already redeemed its rewards.

How to get more Build a Phone Empire codes

The developers don’t follow a fixed schedule for releasing new Build a Phone Empire codes. Most codes are released to celebrate major game updates, seasonal events, bug fixes, or community milestones.

To stay updated, you can:

  • Join the official Discord server: Visit the Build a Phone Empire Discord server to find announcements and newly released codes.
  • Follow the Roblox game page: Make sure to keep an eye on the Roblox page and the Devtech Studios community for updates, announcements, and potential code releases.
  • Bookmark this page: We’ll update this guide whenever new Build a Phone Empire codes become available, so you can easily find the latest rewards in one place.

If you’re looking for more Roblox freebies, check out our latest Hollow codes, Cat Battles Codes, and our complete Roblox Game Codes hub.

FAQs

How do you get better phones in Build a Phone Empire?

In order to get better phones in Build a Phone Empire, you need to research new technologies to get improved components, better cameras, processors, and other features.

Can you customize your phone in Build a Phone Empire?

Build a Phone Empire lets you customize your smartphones by choosing their screen size, cameras, corners, buttons, colour, finish and logo.

How do you earn money in Build a Phone Empire?

You can earn money in Build a Phone Empire by designing and launching smartphones, then making profits from sales.

mainEntity.name: Is Minecraft Java better than Bedrock?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minecraft Java is suited for players who like to install mods and join custom servers. However, Minecraft Bedrock is suited for players with lower-end systems and who want to play with friends across different devices.

mainEntity.name: Can Java and Bedrock players play together?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unfortunately, Minecraft Java and Bedrock players can't play together as they use different multiplayer systems.

mainEntity.name: Which Minecraft edition has better performance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minecraft Bedrock Edition generally has better performance as it's been optimised to run across a range of hardware and platforms.

mainEntity.name: Can you install mods on Minecraft Bedrock Edition?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can install mods on Minecraft Bedrock Edition using add-onset, which can introduce new items, blocks, textures, and other mechanics into your world. These are available on the Minecraft Marketplace and third-party sources.

mainEntity.name: Is Minecraft Java Edition available on consoles?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Minecraft Java Edition is not available to play on Xbox, PlayStation or Nintendo consoles.

mainEntity.name: Do Java and Bedrock have the same updates?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minecraft Java and Bedrock do get the same major updates. However, some features can differ and arrive at different times.

mainEntity.name: Can you convert a Java world to Bedrock?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Java world can be converted to Bedrock Edition using third-party tools such as Chunker. However, keep in mind that the conversion might not be perfect, and modded entities or Java-specific mechanics might not transfer.

title.rendered: GTA 6 PS5 file size revealed: How much storage do you need?

content.rendered:
Rockstar Games has been sharing details about GTA 6 ahead of its launch, but one question remains on many players’ minds: how much storage space will the game require? Rumors have suggested different file sizes, but Rockstar hasn’t officially confirmed the game’s download or installation size yet.

Now, a new report from PlayStation Game Size, an account known for tracking information from PlayStation Store listings, claims that GTA 6’s Standard Edition could require a 210 GB download on PS5. With the game’s release approaching, this gives players an early idea of how much storage they may need to free up. However, the figure remains unconfirmed, so here’s what we know so far.

GTA 6 PS5 file size at a glance

The 210 GB figure comes from a third-party PlayStation Store tracking account, not an official Rockstar announcement. The suggested 250 GB of free space is a practical precaution rather than a confirmed system requirement.

How much storage does GTA 6 need on PS5?

According to PlayStationsize on X, GTA 6 Standard Edition could take 210 GB of storage on the PS5. Although Sony hasn’t listed the game’s official storage requirements yet, the insider has a fairly reliable track record for uncovering such details. The information has been pulled from Sony’s backend, where game-related details surface before an official announcement. However, as always, Rockstar could still make changes before launch, so it’s best to treat this figure as unconfirmed for now.

🚨 Grand Theft Auto VI – 𝐃𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐝 𝐒𝐢𝐳𝐞 : 210 GB – 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐫𝐝 ($79.99) Pre-Load : November 12 Release : November 19 𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐓𝐢𝐦𝐞 : Midnight https://t.co/5vXkgnqfC7

— PlayStation Game Size (@PlaystationSize) October 27, 2026

If this figure is true, GTA 6 takes a massive jump in file size compared to previous Rockstar games. For context, GTA 5 takes up around 95 GB, and Red Dead Redemption 2 requires 105 GB on PS5. However, considering the scale of GTA 6, its highly detailed world, and everything we’ve seen in the official trailers and leaks, a larger file size isn’t all that shocking. Rockstar is going all out when it comes to this open-world, and all that detail is bound to require a lot of storage space.

When can you preload GTA 6 on PS5?

Rockstar has confirmed that GTA 6 preloading will begin on November 12, 2026, which is exactly seven days before the game’s scheduled release.

Considering the GTA 6 file size could be as large as 210 GB, downloading it in advance will give you plenty of time to get things ready, especially if you’re using a slower internet connection.

The same applies if you’re purchasing the physical edition, as it comes with a download code. You will be able to preload the game starting on the same date, giving you enough time to download the files before launch day.

If you’re still deciding which version to buy, check out our guide to GTA 6 editions and what each version includes.

Will GTA 6 have the same file size on PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S?

Insiders haven’t reported the GTA 6 file size for Xbox Series X/S consoles yet, but it’s likely close to what we’ve seen reported for the PS5. Looking at Rockstar’s previous releases, the storage requirements on PlayStation and Xbox consoles have generally been in the same ballpark.

For instance, GTA 5 took 44 GB on PS4 at launch, while the Xbox One version required 42 GB. There’s no guarantee the same will hold true for GTA 6, but we don’t expect a massive difference between the two versions.

However, the file size isn’t the only thing worth considering when comparing the platforms. PS5 and PS5 Pro owners will be able to enjoy exclusive GTA 6 features, which allow the game to take full advantage of Sony’s hardware compared to the Xbox Series X/S.

Will GTA 6’s file size increase after launch?

If you think 210 GB of storage is all you’ll need for GTA 6, you might want to think again. It’s likely that the GTA 6 file size is going to increase after launch, as Rockstar will release updates, bug fixes, and additional content.

These updates can bring new things to the table, such as missions, vehicles, and other features that take up even more space on your console. Then there’s also GTA 6 Online, which is expected to arrive in 2027 and could increase the game’s overall storage requirements.

The developer hasn’t announced a post-launch update schedule or confirmed how much additional storage GTA 6 will need. However, you should keep some extra SSD space available rather than assuming that the 210 GB figure is all you’ll need.

Wrapping up

Rockstar Games hasn’t officially revealed GTA 6’s file size yet, but PlayStation Game Size has reported that the Standard Edition could require a 210 GB download on PS5. If the figure proves accurate, players will need to set aside a significant amount of storage before launch.

Rockstar has confirmed that preloading begins at local midnight on November 12, 2026, ahead of the game’s November 19 release. Until the official storage requirements are published, treat the reported size as provisional and leave some extra space for installation and future updates.

FAQs

What is the GTA 6 file size on PS5?

The GTA 6 file size on PS5 is reportedly 210 GB, according to PlayStationsize on X. However, Rockstar Games hasn’t confirmed the figure yet.

How much free storage should I keep for GTA 6?

As GTA 6 is rumoured to be around 210 GB on PS5, we’d recommend keeping at least 250 GB of free storage to be safe. This also covers potential updates.

When does GTA 6 preload start on PS5?

The GTA 6 preload on PS5 begins on November 12, 2026. This gives players a full week to download the game before launch.

Can I preload GTA 6 before its release date?

Yes, you can preload GTA 6 before its official release date, which allows you to download the game in advance. Preloading begins on November 12, 2026.

Will GTA 6 have the same file size on PS5 Pro?

It’s likely that the GTA 6 file size on the PS5 Pro will also be 210 GB, the same as the standard PS5.

How much storage does GTA 6 need on Xbox Series X|S?

No reports have surfaced suggesting GTA 6’s file size requirements for Xbox Series X/S. However, it’s likely that the game will need a similar amount of storage as it does on PS5 to run.

title.rendered: Apple’s iPhone Duo could grab nearly 30% of foldable market in 2027

content.rendered:
Apple’s first foldable iPhone could become a major force in the foldable smartphone market faster than expected. According to market research firm TrendForce, the iPhone Duo is projected to capture 29.8% of the global foldable smartphone market in 2027, putting Apple in second place behind Samsung.

The forecast comes as early demand for the iPhone Duo appears strong, with delivery estimates on Apple’s website extending into January 2027 for some orders less than a week after preorders opened on October 16. But while brand appeal will help Apple succeed, display reliability and the long-term durability of its folding design remain key challenges.

Apple could challenge Samsung’s foldable dominance

In its latest report on the iPhone Duo’s launch and foldable display challenges, TrendForce estimates that Apple could ship around 5 million foldable iPhones in 2026, giving it approximately 24.8% of the market. Its 2027 projection raises Apple’s expected share to 29.8%.

Samsung is still expected to lead the market, although its projected share could decline from 35.1% in 2026 to 31.9% in 2027. Huawei’s share is also forecast to fall, from 24.8% to 21.3%.

The shift could make Apple one of the most influential players in a market long dominated by established Android foldable manufacturers.

The foldable market could rebound in 2027

TrendForce expects global foldable smartphone shipments to reach 23.5 million units in 2027, representing year-over-year growth of 16.3%. That would be a significant improvement over the just 0.5% growth TrendForce projected for 2026 in its previous forecast.

Apple’s entry could help revive demand by bringing foldable phones to a wider audience. Its integration of hardware, software, and developer tools may also give it an advantage as manufacturers compete to make larger foldable displays more useful for everyday multitasking.

Still, hurdles remain. TrendForce’s latest assessment highlights reports of damaged inner displays, potentially expensive repairs, and apps that do not fully adapt to the Duo’s unfolded screen. TrendForce also notes that Apple has replaced a small number of units with inner-display abnormalities. These issues could become defining factors in how consumers view the iPhone Duo in the long run.

Can Apple turn early demand into long-term success?

The iPhone Duo’s early market performance suggests that Apple could quickly become a serious competitor in foldable smartphones. But capturing nearly 30% of the market in 2027 remains a forecast, not a guaranteed outcome.

Ultimately, Apple’s success will depend on whether it can deliver a reliable folding display, improve app compatibility, and make its larger screen genuinely useful. If it gets those fundamentals right, the iPhone Duo could help push the foldable market beyond hardware experimentation and toward a more practical, multitasking-focused smartphone experience.

acceptedAnswer.text: Minecraft Java is suited for players who like to install mods and join custom servers. However, Minecraft Bedrock is suited for players with lower-end systems and who want to play with friends across different devices.

title.rendered: How to get the Inoxtag skin in Fortnite: Price and bundle details

content.rendered:
Popular French creator Inoxtag is the latest online personality to join Fortnite as an in-game outfit. It’s a milestone moment for the creator, who first gained recognition through his Fortnite videos.

As part of this Fortnite collaboration, players can get more than just Inoxtag’s outfit. The collection also includes Ace’s Cozy Pack back bling, inspired by his pet dog, along with a pickaxe, an emote, and a themed wrap.

The Inoxtag outfit costs 1,500 V-Bucks, while the full Inoxtag Bundle costs 2,000 V-Bucks. The outfit also includes the Inoxtag’d wrap, so you don’t need to purchase that cosmetic separately if you buy the skin. The collection is available in the Item Shop until November 5, 2026, so here’s how to get the outfit and everything included in the collaboration.

Steps to claim the Inoxtag skin in Fortnite

Follow these steps to purchase the Inoxtag outfit from the Fortnite Item Shop:

  1. In Fortnite, go to the Shop tab.
  2. Next, scroll down to the Inoxtag section and select the Inoxtag skin.
  3. Finally, confirm your decision by pressing and holding the Purchase button.

You can purchase the Inoxtag outfit individually for 1,500 V-Bucks or get the full bundle for 2,000 V-Bucks. If you want the other cosmetics as well, the bundle is the better-value option.

List of all Fortnite x Inoxtag cosmetics

The Inoxtag collection includes five cosmetics: the outfit, its accompanying wrap, a back bling, a pickaxe, and an emote. Here’s a breakdown of their prices and bundle availability.

1. Inoxtag outfit

  • Price: 1,500 V-Bucks
  • Also includes: Inoxtag’d wrap
  • Also included in: Inoxtag Bundle

2. Ace’s Cozy Pack back bling

  • Price: 600 V-Bucks
  • Also included in: Inoxtag Bundle

3. Kaizen Mountain Axes pickaxe

  • Price: 800 V-Bucks
  • Also included in: Inoxtag Bundle

4. Lil’ 4×4 emote

  • Price: 500 V-Bucks
  • Also included in: Inoxtag Bundle

5. Inoxtag’d wrap

  • Price: 500 V-Bucks
  • Also included in: Inoxtag Bundle

Fortnite creator collaborations in 2026

A wide variety of internet celebrities, from highly sought-after streamers such as Ninja to eminent TikTok figures such as Khaby Lame, have previously collaborated with Fortnite, resulting in their likenesses appearing in the game.

Meanwhile, when we talk about 2026 specifically, we have witnessed fresh cosmetics inspired by three different creators, namely Kai Cenat, IShowSpeed and now Inoxtag. All these skins are part of the Icon tier, which is a category also shared by the sportsperson-based skins and the singer-based skins in Fortnite.

While only a few creator-based Icon skins have arrived in the game this year so far, the cadence has been noticeably more prolific when it comes to content modeled around singers and rappers, with big names including Lil Wayne and Olivia Rodrigo coming into the fold this year.

On the other hand, sportspersons have faced a similar fate as creators in this regard, as this year saw just a couple of new footballers, namely Vinicius Jr and David Beckham, enter the fray despite it being a FIFA World Cup year.

FAQs

How to get the Inoxtag Fortnite skin for free?

The Inoxtag outfit was available as a free reward for eligible players who achieved the required placement in the Inoxtag Icon Cup. That tournament has already taken place. The current Item Shop options are the outfit for 1,500 V-Bucks or the full bundle for 2,000 V-Bucks.

How to get the Inoxtag Fortnite wrap?

The Inoxtag’d wrap is included with the Inoxtag outfit and the Inoxtag Bundle. It also has a listed standalone price of 500 V-Bucks, but purchasing the outfit means you don’t need to buy the wrap separately.

Which other creators have previously done a similar collaboration with Fortnite?

Fortnite has featured online creators such as Ninja, MrBeast, Kai Cenat, and IShowSpeed in its crossover lineup. The available collaborations and their Item Shop schedules can change over time.

title.rendered: Upcoming Apple products in 2026: Full list of what to expect

content.rendered:
Apple’s 2026 product lineup has turned out to be much bigger than a typical iPhone refresh.

After months of rumors, Apple has officially unveiled a brand-new smart display lineup called HomeView, along with the HomePod mini 2, a new Apple TV 4K, and an updated Siri Remote. We also got the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, its first foldable iPhone Duo, Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4, and AirPods 5.

That is only part of the story. Apple has already refreshed several Macs and iPads this year, including the iPad mini with an OLED display, M6 iMac, 14-inch MacBook Pro M6, MacBook Neo, MacBook Pro M5 Pro & M5 Max, MacBook Air M5, iPad Air M4, Mac mini M6 & M5 Pro, and Mac Studio M5 Max & M5 Ultra.

However, the list doesn’t end here. Here, I have shared all the upcoming Apple products that are still rumored or expected so you can quickly see what you should still wait for.

Apple products still expected later in 2026

Apple’s September event has already eliminated many of the biggest unknowns surrounding its 2026 lineup.

However, several products are still expected or rumored at the end of the year, from October to December, with no officially confirmed launch dates.

MacBook Pro with M6 Pro and M6 Max

Apple has already introduced the M6 chip in the Mac mini, so the next major step is bringing M6-class silicon to Apple’s professional laptops.

A redesigned MacBook Pro with M6 Pro and M6 Max chips is expected later in 2026. Reports have suggested a thinner, lightweight design, OLED displays, and potentially even a touchscreen, packed with next-gen features like cellular support.

If the redesigned MacBook Pro arrives this year, it could become one of Apple’s biggest Mac upgrades in several years.

iPad 12th Generation with Apple Intelligence

The Apple iPad 12th generation is expected to be Apple’s next entry-level tablet.

Rumors suggest it will feature a powerful A18 chip, which could enable Apple Intelligence AI features, Stage Manager 2, Wi-Fi 7, improved multitasking, and smoother everyday performance.

The device is also expected to include around 8GB of RAM, making it better suited for productivity, creative apps, and advanced iPadOS features.

While the overall design may remain similar to the current model, the new iPad could still offer an 11-inch Liquid Retina display, 12MP cameras, and Touch ID, along with improved efficiency.

Apple Display Products

  • Apple Studio Display 2 with mini‑LED back lighting, ProMotion support (120Hz), Thunderbolt 5, and 5K resolution.

Apple products that could arrive in 2027 or later

Not everything Apple is working on is necessarily coming in 2026. These products are strongly rumored but don’t yet have a clear launch quarter:

MacBook Ultra

The rumored MacBook Ultra might turn out to be the company’s most ambitious Mac laptop yet. Current design reports point to a thinner body, OLED display, and touchscreen support, potentially making it the first Mac with a touchscreen.

The laptop is also rumored to replace the familiar display notch with an iPhone-style Dynamic Island, while Apple could explore built-in cellular connectivity. Recent reports suggest the first model may use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.

The MacBook Ultra is expected to sit above the MacBook Pro in Apple’s lineup and be more expensive. The launch date is not clear, but according to current information, the product might be announced in late 2026 or early 2027.

AirPods Pro with Cameras

AirPods Pro with on-device cameras for visual AI features and improved spatial intelligence are expected to debut this year.

Apple is reportedly developing multiple versions of camera-equipped AirPods, including models identified by the code names B790 and B798. A leaked video found in macOS Tahoe 26.7 appears to demonstrate the technology, showing a user looking at a book while Siri uses Visual Intelligence to recognize and remember it.

Apple Glasses / AR Wearable

Apple’s long-anticipated AR glasses may be unveiled, potentially late in 2026 or teased for a 2027 ship window.

AR devices

  • Targeting a 2027 launch, Vision Air could serve as a lightweight and budget-friendly alternative to Vision Pro. It is expected to be ~40% lighter with a magnesium alloy or plastic frame and likely powered by an A-series chip.

Why 2026 is such an important year for Apple

Apple’s strategy in 2026 is shaping up to be more aggressive, category-expanding, and ecosystem-wide than in typical years. The combination of staple updates (like iPhones and Macs), breakthrough category bets (foldable, Apple Glasses, smart home hubs), and AI-oriented experiences places 2026 as a pivotal year for consumer hardware and Apple’s long-term vision.

Bookmark this article; we’ll keep it updated as more rumors and confirmations roll in. Got a favorite from the list? Let us know in the comments!

acceptedAnswer.text: Minecraft Java is suited for players who like to install mods and join custom servers. However, Minecraft Bedrock is suited for players with lower-end systems and who want to play with friends across different devices.

title.rendered: Mac processor history: How Apple transformed computing

content.rendered:
When you think of a Mac today, you probably imagine a fast, powerful machine powered by Apple’s latest M6 chip, Apple’s first 2-nanometer processor, which now ships in the Mac mini, iMac, and 14-inch MacBook Pro. But Macs weren’t always this advanced. Their journey began in 1984 with the Motorola 68K series, a much simpler processor. Over the years, Apple transitioned to PowerPC, then Intel, and finally its own Apple silicon chips.

In this article, we’ll explore how Mac processors have evolved over time. You’ll see how each new chip improved speed, graphics, and memory, shaping the powerful Macs we use today.

2020–Present: Apple Silicon

On June 22, 2020, Apple CEO Tim Cook announced a two-year transition plan to move from Intel processors to Apple silicon. The goal was to create an all-Apple ecosystem by replacing Intel’s x86-64 architecture with Apple’s own ARM64-based chips.

Staying true to its timeline, Apple introduced its first Apple-designed Mac chip, M1, in November 2020. This was followed by more powerful M1 variants in 2021 and 2022. Apple then launched the M2, M3, M4, M5, and M6 chipsets, further pushing the boundaries of performance.

In March 2026, Apple also launched the $599 MacBook Neo, the first Mac sold to consumers that runs on an iPhone-class A18 Pro chip instead of an M-series chip. See how it stacks up in our MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air comparison.

Here’s a detailed table outlining the evolution of Mac processors, from the latest Apple M6 back to the M1:

M6 Chip Family: M6

M6 (August 2026)

Apple’s M6 is the company’s first chip built using a state-of-the-art 2-nanometer process, bringing major improvements in CPU, GPU, storage and AI performance. It features a 12-core CPU (2 super, 4 performance and 6 efficiency cores), delivering up to 1.2x faster multithreaded performance than M5, and a 12-core GPU, with two additional cores compared with M5.

AI is one of the biggest focuses of M6. The chip features an all-new Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says delivers up to 2x the peak AI compute of the previous generation. Combined with the Neural Accelerators in the GPU, M6 is built to handle local AI workloads and next-generation Apple Intelligence features more efficiently.

Memory and storage performance have also been upgraded. Mac mini with M6 starts with 16GB of unified memory, configurable up to 32GB, while memory bandwidth reaches up to 170GB/s. Apple also claims up to 2x faster storage compared with the previous generation. If you’re weighing an upgrade, read our M6 Mac mini vs M4 Mac mini comparison.

After debuting in the Mac mini on August 25, 2026, M6 arrived in the new iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro on October 27, 2026, with both shipping from November 6. The entry iMac uses a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU version of the chip.

M5 Chip Family: M5, M5 Pro, M5 Max, and M5 Ultra

M5 (October 2025)

The M5 is the base chip in the M5 family and is built using TSMC’s third-generation 3-nanometer process for mainstream laptops and tablets. It debuted in the 14-inch MacBook Pro and is the first Apple silicon chip to feature a dedicated Neural Accelerator in each GPU core, focusing on AI-driven tasks.

The chip features a 10-core CPU made up of 4 performance and 6 efficiency cores and up to a 10-core GPU, which provides solid graphics performance for tasks like photo editing and light 3D work. You can also configure it with up to 32GB of unified memory.

At launch, the M5 base model outperformed the whole M4 series in Geekbench Single-Core scores and had the highest single-core score of any Apple silicon chip. Early benchmarks even showed it nearly matching the M1 Ultra. Overall, it delivers a strong balance of performance, efficiency, and affordability for most users, and our M5 vs M4 MacBook Air comparison breaks down the real-world difference.

M5 Pro (March 2026)

The M5 Pro is designed for professionals who need more processing power than the base M5. Apple designed a new Fusion Architecture (a dual-die design) for this chip. It includes an 18-core CPU (6 super and 12 performance cores), offering up to 30% faster processing of intensive workloads. Apple describes it as having “the world’s fastest CPU core.”

The GPU scales up to 20 cores with a dedicated Neural Accelerator in each core, delivering much stronger graphics performance. One of the major improvements in the M5 Pro is higher memory bandwidth of up to 307 GB/s and up to 64GB of unified memory, enabling large projects and datasets to run smoothly without slowdowns.

M5 Max (March 2026)

The M5 Max sits at the top of the M5 laptop lineup and is built for users who need maximum performance. It is targeted at professionals working in fields such as 3D rendering, medical imaging, advanced video production, machine learning, and large-scale creative projects.

This chip features the same high-performance CPU architecture as the M5 Pro but dramatically expands the GPU capabilities. The GPU can scale up to 40 cores, making it one of the most powerful graphics systems available in a laptop.

The M5 Max also offers up to 614GBps memory bandwidth (460GBps on the 32-core GPU version) and supports up to 128GB of unified memory. So, it can run large professional projects efficiently without relying heavily on external storage. For full configurations and pricing, see our guide to the MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and M5 Max.

M5 Ultra (August 2026)

Apple’s M5 Ultra, introduced in August 2026, is designed specifically for demanding professional workflows and advanced AI workloads. The biggest change is Apple’s move to a quad-die architecture using next-generation UltraFusion technology, giving M5 Ultra the scale needed for extreme CPU, GPU and AI workloads.

You can configure it with up to a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU. For AI, Apple has added Neural Accelerators to the GPU for the first time on an Ultra chip, delivering up to 4.3x the peak AI compute performance of M3 Ultra. The chip also supports up to 512GB of unified memory and an enormous 1.2TB/s of memory bandwidth.

Apple says M5 Ultra delivers up to 1.3x faster multithreaded CPU performance and up to 40 percent faster graphics performance than M3 Ultra. These improvements target workloads such as 3D rendering, video production, software development, scientific computing and AI inference. Not sure if you need that much power? Our M6 Mac mini vs M5 Ultra Mac Studio comparison can help.

M4 Chip family: M4, M4 Pro, and M4 Max

Apple’s M4 chip family brought major advancements in silicon technology, delivering enhanced performance and efficiency across various devices. Each chip (M4, M4 Pro, and M4 Max) is designed to meet different user needs.

M4 (May 2024)

The standard M4 chip is built using second-generation 3-nanometer technology, enhancing power efficiency and performance. It features a 10-core CPU with four performance cores and six efficiency cores, delivering up to 1.8 times faster performance than the M1 chip.

The 10-core GPU provides graphics performance up to twice as fast as the M1, making tasks like photo editing and gaming smoother. The 16-core Neural Engine, capable of performing up to 38 trillion operations per second, significantly boosts AI-related tasks and features like Apple Intelligence.

M4 Pro (October 2024)

The M4 Pro chip is designed for users with more demanding workflows. It boasts a 14-core CPU, comprising ten performance cores and four efficiency cores, offering up to 1.9 times faster performance than the M1 Pro.

The GPU includes up to 20 cores, providing graphics performance twice that of the standard M4. This makes it ideal for professionals engaged in tasks like app development, video editing, and complex simulations.

M4 Max (October 2024)

The M4 Max chip is the most powerful in the M4 family, targeting users requiring extreme performance. It features up to a 16-core CPU with 12 performance cores and four efficiency cores.

Its GPU scales up to 40 cores, delivering exceptional graphics capabilities suitable for high-end tasks such as 3D rendering and large-scale data processing. The M4 Max also supports higher unified memory bandwidth, enhancing data-intensive operations.

All M4 chips support advanced features like hardware-accelerated ray tracing and mesh shading, enhancing graphics rendering and gaming experiences. The M4 Pro and M4 Max also enable Thunderbolt 5 connectivity, offering faster data transfer speeds and improved peripheral support.

M3 Chip Family: M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, and M3 Ultra

Apple’s M3 chipset family includes four powerful processors: M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, and M3 Ultra. Each is designed to meet different performance needs, from everyday tasks to demanding professional workloads.

M3 (October 2023)

The M3 chip is built using advanced 3-nanometer technology, making it faster and more efficient. It features an 8-core CPU with four performance cores and four efficiency cores, delivering up to 30% faster performance than the M1.

The up-to-10-core GPU provides enhanced graphics performance, making tasks like photo editing and gaming smoother. The 16-core Neural Engine, capable of performing up to 18 trillion operations per second, significantly boosts AI-related tasks.

M3 Pro (October 2023)

The M3 Pro chip is designed for users with more demanding workflows. It boasts a 12-core CPU, comprising six performance cores and six efficiency cores, offering up to 40% faster performance than the M1 Pro.

The GPU features up to 18 cores, delivering graphics performance ideal for professionals in video editing, programming, and other demanding tasks. Apple has also integrated 37 billion transistors to enhance the overall performance of Mac machines.

M3 Max (October 2023)

The M3 Max chip is the most powerful laptop chip in the M3 family, targeting users requiring extreme performance. It features up to a 16-core CPU with 12 performance cores and four efficiency cores.

Its GPU scales up to 40 cores, delivering exceptional graphics capabilities suitable for high-end tasks such as 3D rendering and large-scale data processing. The M3 Max also has 92 billion transistors to enhance data-intensive operations.

M3 Ultra (March 2025)

The M3 Ultra chip was Apple’s most powerful processor at launch. It features a 32-core CPU with 24 performance cores and eight efficiency cores, delivering up to 1.8 times the performance of the M1 Ultra.

Its GPU includes up to 80 cores, providing up to 2.6 times faster graphics performance than the M1 Ultra. The M3 Ultra also supports up to 512GB of unified memory, the highest ever in a personal computer at the time, making it ideal for tasks like visual effects and AI development.

M2 Chip Family: M2, M2 Pro, M2 Max, and M2 Ultra

M2 (June 2022)

The M2 processor in the MacBook houses an 8-core CPU with a configuration of 4 performance cores and 4 efficiency cores. Apple claims that M2’s CPU delivers nearly twice the performance of the latest 10-core PC laptop processor at the same power level.

In addition, the M2 processor offers excellent work performance with an 8- or 10-core GPU, 16-core Neural Engine, and 100GBps bandwidth. M2 chips come in different RAM variations: 8GB, 16GB, and 24GB.

M2 Pro (January 2023) 

M2 Pro has a robust 10-core or 12-core CPU, including 6 or 8 performance and 4 efficiency cores. Like the M1 Pro, the M2 Pro has a built-in media engine that accelerates H.264, HEVC, and ProRes video encoding and decoding. Besides, the chip provides improved power efficiency when playing 4K and 8K ProRes streams thanks to the 16- or 19-core GPU.

Further, the M2 Pro has a 16-core Neural Engine, 200GBps memory bandwidth, and 16GB or 32GB RAM variants. Apple claimed the M2 Pro offered exceptional image processing capabilities. It was available in the MacBook Pro and Mac mini.

M2 Max (January 2023) 

M2 Max added another layer of efficiency to the Apple silicon range. Its core specifications included a 12-core CPU with 8 performance and 4 efficiency cores. Like its predecessor, the M2 Max comes with two ProRes and video-encoding engines.

Regarding graphics, it supports a 30- or 38-core GPU to give you the most detailed output. While the GPU support is better than M1 Max, the 16-core Neural Engine remains the same for both variants. In addition, Apple introduced the chip in three RAM variants: 32GB, 64GB, and 96GB.

Moreover, Apple asserted that the M2 Max was 30% faster than the M1 version when color grading in DaVinci Resolve. It also offers 400GB/s of memory bandwidth, ensuring quick processing.

M2 Ultra (June 2023) 

At WWDC 2023, Apple launched its most efficient iteration of the Apple silicon series at the time: M2 Ultra. It offers the power of two M2 Max chips connected using the robust UltraFusion architecture. Regarding specifications, M2 Ultra features a 24-core CPU and up to a 76-core GPU.

It also carries 134 billion transistors, up to 192GB of unified memory, and an impressive 800GB/s of memory bandwidth. It powered the 2023 Mac Studio and Mac Pro (here’s how the M2 Ultra Mac Studio compares with the Mac Pro); Apple discontinued the Mac Pro in March 2026. According to Apple, Mac Studio with M2 Ultra is up to 3x faster than its earlier version.

Besides, it can play 22 streams of 8K ProRes video together. The M2 Ultra chip enables the Mac Pro to deliver 3D simulations and video transcoding up to 3x faster. Moreover, the processor can simultaneously handle 24 streams of 4K camera input and encode them to ProRes.

M1 Chip family: M1, M1 Pro, M1 Max, and M1 Ultra

M1 (November 2020)

The M1 processor was Apple’s first venture into chip design for the Mac. Indeed, it was a big blow for Intel! Regarding specs, M1 chips offer an 8-core CPU with 4 performance and 4 efficiency cores and a 7- or 8-core GPU.

Besides, the 16-core Neural Engine embedded in the M1 accelerates and optimizes machine learning operations on Mac. In addition, the chip offered 68.25GB/s of memory bandwidth. However, it only supported two RAM variations: 8GB and 16GB. The limited memory options didn’t go down well with many Mac users.

M1 Pro (October 2021)

Next in line in the M1 series was M1 Pro. This chipset supported 8- or 10-core CPUs, configured as 6 or 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores. Besides, Apple included a 14- or 16-core GPU, which is 2x faster than M1. Also, the new GPU was up to 7x faster than the integrated graphics on the latest 8-core PC laptop chip.

Besides, it featured a ProRes accelerator in the media engine for faster video processing. Its memory bandwidth of up to 200GB/s is nearly 3x better than the M1. This time, Apple expanded the memory options, offering 16GB and 32GB configurations.

M1 Max (October 2021)

The M1 Max and M1 Pro chips were launched together. The M1 Max had a 10-core CPU with 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores, a 24- or 32-core GPU, and a 16-core Neural Engine. The graphics performance of the 32-core GPU is up to 4x faster than that of the M1 chip.

Its two ProRes accelerators can deliver up to 2x faster video encoding than M1 Pro. Moreover, the processor offers up to 400GB/s of memory bandwidth, two times more than the M1 Pro and 6x more than the M1. Besides, the 64GB RAM option adds some extra credit points.

Apple introduced the M1 Max chip only for the MacBook Pro and Mac Studio.

M1 Ultra (March 2022)

The M1 Ultra was launched as an option for the Mac Studio. This powerful processor uses UltraFusion architecture to connect two M1 Max chips. It houses a 20-core CPU with 16 performance and 4 efficiency cores. For graphics, Apple added a massive 48- or 64-core GPU.

So, you get low latency, massive bandwidth, and better power efficiency. Furthermore, the chip has up to 128GB of unified memory built in, offering twice the media engine performance of the M1 Max.

2006-2020: Intel x86

At WWDC 2005, Apple announced its transition to Intel chips, and the first Intel Macs were announced in January 2006. These included an iMac and the MacBook Pro, which boasted up to four-fold enhanced performance over their predecessors.

Further, from Mac OS X 10.4.4, Apple included an advanced translation technology called Rosetta. It helped maintain software compatibility between generations. Soon, Apple introduced programs with universal binaries that could run on both PowerPC and Intel Macs.

As the transition to x86 came full circle, Rosetta was removed from Mac OS X 10.7 Lion going forward. So far, about 80 Mac models have featured Intel CPUs. This changed with the introduction of ARM-based Macs. Apple has confirmed that macOS Tahoe 26 is the last macOS release to support Intel Macs, so macOS 27 Golden Gate runs only on Apple silicon Macs. Apple now also lets Mac App Store apps drop Intel support.

1994-2005: Power PC

In the late 1980s, new trends began taking over the computing industry, overshadowing the legacy CPU architectures. Apple partnered with IBM and Motorola to design a common CPU platform that could rival the “Wintel” (Microsoft-Intel) domination. 

The Power Macintosh 6100 used the PowerPC architecture, following which around 87 different Mac models were launched. Clock speeds increased from 60 MHz to 2.7 GHz, which was remarkable for that era. The final Apple PowerPC model was released in November 2005. 

1984-1995: Motorola 68 K 

The 1984 Apple Macintosh computer had an 8 MHz Motorola 68000 CPU. While in development, an early Mac prototype used an 8/16-bit Motorola 6809 CPU. But after a designer noticed the impressive graphics routines that were being created for the 68000-based Apple Lisa, the more expensive 16/32-bit 68000 was chosen. 

While the Apple Lisa used only a 5 MHz 68000, the new Mac prototype could run at 8 MHz. This appealed to Steve Jobs, who was eager to upstage the Lisa team. 

Over the following decade, every Macintosh used the 68000 or its successors, including the pure 32-bit 68020, 68030, and 68040 chips. These got faster and more complex over time. Overall, at least 72 different Macs used 68K CPUs, the last of which was the PowerBook 190 in 1995.

The best is yet to come! 

The history of Apple processors beautifully captures the tech giant’s true ideology. The Mac has witnessed changes in everything from laptop size to its architecture. And with Apple’s “Pro and Tell” event on October 28, the next chapter may already be here. I hope you enjoyed reading this article as much as we enjoyed traveling the Mac timeline while penning it.

Please share your reviews in the comments section. Till then, enjoy reading.

FAQs

What is the oldest Mac software?

The oldest Mac operating system is System 1, which shipped with the original Macintosh in 1984.

What is the full form of Mac?

The full form of Mac is Macintosh.

title.rendered: Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook Pro is here: Specs, features, and price

content.rendered:
Apple has finally done what Mac users have been waiting years for: the MacBook Pro now has a touchscreen. Announced at the “Pro and Tell” special event on October 28, the all-new MacBook Pro introduces a tandem OLED display, a Dynamic Island, a glowing Apple logo, and a thinner, lighter design. It also brings touch-based controls to macOS for the first time.

But there’s a catch. The redesigned 14-inch MacBook Pro starts at $2,899, while the 16-inch model starts at $3,399. So Apple is clearly positioning these laptops as premium machines for professionals. Pre-orders opened on October 28, 2026, and the first units arrive on Friday, November 6.

Meet the new touchscreen MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display

The biggest upgrade is Apple’s new PROLED XDR display, which replaces the previous MacBook Pro’s mini-LED technology with a tandem OLED panel.

Apple says the display combines advanced tandem OLED technology, sophisticated display-engine algorithms, and factory calibration to deliver “exceptional brightness, striking contrast, and vivid true-to-life colors.”

Here are the key display specifications:

  • Tandem OLED technology: Delivers deep blacks, rich colors, and exceptional contrast.
  • Up to 2,000 nits of peak HDR and SDR brightness: Helps keep content visible in demanding lighting conditions.
  • 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio: Improves the distinction between bright highlights and dark shadows.
  • 10Hz to 120Hz variable refresh rate: Makes scrolling, animations, and supported creative workflows feel smoother.
  • P3 and Adobe RGB color spaces: Supports color-critical work across photography, HDR video, and print design.
  • Optional nano-texture glass: Reduces reflections and glare, with the nano-texture precisely etched into the cover glass.

These features back Apple’s claim that the new MacBook Pro has the “world’s best display in a pro laptop.”

The first touchscreen Mac changes how you use macOS

For years, Apple has kept touch input on the iPhone and iPad while relying on a keyboard, trackpad, and mouse for the Mac. That changes with the new MacBook Pro.

Apple has integrated the touch sensor directly into the display panel, which the company says helps reduce latency. macOS 27 automatically translates touches into clicks, so existing apps work without needing to be updated first.

Here are some of the new touch interactions:

  • Swipe naturally through webpages and other content.
  • Pinch to zoom into photos and images.
  • Drag and drop slides between presentations.
  • Double-tap a window to fill the screen.
  • Flick a window into position to tile it.
  • Draw and manipulate designs directly on the display.

Apple has also redesigned the laptop’s hinge to support touchscreen use, helping keep the display stable when users tap and swipe.

Dynamic Island replaces the notch

Another major design change is the removal of the familiar MacBook Pro notch.

Apple has introduced a smaller Dynamic Island that brings an iPhone-inspired interface to the Mac. It serves as a central place to access Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI. Users can search their Mac, ask questions, check ongoing activities, and control music from this interactive area.

The change also gives the redesigned laptop a more modern appearance, with the Dynamic Island taking up less space than the previous notch.

A thinner, lighter design with a glowing Apple logo

Apple has redesigned the MacBook Pro’s chassis to make it more portable without compromising its professional capabilities. Apple says the 16-inch model is nearly 1mm thinner than the existing design, and the 14-inch model is about half a millimeter thinner.

The new 14-inch model weighs just 3 pounds, while the 16-inch version weighs 4 pounds. Apple says those figures represent reductions of half a pound and 0.7 pounds, respectively, compared with their predecessors.

The redesigned laptop also brings back the glowing Apple logo, a feature that many MacBook fans will remember from older models.

Apple has updated the audio system, too. The laptop features six speakers, an all-new woofer design, and updated tweeters. The company says the system delivers 50% deeper bass and clearer sound.

M5 Pro and M5 Max power the new MacBook Pro

Despite the extensive redesign, Apple hasn’t introduced a new processor generation for these models. The new MacBook Pro uses the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, which Apple describes as its most powerful chips built for a professional laptop. Apple’s newer M6 chip is instead going into the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 and the iMac with M6 chip, neither of which has a touchscreen.

The available configurations support:

  • Up to 128GB of unified memory (M5 Max; up to 64GB with M5 Pro).
  • Up to 16TB of storage (M5 Max).
  • Hardware and software capabilities designed for demanding professional and AI workloads.

The combination of Apple silicon, unified memory, and macOS 27 is designed to handle complex projects, including video editing, graphics work, development, and machine-learning tasks.

Connectivity, camera, audio, and battery life

The redesigned MacBook Pro includes a broad range of hardware features for professionals who need to connect accessories and work away from a desk.

Here’s what else Apple has confirmed:

  • Battery life: Up to 24 hours on the 16-inch M5 Pro model (up to 22 hours on the 14-inch M5 Pro model), according to Apple.
  • Camera: A 12MP Center Stage camera.
  • Microphones: Studio-quality microphones.
  • Ports: Three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe charging, and a headphone jack.
  • Wireless connectivity: Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, powered by Apple’s N1 wireless chip.
  • Security: Touch ID for convenient and secure authentication.
  • External displays: Up to three with M5 Pro and up to four with M5 Max.

This feature set is particularly useful for photographers, video editors, and other professionals who regularly connect external storage, cameras, and displays.

MacBook Pro price and availability

The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, with M5 Pro and M5 Max configurations. Buyers can choose Silver or Space Black finishes, with standard or nano-texture display configurations.

Here’s the full US starting-price breakdown:

Apple also lists education pricing of $2,749 for the 14-inch M5 Pro model, $3,199 for the 16-inch M5 Pro model, $4,199 for the 14-inch M5 Max model, and $4,499 for the 16-inch M5 Max model. Opting for nano-texture glass adds $150 in the US.

Pre-orders opened on October 28, 2026, and the new MacBook Pro is scheduled to begin arriving to customers, and in Apple Store locations and authorized resellers, on Friday, November 6.

title.rendered: 10 best ChatGPT alternatives in 2026 (free and paid)

content.rendered:
ChatGPT is great, and it now gives even free users unlimited text chats. Still, some jobs are much better done with another AI model. We’ve been testing AI tools constantly for the last four years, and this list collects the alternatives worth trying.

The list is ordered by use case, not by overall performance, so you can pick the one that fits what you actually do. Most have a free tier, so you can try the part that matters to you before paying for another subscription.

ChatGPT alternatives compared: free tiers and prices

Prices below are standard US monthly web prices at the time of writing. We’ll keep this article updated, but some details can change quickly in this space.

1. Claude: My pick for writing and coding

Claude is the first alternative I’d try if ChatGPT keeps sanding your writing into the same smooth, generic voice. Claude is also currently a bit better at coding than ChatGPT’s Codex, if you’re into that. But the main reason to use Claude is that it has a better sense of what you’re asking and makes slightly fewer hallucination mistakes.

You also lose very little in the switch, because Claude has a good range of connectors and features like artifacts. However, it can’t generate images, and top-tier models like Fable are only included on Max plans; Pro users have to pay for them through usage credits. So if you want to stick to a $20 Pro plan, ChatGPT may still have an edge here.

Pro costs $20 a month or $200 billed annually. It raises your allowance, but paid access still has caps, and long chats or large attachments use up more of it. Upgrade when the free limits start interrupting your work, rather than expecting Pro to mean unlimited.

If you’re still deciding between the two, our ChatGPT vs. Claude comparison breaks down how they differ in writing, coding, and everyday use, so you can decide which one fits your workflow better. If you’re new to Claude, our guide to Claude’s icons and symbols explains what its buttons and controls do.

Try Claude

2. Meta AI / Muse: Help where you’re already chatting

Meta AI’s appeal is convenience. If you spend your day in WhatsApp or Instagram, asking for a gift idea there is easier than opening another app. Everyday use remains free, while Meta One Core starts at $7.99 a month for more AI creation and app perks.

Muse is Meta’s separate personal agent. It can work across connected services and take actions, with approval for sensitive steps such as sending an email. It has a limited free allowance and separate subscriptions starting with Power at $20 a month. So if you use ChatGPT’s dots, Muse gives you an alternative agent.

However, the major limitation with Meta is the model itself. While it’s impressive and has improved a lot, it’s a smaller model at the end of the day compared to models like OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra.

Muse is worth considering if you want help carrying out personal tasks, but it’s only available in the US and Canada for now. Give it one small task you can check before connecting more services. A chatbot suggesting a reply and an agent sending one need different levels of trust.

Try Meta AI or try Muse.

3. Microsoft Copilot: An easy start for Windows users

Copilot is an easy place to start if you already use Microsoft’s apps. Its free chat handles everyday jobs such as rewriting an awkward email or explaining a spreadsheet formula. Web and mobile apps mean you don’t need a Windows PC, though Windows and Microsoft 365 users have the clearest reason to pick it.

Working inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Outlook is where a subscription becomes useful. Microsoft 365 Personal costs $9.99 a month and includes Copilot in those apps. Premium costs $19.99 and adds more usage and exclusive features. Check what you already pay for before upgrading.

The catch is that free Copilot chat doesn’t include the same access inside Microsoft 365. If you only need a few answers and email rewrites, paying for the Office integration may buy you very little.

Try Microsoft Copilot

4. DeepSeek: A free second opinion on a hard problem

DeepSeek is worth trying for a math problem or a spreadsheet formula that keeps returning the wrong number. Students and anyone looking for another approach to a problem can use its reasoning and web search without buying a subscription. The consumer app and web chat are free; developer API billing is separate.

The trade-off is data handling. DeepSeek processes and stores personal data in China, and its policy allows data use to improve its models. Use a made-up spreadsheet example instead of your employer’s file. You can fix the formula without sharing the real figures. We’ve already covered DeepSeek vs. ChatGPT on iPhone, so you can check that comparison in detail.

Try DeepSeek

5. Duck.ai: Quick questions without an account

Duck.ai is the one I’d suggest to someone whose first question is, “Do I have to sign up?” You can choose a model and chat for free without an account. DuckDuckGo removes identifying metadata before forwarding requests, and its provider agreements prohibit using those chats for model training. That makes it a useful option for occasional questions you don’t want attached to a chatbot account.

The free version has a daily cap, so long work sessions can hit a wall. In supported countries, DuckDuckGo Plus costs $9.99 a month and Pro costs $19.99, bundling more AI access with other privacy services. I’d pay for the bundle only if you’ll also use its VPN or other included services.

Your prompts still go to a model provider. Recent chats stay on your device by default, with optional encrypted Sync & Backup for other devices.

Try Duck.ai

6. Mistral Vibe: The assistant formerly called Le Chat

If you remember Le Chat, this is the same service under its newer Vibe name. Mistral has added work and coding modes, but the conversational Chat mode remains. It’s a useful general assistant to try if you’d prefer France-based Mistral over another major US platform.

The free plan includes limited messages, web search, document uploads, and basic image generation and editing. Start with an ordinary document task, such as pulling deadlines out of a club newsletter, before connecting your apps.

Pro costs $14.99 a month, excluding taxes, and gives you more room to work. It undercuts Claude and Perplexity, but a lower price only matters if you like the answers. Messages, searches, and uploads still have plan limits, with fair-use restrictions on paid access too.

Try Mistral Vibe

7. Perplexity: Research you can follow back to a source

Perplexity searches the web and puts citations alongside its answers. Use it to compare subscription plans or find the origin of a statistic, then open the relevant source. Students, researchers, and anyone gathering facts before a decision get somewhere to check the answer.

Core search and chat are free, with limits on advanced features. Pro costs $20 a month or $200 billed annually and makes sense when deeper research and file work become regular needs.

A citation can still fail to support the exact claim beside it. Check the source behind the detail that changes your decision, such as a product’s compatibility requirement. Perplexity saves you the hunt for pages; you still need to read the relevant bit.

Try Perplexity

8. Gemini: The practical pick for Google users

Gemini makes more sense if your email and documents already live in Google. Summarizing a thread inside Gmail saves copying it into another chatbot. The paid plans bundle storage too, so check whether an AI plan could replace your existing storage subscription.

The free version offers everyday chat, Gemini Live, image tools, and limited research features, with Flash-Lite listed on the current US plan. Google AI Plus costs $4.99 a month, while AI Pro costs $19.99 and includes stronger models, higher limits, and Gemini in Docs and other apps.

Choose carefully if you’re paying for a particular model. Following Google’s October changes to Gemini access, free and entry-level plans have a narrower selection. AI Plus won’t give you everything in Pro. The higher tier earns its price when you’ll use both the stronger models and the app integration.

Try Gemini

9. Grok: Useful when the conversation is happening on X

Grok can search both the web and posts on X. That helps when you want reactions to a product launch or the original post behind a claim being passed around. If you regularly follow discussions and breaking developments on X, that connection matters more than its chatbot personality.

Free access includes limited chat. For new customers, X Subscription Plus costs $8 a month and Premium costs $30, with paid plans bundling Grok, X, and Cursor access. Existing SuperGrok plans can continue, so check your subscriptions before adding another one.

Finding a claim on X doesn’t establish that it’s true. Ask for the original post and separate it from what other accounts are repeating. A busy discussion can tell you what people think without proving what happened.

Try Grok

10. Kagi Assistant: Worth a look if you’re paying for search

Kagi combines a paid, ad-free search engine with an AI assistant. It’s most appealing if you want both in one subscription, since you’re deciding whether to replace your search engine as well as where to ask AI questions.

There’s a free trial with 100 searches and 100 Assistant interactions. After that, Starter costs $5 a month for 300 searches and Quick-mode Assistant access. Professional costs $10, removes the search cap, and increases the Assistant allowance.

The catch is that Research mode and flagship model selection require the $25 Ultimate plan, still subject to fair use. Spend the trial on questions you normally search for. If those results don’t earn your money, the bundled assistant is a weak reason to keep paying.

Try Kagi Assistant

Honorable mentions: Brave Leo and Poe

These two make more sense for a particular habit than as the first replacement for everyone.

Brave Leo

Leo works inside the Brave browser and can summarize the page or PDF you’re reading. There’s a free version, and Leo Premium costs $14.99 a month. Try it if you already use Brave and keep copying text into another chatbot. Its browser focus is also a reason to skip it if you’re happy elsewhere.

Try Brave Leo

Poe

Poe puts multiple AI models in one app, with free access and paid plans that add points and model options. It suits people who want to compare models without maintaining several separate subscriptions. Each bot has its own point cost, though, so check how much your preferred model uses before subscribing.

Try Poe

Which ChatGPT alternative should you choose?

I’d start with Claude if writing and editing take up most of your AI use, or Perplexity if you spend more time finding facts and checking sources. If your main frustration is copying work between apps, Gemini or Copilot may be the more useful switch, depending on whether you use Google or Microsoft tools.

For occasional questions, try a free option before adding another subscription. Duck.ai is an easy starting point if you don’t want an account, while DeepSeek is worth trying for non-sensitive problems you want help working through.

Pick the two that fit your routine and give them the same real task. Keep the one that needs less correcting, and pay only when its free limits regularly get in your way.
