title.rendered: Best Halloween apps for iPhone and iPad: Get spooky the smart way

content.rendered:
Halloween season is creeping closer, and it’s officially time to turn your iPhone into a haunted playground. While most of us are busy decking out our homes with pumpkins and cobwebs, there’s another way to get in the Halloween spirit, through your phone!

This year, I’ve been testing out the best Halloween apps for iPhone and trust me, they’re the perfect mix of spooky, creative, and fun. Whether you want to decorate your phone with eerie wallpapers, play Halloween games with your kids, or discover haunted attractions near you, there’s an app for every kind of ghoul and ghost.

So, if you’re ready to level up your Halloween celebrations (digitally and IRL), keep scrolling, because this list will get you in the spooky spirit in no time.

Why you’ll love these Halloween apps

Before we jump into the list, let’s look at why downloading Halloween-themed apps this year is totally worth it.

Decor and Customization

  • Themes: Give your iPhone a Halloween makeover with spooky wallpapers, lock screen backgrounds, and icons that reflect your love for spooky season.
  • Decorations: You don’t need real cobwebs or pumpkins to set the mood. Several Halloween apps let you virtually decorate, from glowing jack-o’-lanterns to ghostly animations.

Entertainment

  • No Halloween is complete without creepy stories and chilling soundtracks. Many Halloween apps curate paranormal tales, haunted radio stations, and ghostly soundscapes to keep your evenings spine-tingling.

Costumes and Makeup

  • Half the fun of Halloween lies in dressing up! You’ll find plenty of apps that inspire costume ideas, guide you through Halloween makeup looks, or even apply digital face paint for your next selfie.

Trick-or-Treating

  • Maps: Some Halloween apps now help you plan the perfect trick-or-treat route, showing candy-friendly neighborhoods and spooky hotspots.
  • Planning: You can even strategize your trick-or-treat rounds with interactive maps, great for parents who want to keep things fun yet safe.

Social Sharing

  • Halloween Filters: Keep your Instagram and TikTok feeds festive with apps that offer ghostly filters, themed frames, and creative editing tools.
  • Sharing: Even if your loved ones are far away, many Halloween apps make it easy to share your creations and spooky selfies with a single tap.

Educational Fun

  • Learn About Halloween: For the curious little ones, some apps teach the history and traditions behind Halloween through interactive stories and mini-games.
  • Educational Gameplay: You’ll also find Halloween learning apps that make math, art, and logic fun for toddlers and young kids.

How we picked the best Halloween apps?

If you’re anything like the typical iGeeksBlog reader, you expect more than just a few cute stickers. You want functionality, creativity, and value – all rolled into one. That’s exactly how this list was curated.

  • Focus on the iGeeks Audience: These apps are handpicked for Apple enthusiasts who love smooth interfaces, great design, and unique experiences.
  • Spooky Aesthetic: Each app adds a Halloween vibe to your iPhone or iPad, from fonts and wallpapers to widgets and ringtones.
  • Variety: From kids’ games to social filters to haunted event maps, there’s something for everyone.
  • Quality Over Quantity: Every app here was chosen based on reviews, reliability, and real functionality, not just download counts.
  • Value for Money: Whether free or paid, each app offers something genuinely worth your time (and your coins).

Best Halloween photo and makeup apps

Give your Halloween selfies a spooky makeover or experiment with costume makeup before the big night. They can come in handy when you wish to be more experimental and make your seasonal photos stand out. 

1. Spooky Photo Video Maker Vody 

If your Halloween selfies look a little too ordinary, Spooky Photo Video Maker Vody offers a way to give them a horror-inspired makeover. The app gives your pictures and videos an eerie twist, featuring horror themes like ghosts, zombies, vampires, witches, or even werewolves.

It’s a fun option for anyone who wants to create something creepy for Instagram, TikTok, or a Halloween group chat without learning complicated editing software.

Pros

  • Offers a variety of horror-inspired transformations. 
  • Useful for creating Halloween photos and videos for social media. 
  • Free to download, with additional paid options. 

Cons

  • Generated effects may not always look exactly as expected. 
  • Some video credits and subscriptions cost extra. 

Price: Free (In-app purchases start from $1.99) 

Download 

2. Halloween Makeup Editor 

Selecting the right Halloween costume is not enough; it’s the makeup that transforms an ordinary dress into something really interesting. Halloween Makeup Editor is worth exploring if you want to experiment with different spooky looks before applying real face paint.

I tried imagining myself as a vampire, a witch, and a frightening horror character before deciding which costume suits me best. It’s particularly useful if you’re short on inspiration or want to compare ideas with friends.

Pros

  • Helps you explore Halloween makeup ideas before committing to a look. 
  • Useful for planning individual or group costumes. 

Cons

  • Digital effects may not perfectly resemble real makeup. 
  • Results depend on photo quality and available editing options. 
  • The selection may feel limited if you want advanced photo-editing tools. 

Price: Free  

Download 

Best Halloween music and sound apps 

Set the mood with creepy sound effects and horror-inspired beats. Whether you’re hosting a party or creating a haunted atmosphere at home, these apps add an extra layer of Halloween fun. 

3. Spooky Beats Maker: Horror Mix

Want your Halloween party to sound as spooky as it looks? Spooky Beats Maker: Horror Mix is a music-making game which allows you to play around with beats, sounds, and animated characters, creating your own songs.

I suggest using it as a fun activity before a party, challenging friends to create the creepiest beat, or simply enjoying mixing sounds while getting into the Halloween mood.

Pros

  • Interactive music-making experience with spooky themes. 
  • Lets you experiment with different sound combinations. 
  • The simple interface is teen-friendly. 

Cons

  • May not offer the control of professional music-production software. 
  • Ads or paid features can interrupt the experience. 
  • The game-like format may not suit users looking for ready-made background music. 

Price: Free (Remove ads for $1.99) 

Download 

4. Spooky Halloween Sounds 

Sometimes, the right sound can do more for a Halloween atmosphere than an elaborate decoration. Spooky Halloween Sounds is an option for anyone who wants creepy audio to accompany a haunted-house setup, storytelling session, or Halloween party.

I would try the following combination at a Halloween party: lowering the lights, setting some artificial webs in the room and playing eerie sounds in the background while telling ghost stories.

Pros

  • Convenient for adding atmosphere to Halloween gatherings. 
  • Instant scares and long ambient music mixes. 
  • Includes mini games for fun. 

Cons

  • Repeated sound effects may become predictable. 
  • A separate speaker may be useful for larger gatherings. 

Price: Free 

Download 

Best Halloween games and scary entertainment apps

From relaxing coloring activities to intense horror games and paranormal-themed experiences, here are plenty of scary entertainment apps for all kinds of players. 

5. Halloween Color by Number Game 

Not everyone wants jump scares and terrifying monsters on Halloween. Sometimes, a relaxing activity is exactly what you need between decorating the house and preparing treats.

Halloween Color by Number Game offers a gentler way to enjoy the season through themed coloring, especially for your kids. The gameplay is simple: follow the color guide and gradually complete Halloween-themed illustrations.

Pros

  • Relaxing alternative to action and horror games. 
  • Easy-to-follow coloring format. 
  • Alternative seasonal themes for refreshment. 

Cons

  • Gameplay may feel repetitive for players who prefer action. 
  • Some pictures or features may require payment. 
  • Small coloring areas can be less comfortable on smaller screens. 

Price: Free (In-app purchases start from $1.99) 

Download 

6. The Ghost – Multiplayer Horror 

Watching a horror movie with friends is fun, but trying to survive a frightening game together can make Halloween night even more memorable. You may give The Ghost – Multiplayer Horror a shot if you like dark environments, exploratory gameplay, and unpredictable multiplayer action.

I liked its suspicious sound and unexpected, intense encounters, perfect for a Halloween gaming session with friends who enjoy horror and cooperative challenges.

Pros

  • Combines horror-themed gameplay with multiplayer entertainment. 
  • Offers a shared experience for up to five friends. 
  • Different playing modes for new experiences. 

Cons

  • Horror themes may be too intense for younger players. 
  • Multiplayer sessions depend on compatible devices and connectivity. 
  • Players who prefer relaxed games may find the atmosphere stressful. 

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $0.99) 

Download 

7. Horror Stories & Scary Stories 

Not everyone wants to spend Halloween playing action games. Sometimes, a creepy story shared with friends is enough to create the right atmosphere. Horror Stories & Scary Stories comes with an interactive survival game through frightening chats and stories.  

Your choice shapes the story. I prefer it when I want to enjoy horror at my own pace rather than dealing with sudden visual jump scares.

Pros

  • Offers a reading-based alternative to horror games. 
  • Suitable for solo reading or sharing stories with friends. 
  • Multiple endings to the same story with darker consequences. 

Cons

  • Story quality and variety may vary. 
  • Some content may be too disturbing for younger readers. 
  • Advertisements or paid content may affect the reading experience. 

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $0.99) 

Download 

8. Spirit Board: Very Scary 

Looking for a spooky activity to make Halloween night more mysterious? Spirit Board brings the traditional Ouija board concept to your iPhone or iPad. It’s perfect for creating an interactive experience for paranormal-themed entertainment.  

The app lets you ask questions using your voice or text and displays responses through a moving planchette. However, treat it as entertainment rather than evidence of actual communication with spirits. 

Pros

  • Fits a paranormal-themed Halloween gathering. 
  • Offers an alternative to conventional horror games. 
  • Works as a conversation starter 

Cons

  • The experience may rely more on atmosphere than substantial gameplay. 
  • Supernatural themes may make some users uncomfortable. 

Price: Free (Unlock Pro features and remove ads for $2.99) 

Download 

Best apps for Halloween party planning and creativity 

Make your Halloween gathering easier to organize with creative invitations and seasonal activities. These apps can help you prepare for the party and give your guests a taste of the theme before they arrive. 

9. Invitation Maker – Cards & RSVP 

Planning a Halloween party is exciting until you have to message everyone individually, explain the theme, and work out who’s actually coming. Invitation Maker – Cards & RSVP can help with the invitation-design side of the process. 

Rather than sending a plain text message, it helps me create a more polished invitation that communicates the party’s mood before guests even arrive.

Pros

  • Helps create visually appealing party invitations. 
  • Useful for coordinating a Halloween event’s theme. 
  • Can reduce the effort involved in preparing invitations and organizing attendance. 

Cons

  • Some designs and customization options may cost extra. 
  • RSVP capabilities may differ from those of a full event-management service. 
  • Guest questions and last-minute changes still need to be managed. 

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $1.99) 

Download 

10. Halloween All-in-One 

If you enjoy Halloween but don’t want to download a separate app for every little seasonal activity, Halloween All-in-One is worth investigating. You get Halloween-focused wallpaper, sound effects, music, countdown, and spooky stories, making it an interesting option for people who prefer seasonal entertainment gathered in one place. 

Ironically enough, I found the app’s greatest strength to also be its greatest weakness. While the app offered a bit of everything, it didn’t excel in any particular area. 

Pros

  • Has a Halloween-specific focus. 
  • Could be convenient for users who prefer a consolidated seasonal app. 
  • Completely free app. 

Cons

  • A multipurpose app may not match specialist tools in every category. 
  • The collection of wallpapers and sounds isn’t extensive. 

Price: Free 

Download 

Best apps for Halloween phone customization 

Get the Halloween theme to your iPhone screen through widgets, scary wallpapers, and countdowns. These apps are ideal for anyone who enjoys celebrating the season through their iPhone or iPad’s appearance. 

11. ThemeMate: DIY Themes & Widgets 

Your Halloween mood doesn’t have to stop at your costume or your front door. ThemeMate: DIY Themes & Widgets is here to personalize your iPhone’s appearance. Imagine unlocking your phone and seeing a coordinated Halloween-inspired design instead of your usual everyday layout.

I use it to get a more unified look, matching icons, widgets, and backgrounds. Moreover, the dynamic Live wallpapers bring the spooky right to your Lock Screen.

Pros

  • Appeals to users who enjoy personalizing their Home Screen. 
  • Offers a seasonal approach to phone customization. 
  • Virtual pets and charging effects make iPhone screen livelier. 

Cons

  • Setup may involve several customization steps. 
  • Some themes, widgets, or design packs may require payment.

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $5.99) 

Download 

12. Crestwall: 4K Wallpapers 

Customizing the whole theme of your iPhone seems daunting? Then the easiest way to make your iPhone feel ready for Halloween is to change its wallpaper.

Crestwall: 4K Wallpapers provides high-resolution wallpapers and pictures in line with your holiday-themed needs. You may choose from a dramatic moonlit landscape, a dark minimalist design, or a creepy illustration that gives your Lock Screen a more mysterious feel.

Pros

  • Focuses on high-resolution wallpaper. 
  • Useful for seasonal Home Screen and Lock Screen refreshes. 
  • Pairs well with other customization tools. 

Cons

  • Halloween-specific content may be limited. 
  • Some wallpaper collections may require a subscription or purchase. 

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $1.99) 

Download 

13. Halloween Countdown Live 2026 

For some people, Halloween excitement starts weeks before October 31. Halloween Countdown Live 2026 is worth considering if you enjoy watching the days tick down to the big night.

I like to add a countdown as it adds anticipation to my daily routine, especially when planning costumes, buying candy, decorating my home, or organizing a party. Rather than repeatedly checking the calendar, it offers a dedicated way to keep Halloween in mind.

Pros

  • Keeps Halloween preparations visible and exciting. 
  • Offers a simple way to track the approaching date. 
  • Multiple themes to match your mood. 

Cons

  • Its main purpose may become less useful after October 31. 
  • Widget and live-display functionality should be verified. 

Price: Free (In-app purchase starts at $2.99) 

Download 

Best apps for trick-or-treating and Halloween safety 

Halloween outings are more enjoyable when everyone knows the plan. Explore haunted attractions and seasonal destinations to find ideas for a memorable night out with friends or family. 

14. Life360: Family Safety GPS 

Though Halloween is fun for kids, sometimes it means a lot of hassle for parents who have to organize everything properly. Life360 is a family location-sharing and safety app that may help participating family members stay informed about one another’s whereabouts. 

For instance, if your kids are going to trick-or-treat in the evening and you plan to host some guests at home, agreed location sharing can make coordination easier. It can also be useful for arranging pickups or meeting at a particular location after an event.  

Pros

  • Supports family coordination during busy Halloween outings. 
  • Can help participating family members share locations and get place alerts. 
  • Useful beyond Halloween for everyday family logistics. 

Cons

  • Some features may require a paid subscription. 
  • Location tracking is not a substitute for supervision or agreed safety rules. 

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $7.99) 

Download 

15. FrightMaps: Haunt Finder 

If you are a real Halloween enthusiast, the most exciting part of October might be visiting a haunted house rather than staying home to watch horror movies. FrightMaps: Haunt Finder is designed to help users discover haunted attractions, making it a useful starting point when planning a spooky outing. 

Instead of relying on word of mouth, you can look for places to visit and build a Halloween itinerary. It could be handy for friends deciding where to spend a weekend evening or for a couple looking for something more memorable than another dinner out.  

Pros

  • Focuses on discovering haunted attractions and spooky outings. 
  • Useful as a starting point for Halloween trip planning. 
  • Know about the latest contests and spooky adventures nearby. 

Cons

  • Some features may require a paid subscription. 
  • Location tracking is not a substitute for supervision or agreed safety rules. 

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $1.99) 

Download 

Final thoughts: Make this Halloween spook-tacular!

Halloween is the perfect time to get creative with your iPhone and iPad, and these apps make it easier to bring the spooky spirit to life. Whether you want to create creepy selfies, enjoy horror games, set the mood with eerie sounds, customize your Home Screen, or plan a fun Halloween outing, there’s something for everyone. You can even use family safety apps to make Halloween adventures easier to coordinate.

My advice is to choose the apps that match your Halloween plans rather than downloading them all. Try a photo editor for spooky selfies, a sound app for your Halloween party, or a customization app to give your iPhone a festive makeover. Which Halloween app are you excited to try this year? Let me know in the comments below, and have a spooktacular Halloween!

title.rendered: How to use Apple Watch Always On display and customize it

content.rendered:
I’m amazed by how much information my Apple Watch can pack into its small screen, especially when using the Modular watch face, which shows information from five different apps. And it gets even better, as I can check the watch face on my Apple Watch without having to wake up the display, thanks to the Always On feature.

On supported models, Always On is turned on by default. Here’s how to enable it on your Apple Watch if you disabled it previously and customize it to serve you better.

What is the Always On feature on the Apple Watch?

Always On is a feature that keeps the watch face on your Apple Watch visible at all times, so you can glance at important information without waking up the display.

When enabled, your Apple Watch shows a simplified version of your watch face whenever your wrist is down. This means essential information, such as the time, notifications, and complications, is visible but with decreased brightness and a lower refresh rate.

Then, as soon as you lift your wrist or tap the screen, your Apple Watch displays the regular watch face with all complication data at full brightness. You can then interact with the watch screen like you normally do.

Apple lets you configure what you want to see in Always On mode on your Apple Watch. Most complications refresh once a minute, whereas complications that display live data, such as Compass and Noise, won’t be active. Apple Watch Series 10 and later and Apple Watch Ultra 3 and later update more often while your wrist is down, and supported watch faces can even show a ticking seconds hand. However, the time is always shown in Always On mode.

Which Apple Watch models support Always On display?

Always On works on Apple Watch Series 5 and newer, Apple Watch SE 3, and every Apple Watch Ultra. The first- and second-generation Apple Watch SE don’t have it. Here’s the full list:

  • Apple Watch Series 5
  • Apple Watch Series 6
  • Apple Watch Series 7
  • Apple Watch Series 8
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 12
  • Apple Watch SE 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 4

watchOS 27 runs on Series 9 and later, SE 3, and Ultra 2 and later. Older models in the list above stay on an earlier watchOS, so their settings screens may look a little different from the steps below.

How to turn on or off the Always On display on an Apple Watch

There are two ways to enable or disable the Always On display feature on an Apple Watch. You can either enable it on the Apple Watch directly or use the Apple Watch app on your iPhone.

On the Apple Watch itself

  1. Open the Settings app.
  2. Select Display & Brightness.
  3. Tap Always On and turn on the toggle.

Using the Apple Watch app on an iPhone

  1. Open the Watch app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap My Watch, then select Display & Brightness.
  3. Select Always On and turn on the toggle on the following page.

You can repeat the above steps and disable the toggle to turn off Always On.

How to customize your Apple Watch’s Always On display

When your Apple Watch is in Always On mode, it displays notifications, complications, or the most recently active app by default. However, you can customize and control what you want to see. Plus, you can choose which apps can appear and display complications and notifications when your wrist is down.

This helps you control the information you see in Always On mode and keep it clutter-free. You can customize these settings on your Apple Watch or in the Apple Watch app on your iPhone.

On the Apple Watch itself

  1. Open Settings and select Display & Brightness.
  2. Tap Always On.
  3. Select Show Complication Data, Show Notifications, or Show Apps.

  4. Use the toggle to enable or disable their visibility on the Always On screen.

  5. In each menu, scroll down and use the toggle to turn off the apps you don’t want to display information on the Always On screen.

On the Watch App on an iPhone

  1. Open the Watch app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap My Watch, select Display & Brightness, and tap Always On.
  3. Select Show Complication Data, Show Notifications, or Show Apps.

  4. In each of these menus, you can choose which apps can display complications, notifications, or app content in Always On mode. Flip the toggle to enable or disable them.

How does Always On impact the battery life of your Apple Watch?

You might be wondering if enabling the Always On display affects the battery of your Apple Watch. It can be a valid concern if your Apple Watch is already old and struggles to last an entire day due to poor battery health.

The truth is, Always On does increase battery consumption. That’s expected of a feature that keeps the display on all the time. That said, the feature dims the display and lowers its refresh rate to optimize battery life. Further, the Always On display turns off automatically when you enable Low Power Mode or Theater Mode on your Apple Watch.

My Apple Watch lasts an entire day without Always On mode. When it is enabled, the battery is fully drained by late evening, so it lasts only about 75 percent of the day. However, this isn’t a standard estimate of the battery drain while using the Always On display. That depends on your model, your Apple Watch’s battery health, and your usage patterns. Based on your experience, you can decide whether to turn off the Always On display if it isn’t necessary or keep it on all the time.

Practical use cases of the Always On display feature on the Apple Watch

I keep the Always On display enabled at all times since I find it quite helpful in several scenarios in my everyday life. If it helps you decide how to use the feature, here are a few practical situations when you might want to enable Always On.

  • A sneak peek at the time: In the middle of a meeting or a long conversation, it may seem disrespectful to flick your wrist to check the time. Having Always On mode enabled helps me check the time without making it obvious.
  • Check workout stats: You wouldn’t want to raise your wrist while running or cycling, as it can be distracting. Always On is a huge blessing in such cases, and it lets me view my workout stats without having to wake the display.
  • Check health vitals during workouts: I always keep an eye on my heart rate and SpO2 levels during high-intensity workouts. Thanks to Always On mode on my Apple Watch, I can glance at such details easily.
  • Quickly view notifications: We all hate being distracted in the middle of a task. Checking notifications without having to raise my wrist off the keyboard is a great advantage. If it were the other way around, I’d check the notification, ponder over it, eventually pick up my iPhone, and then mindlessly use it for an hour.
  • Check timers while cooking: A timer is a cook’s best friend in the kitchen, ensuring you turn off all the knobs and switches at the right time. Always On mode lets me check the status of the timer complication without having to move my wrist or physically interact with my Apple Watch.
  • Check notifications during presentations: Always On lets me subtly check a notification during a presentation or a conversation that demands my focus. This helps me stay engaged and maintain the flow of the discussion without appearing distracted.
  • My Apple Watch looks better: I sometimes pair a watch face and a strap that look great together. So when the watch face is visible all the time, my Apple Watch looks visually appealing.

Wrapping up…

We hope this article helps you enable the Always On feature and check information without having to interact with your Apple Watch. Similarly, there’s another feature that lets you control your Apple Watch without having to touch the display. You can use a few hand gestures to perform actions on your Apple Watch. So do check that out as well!

FAQs

Why isn’t the Always On display working on my Apple Watch?

There could be several reasons. However, you can easily troubleshoot the Always On display when it’s not working on your Apple Watch to get it working again.

Why does the display dim when Always On is enabled?

The display dims in Always On mode to conserve battery life. Keeping the screen at full brightness constantly would drain the battery much faster. Therefore, Apple has designed the Always On feature to tone down the brightness when your Apple Watch is idle.

Do all watch faces support Always On?

As mentioned earlier, the Always On feature simplifies the visuals of the watch face and displays essential information when it is idle. Therefore, in Always On mode, the watch face may not appear as it normally does.

  • How to organize apps on your Apple Watch
  • How to increase Apple Watch screen brightness
  • How to use Apple Watch Control Center
  • Best Apple Watch faces you must try

mainEntity.name: Why does the display dim when Always On is enabled?

acceptedAnswer.text: The display dims in Always On mode to conserve battery life. Keeping the screen at full brightness constantly would drain the battery much faster. Therefore, Apple has designed the Always On feature to tone down the brightness when your Apple Watch is idle.

title.rendered: How to change gamemode in Minecraft: Commands and F3 + F4 switcher

content.rendered:
Wondering how to change gamemode in Minecraft? Well, you’re in the right place, gamers! The sandbox game offers five different gamemodes to choose from, each providing a unique experience. You can switch between them with the /gamemode command or, on Java Edition, the F3 + F4 gamemode switcher, as long as cheats are enabled.

However, switching between them can be a bit difficult, as the game doesn’t clearly explain how to do so. But there’s no need to worry, as we’ve got you covered. So, let’s take a look at how to change gamemode in Minecraft and what each one brings to the table.

All gamemodes in Minecraft explained

As we’ve said before, there are five gamemodes in Minecraft to choose from: Survival, Creative, Adventure, Hardcore and Spectator. Let’s take a look at each of them in detail:

1. Survival mode

Survival Mode is where the real Minecraft journey begins. You’ll be heading out to explore the world, gather resources, craft tools, and fend off hostile mobs in order to stay alive. This won’t be an easy task, as you need to keep an eye on your hunger and health while making the most of the resources you find.

It’s all about starting with nothing, building yourself up, and eventually going up against the Ender Dragon.

2. Creative mode

Want to build your dream base without spending hours gathering materials? Creative Mode has you covered. You start the game with unlimited blocks and items and the ability to fly, and you don’t need to worry about hunger or damage.

You can break blocks instantly and experiment with different building ideas without any restrictions. It’s a perfect choice for players who want to unleash their creativity or simply have fun with friends.

3. Adventure mode

Adventure Mode is all about exploring custom maps, completing quests, and taking on challenges crafted by the Minecraft community. It seems like Survival mode on paper, but there are a few catches.

By default, you won’t be able to place or break blocks freely; what you can do depends on the permissions and tools set by the map’s creator.

4. Spectator mode

Don’t want to deal with mobs or obstacles? Consider switching to Spectator Mode. You can freely fly through blocks, explore underground caves, discover hidden structures, and observe other players without affecting their run.

However, you won’t be able to interact with the world. It’s a great way to explore the world or watch how other players approach the game. Bedrock players have had Spectator mode since the 1.19.50 update, so it’s no longer a Java-only feature.

5. Hardcore mode

Hardcore Mode is just like Survival Mode, but takes everything up a notch. It locks the difficulty to Hard, which means mobs hit like a truck, and staying alive becomes even more challenging. However, the biggest catch is that you only get one life. If you die, you won’t be able to respawn and continue your adventure as usual; you can only spectate the world. It’s a high-risk game mode that puts your Minecraft survival skills to the ultimate test.

However, you can’t switch a regular world into Hardcore mode, as it can only be chosen when creating a new world. Bedrock Edition got Hardcore as a full release with version 1.21.40, so it’s now available on both editions.

How to change gamemode in Minecraft

So, how do you change your gamemode in Minecraft? Well, you first need to enable cheats. If you’re creating a new world, just turn on the Allow Cheats (Java) or Cheats (Bedrock) toggle in the world settings. For an existing world:

  • Java Edition: Press Esc, select Open to LAN, switch Allow Cheats to ON, and click Start LAN World. This only enables cheats for as long as the world stays open to LAN, so you’ll need to repeat it each session.
  • Bedrock Edition: Pause the game, go to Settings > Game, and turn on Activate Cheats. Keep in mind that turning on cheats disables achievements in that world.

Once that’s done, you can switch between game modes using either of these two methods:

1. Use commands

Enter your world and open the chat window by pressing T on your keyboard or tapping the chat icon on your device. Now, type one of the following commands and hit Enter:

  • /gamemode survival
  • /gamemode creative
  • /gamemode adventure
  • /gamemode spectator

On Bedrock, you can also change modes through the Personal Game Mode option in World Settings once cheats are on.

2. Use the gamemode switcher

On Java Edition, you can also use the built-in gamemode switcher to change modes without typing commands. Here’s how:

  • Hold F3 and press F4 to open the gamemode switcher.
  • Keep holding F3 and press F4 to cycle through Survival, Creative, Adventure, and Spectator mode.
  • Release F3 to choose the game mode you wish to play on.

If you’re on a laptop and nothing happens, try holding the Fn key as well, since F3 and F4 are often mapped to hardware controls.

Wrapping up

Minecraft offers five different game modes, each providing a unique experience for players. Whether you want to build freely, survive against mobs, or explore the world, there’s a game mode for every playstyle.

To switch between them, you’ll need to enable cheats or have the required permissions. Once that’s done, you can use commands or the gamemode switcher to choose your preferred playstyle and continue your adventure in Minecraft.

FAQs

Can you change gamemode in Minecraft without cheats?

No, you need to enable cheats in order to change gamemodes in Minecraft. Once that’s done, you can use commands or the gamemode switcher to do so.

What is the command to change gamemode in Minecraft?

The command to change gamemode in Minecraft is /gamemode, followed by the mode you wish to play. For instance, enter /gamemode creative to play Creative mode.

Can you change gamemode in Minecraft multiplayer?

Yes, but you need operator (op) permissions, which can be granted by the server owner, to change gamemode in Minecraft multiplayer. The F3 + F4 shortcut on Java servers also depends on those permissions.

mainEntity.name: How can I bypass the Activation Lock on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You cannot legally bypass Activation Lock. Apple designed it as a security feature to prevent stolen devices from being used. The only way to remove it is by entering the original Apple Account and password. If you forgot your Apple Account, visit Apple's official recovery page.

mainEntity.name: Does factory resetting remove the Activation Lock?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Factory resetting does not remove the Activation Lock from an Apple device. Activation Lock can only be disabled by turning off Find My iPhone before erasing the device.

title.rendered: Adaptive Power vs. Low Power Mode on iPhone: Which is better?

content.rendered:
An iPhone excels in almost everything it offers, except when it comes to battery capacity compared to its competition. For years, Low Power Mode has been the go-to feature for users wanting to squeeze extra hours out of their iPhones. Since iOS 26, Apple has offered a feature called Adaptive Power alongside the long-standing Low Power Mode.

While both aim to extend your iPhone’s battery life, they work in very different ways: Adaptive Power is limited to iPhone 15 Pro and newer, while Low Power Mode works on almost every iPhone. So, if you’re wondering which one to use, Adaptive Power or Low Power Mode, you’re in the right place. This guide explains how each works, their differences, and the best situations to use them.

What is Low Power Mode?

Low Power Mode has been around since iOS 9 and is available on all modern iPhones. Once enabled, it immediately reduces system activity and pauses power-hungry background tasks to extend battery life.

The mode reduces overall iPhone power usage by:

  • Disabling background app refresh
  • Reducing display brightness
  • Stopping automatic downloads and mail fetch
  • Reducing some visual effects
  • Pausing iCloud Photos for a while
  • Shortening Auto-Lock to 30 seconds

You can enable or disable Low Power Mode manually at any time. If Adaptive Power is on, Low Power Mode turns on by itself when your battery dips below 20%. Without Adaptive Power, iOS prompts you to turn it on at that level. Once your iPhone charges to 80% or higher, it turns off automatically.

When active, the battery icon turns yellow in the status bar instead of white.

Although you can use Low Power Mode even when your iPhone is fully charged, Apple designed it as an emergency power-saving feature, making it best when your iPhone is running low and you can’t plug it in right away.

What is Adaptive Power?

Adaptive Power debuted in iOS 26 as Apple’s smart battery optimization tool, and it’s still part of iOS 27. Unlike Low Power Mode, which aggressively reduces power usage until turned off, Adaptive Power runs quietly in the background. It uses on-device analysis of your recent usage to predict when you’ll need extra battery life.

Think of it as a smart efficiency assistant, fine-tuning your iPhone’s power usage in real time without making the phone feel sluggish.

Example: If you’re editing a batch of RAW photos, Adaptive Power may dim the display slightly, limit background activity, or adjust performance to save energy, all while remaining almost unnoticeable. It leaves performance alone while you use the camera or play games with Game Mode on.

Adaptive Power is available on iPhone 15 Pro and newer models, including the latest iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo.

Key differences between Adaptive Power and Low Power Mode

Here’s a quick comparison:

Which one should you use?

The answer depends on your iPhone model:

  • If you own an iPhone 15, iPhone 15 Plus, or an older model, you only get Low Power Mode.
  • If you have an iPhone 15 Pro or newer, you can use both.

Use Adaptive Power Mode if:

  • You want hands-free, smart battery management.
  • You have an iPhone 15 Pro or newer.
  • You regularly perform heavy tasks but don’t want big performance drops.

Use Low Power Mode if:

  • Your battery is critically low.
  • You want manual control over when to save power.
  • You’re traveling or going hours without charging.
  • Your battery health has dropped below 80%, and you want to stretch it without replacing it.

How to turn on or off Adaptive Power and Low Power Mode

On iPhone 15 and later, Low Power Mode sits on the Power Mode screen, and on models that support Adaptive Power, both switches live there together.

Low Power Mode:

  1. Open Settings → Battery → Power Mode, then toggle on Low Power Mode.
  2. Alternatively, swipe down from the top-right corner, tap the battery icon in Control Center, and turn on Low Power Mode.

You can also ask Siri to enable it.

Adaptive Power:

  1. Open Settings → Battery → Power Mode.
  2. Toggle on Adaptive Power.

Adaptive Power is on by default on iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 17, iPhone 17e, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, and iPhone Air. It starts off on iPhone 16 models, iPhone 16e, and iPhone 15 Pro models, so you need to switch it on yourself. It also needs at least 7 days to learn your charging habits before it kicks in. Adaptive Power Notifications is a separate toggle on the same screen, and turning it off doesn’t stop Adaptive Power from saving battery.

Tips to maximize iPhone battery life beyond power modes

Besides relying on these two features, here are everyday habits that can boost battery life:

  • Lower screen brightness or enable Auto-Brightness.
  • Limit Background App Refresh for unnecessary apps.
  • Enable Optimized Battery Charging for long-term health.
  • Turn off Location Services for apps that don’t need it.
  • Use Airplane Mode in low-signal areas to reduce drain.

Final verdict

Both Adaptive Power Mode and Low Power Mode are valuable, but they serve different purposes.

  • Adaptive Power is your smart, everyday companion that optimizes in the background.
  • Low Power Mode is your emergency savior when every percent counts.

The best strategy is to use both. Let Adaptive Power handle daily efficiency, and switch to Low Power Mode when your iPhone’s battery gets critically low.

Which one do you prefer, the subtle efficiency of Adaptive Power or the aggressive savings of Low Power Mode? Share your thoughts in the comments.

keyPoints.title: What is Low Power Mode?
keyPoints.explanation: Low Power Mode is an available feature on all modern iPhones that reduces system activity and pauses background tasks to extend battery life, especially useful when the battery is low.

keyPoints.title: What is Adaptive Power in iOS 26?
keyPoints.explanation: Adaptive Power is Apple's new smart battery optimization tool introduced in iOS 26, which runs quietly in the background and activates during high-demand tasks to conserve energy without noticeable performance drops.

keyPoints.title: Key differences between Adaptive Power and Low Power Mode
keyPoints.explanation: Adaptive Power automatically activates during demanding tasks on newer iPhones and makes minimal adjustments, while Low Power Mode is manually toggled and causes noticeable slowdown to maximize battery savings.

keyPoints.title: Which one should you use?
keyPoints.explanation: Use Adaptive Power if you want automatic, intelligent management of power on compatible iPhone models, and Low Power Mode if you need manual control or are experiencing critically low battery.

keyPoints.title: Tips to maximize iPhone battery life beyond power modes
keyPoints.explanation: Improve battery life through habits like lowering screen brightness, limiting background app refresh, enabling optimized charging, turning off unnecessary location services, and using airplane mode in low-signal areas.

  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

title.rendered: How to get the Jack-O’-Cat sidekick in Fortnite before it leaves

content.rendered:
The Jack-O’-Cat sidekick is a cat-like companion that has made its way into Fortnite. Its central theme is Halloween, and it is inspired by the Sugar skin, which is also currently available in the Item Shop.

As part of the Fortnitemares lineup of cosmetics, the Jack-O’-Cat sidekick is up for grabs for 1,200 V-Bucks until October 27 at 5 PM PT / 8 PM ET. Even though it has an obvious link to the Sugar skin, it is surprisingly not included in the Sugar Bundle, which costs 1,600 V-Bucks. Keep reading to find out how you can claim the sidekick in the game.

Steps to get the Jack-O’-Cat sidekick in Fortnite

  1. Open Fortnite and navigate to the Shop tab.
  2. Scroll down to the Locker of Horrors section and select the Jack-O’-Cat sidekick.
  3. Press and hold the Purchase button to confirm your purchase.

After you purchase Jack-O’-Cat, you can customize it to your liking. However, you only get to do this once, and the appearance you lock in will stay on this sidekick permanently. You can tailor the colors of its base, accent, details, and eyes.

Jack-O’-Cat rewards: Items unlocked using Sidekick Points

As soon as you unlock Jack-O’-Cat, you will see its quests in the Sidekicks section of the Quests tab in Fortnite. By equipping this sidekick in eligible matches, you can earn Sidekick Points that help complete these side missions and unlock a bunch of rewards. Each stage needs 1,500 Sidekick Points, so you’ll need 6,000 in total to unlock everything listed below.

  1. Sweet Fish (emote)
  2. Pumpkin Heart (reaction)
  3. Jack-O’-Cat (Candy) (style)
  4. Midnight Meow (sidekick emote)

All Sugar cosmetics in Fortnite

1. Jack-O’-Cat sidekick

  • Price: 1,200 V-Bucks

2. Sugar

  • Price: 1,000 V-Bucks
  • Also available in: Sugar Bundle

3. Lollypopper

  • Price: 800 V-Bucks
  • Also available in: Sugar Bundle

4. Sugar’s Steppers

  • Price: 600 V-Bucks
  • Also available in: Sugar Bundle

5. Sugar Bomb

  • Price: 500 V-Bucks
  • Also available in: Sugar Bundle

Wrapping up

Jack-O’-Cat is yet another Halloween-appropriate sidekick introduced by Fortnite this spooky season. Before this, the devs released Rowena Rabbit and The Knight as sidekicks for eager players. Apart from these, the usual sidekicks that are more cute than spooky, such as Jimothy, have also been rolled out.

While the Jack-O’-Cat sidekick is a fun cosmetic to equip on its own, for those who also own the Sugar skin, this sidekick more or less completes the look. It will be interesting to see if Jack-O’-Cat can rival other noteworthy sidekick arrivals from earlier in October, especially the Hollow Knight collab sidekick, in terms of popularity.

You might also like:

  • How to unlock and find Finger Guns in Fortnite
  • How to get the Dollie skin in Fortnite
  • Stalkboxes in Fortnite: What they do and how to find them

title.rendered: Google Maps on CarPlay now has Gemini, and it handles follow-ups

content.rendered:
Google Maps is rolling out Gemini in navigation on Apple CarPlay, letting iPhone users ask questions about places, request routes, and report traffic disruptions by voice. The rollout began on October 21, bringing Google’s conversational assistant onto the car display while Maps is navigating.

The appealing part is being able to keep the conversation going. Ask about a place, ask whether now is a good time to visit, then ask for directions that avoid tolls. That’s closer to how a person gives directions, assuming your passenger has resisted the urge to say “I think it was that turning” after you’ve passed it.

US drivers get it now; the global rollout has fewer specifics

Gemini in Google Maps on CarPlay is available in the US, with a global rollout also underway. Google hasn’t announced a country-by-country schedule, so drivers elsewhere shouldn’t take “rolling out globally” as a promise that the button is already waiting in their car.

The entry point is inside Google Maps during navigation. Tap the Gemini icon on the right side of the CarPlay screen to start talking. This is a Maps feature, so look there rather than searching the CarPlay app launcher for a new Gemini app.

Keep Maps updated on your iPhone, but don’t assume an app update will make a gradual rollout reach you immediately. A missing button is frustrating enough without turning it into an afternoon of reinstalling things.

Gemini is coming to Google Maps navigation on CarPlay, bringing you a helpful, conversational assistant right to your in-car display. Try asking things like: 🚗 “What park is famous for gorgeous views overlooking the city?” 🌤️ “I want to go at a time when it’s not too busy and the weather will stay nice. Is now a good time?” 🧭 “Start navigating me there but make sure to avoid toll roads.” Rolling out now everywhere Gemini is available — just tap the Gemini icon in Google Maps on your car’s display to try it on your next drive.

— Google Maps (@googlemaps) October 21, 2026

Ask about a place, then turn the answer into a route

You can ask which park has a view over Seattle, follow up about crowds and weather, and then request navigation there while avoiding toll roads. The questions build on the destination being discussed, saving you from repeating its name with every request.

You can also use the conversation to find stops along your way and get information about places. That’s useful when the decision is more complicated than choosing the nearest pin. Finding somewhere worth stopping, checking whether it fits the trip, and adding it to the route should belong in the same interaction.

This sits alongside the earlier Ask Maps experience, which brought more detailed, conversational place searches to the phone. The new part here is having Gemini available in the CarPlay navigation view. Previously, Google’s assistant functionality in Maps was available directly on the iPhone, without the equivalent experience on the CarPlay screen.

Voice reporting is included too. Drivers can tell Gemini about traffic disruptions instead of working through the reporting controls. That’s the kind of small convenience I’d use more often than an elaborate conversation about the perfect afternoon out. Sometimes the useful contribution is simply that the road ahead is a mess.

Gemini in Maps doesn’t replace Siri or become a separate CarPlay app

CarPlay already has standalone conversational apps such as ChatGPT and Claude. This release puts Gemini inside a navigation app you may already be using. It doesn’t establish a separate Gemini app for CarPlay or make Google’s assistant the system-wide replacement for Siri.

Apple has its own Siri AI and voice-control changes in iOS 27 CarPlay. Google’s addition gives Maps users another way to handle their trip, rather than requiring them to switch navigation apps whenever they want a more conversational request.

Personal Intelligence hasn’t been confirmed for CarPlay, even as Google rolls it out for Android Auto. Don’t assume Gemini on the dashboard can now use your Gmail or Calendar just because another version of Gemini can.

I’d judge this update on whether it understands the destination and follows the route request with fewer taps. Finding the park and skipping the tolls would be a useful start. The grander business of reorganizing my life can wait until I’ve parked.

excerpt.rendered: Google Maps brings conversational Gemini to CarPlay navigation. US access is live, a global rollout is underway, and Personal Intelligence remains unconfirmed.

title.rendered: Apple Music’s new logo was made from real sound waves

content.rendered:
Apple Music has unveiled a new brand identity, with a redesigned wordmark, musical-note imagery, and an original composition by Fred again.. and NEST Acoustics. Apple calls it “made by sound,” and this time the branding slogan comes with a fairly convincing science demonstration.

The team played musical frequencies through a rig, used the vibrations to move liquid, and filmed what happened to the Apple Music graphics underneath. The ripples and refractions became part of the new look. Somewhere, a perfectly serviceable logo-design brief turned into a physics experiment. I’m glad it did.

Fred again.. helped write the music that shaped the visuals

Apple’s behind-the-scenes film follows the process from sound to moving image. Individual notes create physical vibrations, which send waves through the liquid and distort the brand elements seen through it. Change the sound and you change the movement on camera.

Fred again.. and NEST Acoustics supplied the original composition behind that movement. It also gives the identity its own short musical signature, so the sound and animation belong together from the start. That’s a fitting approach for a music service: let the musicians influence what the thing looks like, too.

Apple says the visuals were captured entirely in camera. The glassy edges and shifting colors have a physical source, which makes the film more interesting than another animation that simply tells you a logo is exciting now. You can see the process in Apple’s video below.

The new wordmark has personality. But we’ll still miss the red branding on Apple Music

The Apple symbol now sits beside heavier, tightly packed lowercase “music” lettering. The musical note also gets a more expressive treatment, with the announcement showing it surrounded by liquid-like edges and flashes of color.

The wider shift toward black-and-white branding is more divisive for me. The old red gave Apple Music an immediately recognizable spot among your apps. A monochrome icon has to work harder to stand out beside all the other monochrome icons. Apparently, every app wants to wear the same outfit now.

The moving identity is where this redesign makes the strongest case for itself. Light bends around the note, colors appear at its edges, and the wordmark ripples with the composition. Those effects fit neatly into Apple’s broader Liquid Glass design language, while giving the music service an effect built around its own subject.

Apple has already paired a media rebrand with a musician through Apple TV’s new identity and Finneas sound. Fred again.. and NEST Acoustics give Apple Music its own version of that audiovisual introduction. A streaming service’s identity now apparently needs credits. At least these credits explain something worth watching.

The branding is official; the app rollout is still catching up

Parts of the refresh appeared during the iOS 27.2 beta cycle, including a black-and-white Music app icon. Those early app changes and the newly announced identity are parts of the same refresh, although the promotional animation and the small Home Screen icon serve very different jobs.

Apple’s launch post doesn’t give a complete platform-by-platform rollout schedule. If your devices still show the older branding, that alone doesn’t mean anything is broken. I’d wait for the normal software updates rather than install a beta to acquire a different-colored musical note.

This announcement is about the service’s look and sound as a brand. It doesn’t announce a new listening feature or subscription benefit. I like the craft behind it; the songs still have to do the rest.

title.rendered: Honey Sprite in Fortnite: What it does and how to get it

content.rendered:
Honey Sprite has finally landed in Fortnite, completing the lineup of community-made sprites scheduled to release this season. It is the fifth such sprite to roll out in Fortnite Override, following X-Ray Sprite, Onigiri Sprite, Pond Sprite, and Dumpster Dive Sprite. It is also the twenty-seventh unique sprite currently available in the game overall.

Created by Conejito_sam, Honey Sprite was one of the winning submissions in Fortnite’s Design A Sprite Concept Royale, which took place in June and July. It was pushed into the game in the October 15 update (v42.40), alongside the Obsession-inspired One Wish Willow Sprite and the Quack sprite variant.

You can learn about Honey Sprite’s abilities and the various ways to add it to your collection in the following guide.

What Honey Sprite does in Fortnite

When equipped, Honey Sprite grants you a rather peculiar ability. Staying true to its name, it offers a chance of a swarm of bees being unleashed on your enemy when you deal damage to them using a gun or any other ranged weapon.

This ability also comes into play if you fire at anything other than an enemy, with the bees emerging at the hit point.

As you upgrade this Epic-tier sprite through its levels, the likelihood of a bee swarm appearing near your target increases steadily, from 5% at level 1 to 10% at level 5. There are also five other Honey Sprite variants you can master in Fortnite, as laid out below.

Honey Sprite variants and their uses

Besides the base variant, the following variants of Honey Sprite exist in Fortnite. On top of the bee ability, each variant grants an additional benefit based on its type.

  • Gold Honey Sprite: Gives three times more XP for eliminating an enemy.
  • Cheat Master Honey Sprite: Lets you enter cheat codes by tapping the buttons in any order.
  • Loot Hacker Honey Sprite: Increases the chances of items from your Loot Hacks appearing during a match.
  • Bounty Hunter Honey Sprite: Gives you a chance to obtain a Sprite by eliminating an opponent. However, this variant earns XP only from eliminations.
  • Trick or Treat Honey Sprite: Increases the chances of getting Halloween candy consumables from chests and other containers.

How to find Honey Sprite in Fortnite

1. Cheat codes

The best way to get your hands on Honey Sprite is by using cheat codes. Since it is a sprite of Epic rarity, you should aim to interact with pink and golden cheat codes, both of which usually offer Epic and higher-tier sprites.

In Fortnite Battle Royale, the most cheat code-dense areas are Heatwave Harbor, Cluster Coast and Sunken Shores, followed by Shaken Sanctuary. You can either visit these areas and scour them for the input consoles or use a Cheat Code Locator gizmo to mark a nearby cheat code. Those looking for this item can use one of the corresponding Fortnite Lobby Hacks to get it for free.

2. Pumpkin Chests

These are a special type of chest introduced in Fortnitemares 2026. Each one offers a sprite from the current roster, generally leaning towards the spooky-themed ones.

You can find multiple Pumpkin Chests in POIs such as Nightmare Neighborhood, Freaky Fields, Freddy Fazbear Pizzeria, Green Hill Zone, Shaken Sanctuary and Wonkeeland. It’s advisable to go through these locations while keeping an eye out for enemy players.

3. Rare Chests

If you have the Loot Hacker sprite equipped and the All Sprite Variants Loot Hack maxed out, you have a strong chance of getting sprites, including Honey Sprite, simply by opening chests, especially Rare Chests.

The places with the most of these blue-colored chests include Nightmare Neighborhood, Stone Sanctum, the Pac-Man islands, Cluster Coast, and the maze that lies northeast of Sunken Shores. These are some of the most highly contested hotspots on the Fortnite map, so it’s recommended to load up on ammunition before going there.

4. Get eliminations with the Bounty Hunter variant

Bounty Hunter sprites in Fortnite are very useful for growing your sprite collection, since they have a strong chance of providing a sprite when you eliminate an opponent. In other words, players who don’t want to be distracted by hunting for chests or cheat codes can rack up sprites as they go about their matches naturally.

5. Borrow and index it with the help of a friend

If you have a friend in Fortnite who already owns Honey Sprite, or can find someone willing to lend theirs temporarily, this is the easiest and most efficient way. The two of you just have to play a couple of matches together.

In the first match, ask your friend to let you take the sprite and extract with it to index it in your collection. In the second match, do the same thing in reverse and return the sprite to its original owner. Later, go to the Override tab, open the Sprites tab, and recall Honey Sprite from the list using Sprite Dust.

If you can’t find help this way, you can check out the official Fortnite Discord server for like-minded players.

Rounding up

Honey Sprite is among the more intriguing sprites in Fortnite, since it gives players an entirely new threat to deploy on enemies. It is also the final missing piece of the community-made sprites puzzle that was first teased at the beginning of the season.

It will be interesting to see how players warm up to this sprite and how popular it becomes among the current crop of these critters.

  • Stalkboxes in Fortnite: What they do and how to find them
  • 10 Safety In Numbers quests and rewards in Fortnite

title.rendered: Claude Duet wants to run your to-do list. First, join the waitlist

content.rendered:
Anthropic has introduced Claude Duet, an AI assistant that messages you first, checks what needs doing, and keeps working after you close your laptop. It can prepare a morning briefing, chase down unpaid invoices, or build a dashboard while you’re somewhere else.

The research preview opened on October 21. Duet runs on Claude Opus 5.5, with a separate app for iPhone and Android and web access at claude.ai. Anthropic is pitching it to professionals and small business owners. People whose to-do lists have started developing their own to-do lists, basically.

Only Pro and Max subscribers, and only in the US

You need a US Claude account, a Pro or Max subscription, and an invitation from the waitlist. Paying gets you eligibility. Then you wait for the email. Free, Team, and Enterprise users aren’t included in this preview.

Invitations are going out in waves, with no guaranteed date. If you’re in India, even a Max subscription won’t get you into the current preview. I’d hold off on upgrading just for Duet until Anthropic expands access.

There’s no extra Duet charge during the preview, but it shares your existing Claude usage limits. Its morning briefs and background checks count too. So yes, the assistant can use up some of your allowance before you’ve even opened a chat. Bigger jobs, such as financial models or slide decks, use more of it.

It can deal with the inbox or even with coding works

Duet sends a morning brief based on your connected accounts, then checks them every few hours for things that need your attention. You can tell it what deserves an interruption and how often you want updates. An assistant that announces every email has merely invented another inbox.

You can hand it work by typing or speaking. It has its own cloud computer and browser, so your devices don’t need to stay on. When a task is finished or needs your decision, it sends a notification. Your existing Claude memory, skills, and connected apps come with you, saving another round of explaining your job to a chatbot.

Anthropic says Duet can use more than 6,000 Marketplace connectors and plugins. Its examples include finding missed Gmail and Slack messages, drafting invoice reminders from QuickBooks, and preparing payroll in Gusto. It can also put together forecasts, presentations, dashboards, and web apps.

That’s a lot of responsibility for something you message from your phone. I’d start with the invoice reminder and see whether it understood the invoice.

It still needs your permission to send, spend, sign, or delete

Duet can read information and prepare work on its own. Before sending a message, making a payment, signing a document, or deleting anything, it’s designed to show you the action and wait for approval. Securities trading and moving money between accounts remain off-limits even if you say yes.

Purchases can go through Stripe’s Link wallet or Shopify’s Shop Pay. With Link, you approve the spend and it pays using a virtual card, keeping your real card number out of the transaction. Support for signing into sites through 1Password is coming later.

Anthropic also says Duet never directly sees passwords or sign-in tokens. A new safety check is designed to block sharing information such as card numbers and government IDs; sharing health or personal-finance details requires explicit instructions. That approval screen still deserves a read. An AI-written email can be wrong in impressively fluent English.

Grok Bot, OpenAI Dots, Meta Muse. Everybody wants the job

Grok Bot already offers teams of agents that work across apps on a shared cloud computer. Its current beta covers eligible Grok and Cursor subscriptions, with a separate Bot usage allowance. That’s a different arrangement from Duet dipping into your regular Claude limits.

OpenAI Dots take on ongoing responsibilities inside ChatGPT, can reach you through Slack or Teams, and delegate work to ChatGPT Work or Codex. They’re rolling out to eligible Pro, Business Premium, and Enterprise accounts, with plan and regional restrictions. If your work already lives there, that continuity is a reason to look at Dots before adding another assistant.

Meta’s Muse leans further into personal errands, including shopping and booking travel, with access through its app or WhatsApp. Meta’s announced rollout starts in the US, with free access for much of its functionality and subscriptions for heavier use. Anthropic admits Duet’s personal errands, including ticket booking, are less developed. I’d take that admission seriously before handing it a holiday.

Duet’s appeal is strongest if Claude already knows your work. Switching assistants means reconnecting accounts and explaining yourself again. I need a better reason than a new app icon.

You can’t watch its browser yet. I’d like that fixed

Duet currently won’t let you watch or take over its browser. It can’t access local computer files, Microsoft 365 isn’t available yet, and some connectors have restrictions. The enormous connector count deserves that footnote.

Anthropic acknowledges that Duet can misread conversations or get urgency wrong. Something important can also arrive between its periodic checks. I’ll happily take help drafting a reminder, but I’d keep checking time-sensitive messages myself until the preview has earned more trust.

title.rendered: One Piece pirate chest in Fortnite: Here’s where you can find it

content.rendered:
The forthcoming collaboration between Fortnite and One Piece has been something of an open secret for weeks now. In what appears to be the first implicit confirmation, a pirate chest has spawned on the Battle Royale island, possibly teasing players about the coming together of these two hugely popular IPs.

Thanks to the sudden appearance of this unmissable chest, which sits in a lagoon east of Sunken Shores, many Fortnite players have been flocking to it in anticipation of the Fortnite x One Piece collab, which is expected to be fully revealed soon. You can learn more about the pirate chest, its exact location in Fortnite, and the highly anticipated crossover below.

One Piece chest location in Fortnite

The pirate chest is well marked with a treasure chest icon on Fortnite’s Battle Royale map. Its location is flanked by Sunken Shores on the west and Pinky Island on the east. Moreover, it lies directly south of Mega Maze, the shapeshifting maze that is another POI known for being highly contested.

Upon reaching the exact spot, you will come across a giant chest emblazoned with a Jolly Roger. Parts of it may appear translucent blue, depending on how much of it has loaded in the game at that point in time. The other parts are opaque and painted in conventional colors. At the time of writing, more than half of the chest had yet to load.

The chest loads in one stage per day at 9 AM ET (6 AM PT) and should be fully visible by the end of this week.

According to information shared by X users Luwani and Wenso and corroborated by popular leaker SpushFNBR, you can hear certain songs playing near the chest. These songs are reportedly:

  • Birdbrain by Jamie Paige (ft. Kasane Teto)
  • Miku by Anamanaguchi (ft. Hatsune Miku)
  • RIOT by A$AP Rocky
  • What You Saying by Lil Uzi Vert

There are also voiceovers discovered in the game’s files that are audible in the vicinity of the chest.

Fortnite x One Piece collab: What to expect

According to leaks going back to late September, Fortnite x One Piece is planned as a mini-season for November. It would follow right after the Fortnite Override season, which is scheduled to run until October 31. Besides that, files for a similar crossover with the famed anime franchise were also spotted in Rocket League, another online multiplayer title owned by Epic Games.

ONE PIECE SHOULD BE THIS YEAR’S MINI SEASON 🔥👀 I’ve heard from many sources that One Piece will be happening at the end of this year, and will most likely be the November mini season! Recent Rocket League leaks seem to confirm this! #Fortnite | via: me & @SamLeakss https://t.co/YHZhRvYQ9J

— SpushFNBR (@SpushFNBR) September 23, 2026

Moving on from the mini-season reports, not much concrete information has surfaced about what the Fortnite x One Piece event may entail. However, judging by how previous Fortnite mini-seasons played out, we may see a themed Battle Pass, new map POIs, and loot pool updates roll out in the game.

Epic has also started teasing the mini-season itself. Posters spotted in Madrid and Tokyo this week show anime-style Fortnite characters and a pirate skull, though no One Piece characters. A$AP Rocky also teased a Fortnite collab with pirate imagery on October 21.

Wrapping up

The giant pirate chest is one of the most intriguing additions to Fortnite’s Chapter 7 Season 4 map as the Override season approaches its end. Its changing appearance, reported music, and voice lines have given players plenty to speculate about.

If the rumored One Piece crossover becomes official, it could become one of the best Fortnite collabs, bringing exciting new cosmetics, map changes, and themed gameplay to the island. However, Epic Games has yet to confirm the collaboration or reveal what it might include.

For now, players can visit the lagoon east of Sunken Shores and south of Mega Maze to check out the chest for themselves. We’ll know more when Epic Games shares an official announcement.

Don’t miss these related reads:

  • All Pumpkin Chest locations in Fortnite
  • How to find and use the Skeleton Key in Fortnite

title.rendered: How to get Quack Sprites in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4

content.rendered:
In the final weeks of Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4, the Quack Sprite variant has been brought back to the game after last appearing in the previous season, Runners. The v42.40 update on October 15 added five Quack Sprites alongside the new Honey and One Wish Willow Sprites, taking the total Sprite count in Fortnite Override to 162 different versions.

What separates the Quack Sprites from others is the exclusive way in which they need to be acquired. Unlike the various other Sprites, including original ones and those stemming from brand collabs, these Sprites can’t be obtained by any of the traditional methods, such as using cheat codes, opening chests, or even smashing the Pumpkin Chests that arrived with Fortnitemares.

Instead, each Quack Sprite requires you to master a certain number of Sprites in order to unlock it. Moreover, you only have until November 1 (Eastern Time) to tackle this challenge, as the Fortnite Override season ends on that day. Below, you can learn more about this Sprite variant itself and the different Sprite Mastery levels at which different Quack Sprites become claimable.

What Quack Sprites do in Fortnite?

Quack Sprites have a peculiar benefit in the sense that they don’t outright provide a gameplay boost or grant a unique ability. On the contrary, they do their work behind the scenes. According to Epic’s v42.40 update notes, whenever a Quack Sprite gains XP, every other Sprite you’re carrying gets extra Sprite XP as well. Community guides put that bonus at 50% of the XP the Quack Sprite earns.

That allows you to level up several Sprites at the same time in a single match, which makes a Quack Sprite most useful once you already have one and are pushing for the next mastery milestone.

All Quack Sprites in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4

There are five different Quack Sprites available in Fortnite Override, namely:

  • Quack Jonesy Sprite
  • Quack Adventure Sprite
  • Quack Bush Sprite
  • Quack Klombo Sprite
  • Quack Spooky Dash Sprite

How to get Quack Sprite in Fortnite

As mentioned earlier, a particular Quack Sprite can only be unlocked by reaching a particular level of Sprite Mastery. Mastery corresponds to the number of Sprites that you level up to Level 5 through eliminations, opening chests, opening ammo boxes, and so on, and then successfully extract during a match.

You can either master a Sprite in one match itself, which would usually require you to go all the way and achieve a Victory Royale. Optionally, you can also level up a Sprite to an extent and extract it. Since these leveled-up Sprites retain their progress, you can continue where you left off in the next match, max the Sprite out, and extract the same eventually. Keep in mind that each Sprite counts only once toward your mastery total.

Here, you can check the number of Sprites that you would need to master in order to get any given Quack Sprite in Fortnite.

If you go further and master 70 Sprites, the same final Mastery page also rewards a new style for the Pixel Polli outfit.

Lastly, once you have reached the desired level, don’t forget to go to the Override tab and then the Mastery tab, from where you can easily claim the unlocked Quack Sprite.

How to reach the higher mastery levels faster

Since the Quack Jonesy Sprite unlocks first, it makes sense to equip it as soon as you claim it. Every match after that levels your other carried Sprites alongside it, which helps close the 20-Sprite gap between Quack Jonesy and Quack Klombo. Landing at loot-heavy spots, opening every chest and ammo box early, and extracting a Sprite as soon as it hits Level 5 also keep your progress safe.

How Season 4 Quack Sprites differ from Season 3

The Quack variant first arrived in Chapter 7 Season 3 with update v41.30 on July 30, 2026. Back then, it covered four different Sprites: Quack Water (35 mastered Sprites), Quack Earth (40), Quack Fire (45) and Quack Zero Point (55).

This season’s five Quack Sprites are built on different base Sprites and need up to 60 mastered Sprites, so they’re tracked separately from the Season 3 set.

How the Sprite pool has changed

Throughout Fortnite Override, Sprites have received a lot of interesting updates, ranging from brand-collab Sprites to community-made ones. The latest update from October 15 brought the One Wish Willow Sprite, the Honey Sprite and the Quack Sprites into the mix, which further populated and diversified the existing pool.

Given that this time it’s just two new Sprites and the return of an older variant from Fortnite Runners, some players may have found it not as exciting as they would have hoped.

However, the coupled rollout of the One Wish Willow Sprite and the Quack Sprites makes it a suitable time for those players pushing to complete and master their Sprite collection before a new Fortnite season kicks off. One Wish Willow lets you pull out an enemy’s equipped Sprites as soon as you eliminate them, while also knocking nearby enemies back when you take damage. The only catch is that removing it marks you on the map.
