title.rendered: Download spooky Halloween wallpapers for iPhone in 4K

content.rendered:
It’s time to add a touch of horror to your iPhone screen! Give your device a spooky makeover this Halloween with a collection of wallpapers we’ve curated especially for you. From ghostly figures and glowing pumpkins to eerie landscapes and creepy characters, there’s something for every Halloween lover.

Whether you prefer cute Halloween designs or dark, chilling scenes, these wallpapers will bring the perfect spooky vibe to your Lock Screen and Home Screen. Explore our collection below and download the best Halloween wallpapers for iPhone in stunning 4K quality to celebrate the season in style.

1. Ghost over the starlit village 

A cheerful little ghost floats above a charming village, holding a glowing pumpkin lantern. I like how the sky with a crescent moon, glowing stars, and a fairytale castle on the mountain creates a Halloween dreamscape. 

Download

2. Gothic midnight 

If you want a classic haunted castle on your screen, go for this one. A towering gothic mansion beneath a golden full moon with flying bats and swirling fog makes the atmosphere eerie. 

Download

3. Halloween witch kitten 

Who said Halloween wallpaper can’t be cute? Check out this one. A fluffy black kitten wearing a witch hat sits atop ancient spellbooks surrounded by warm candles, pumpkins, and autumn leaves.  

Download

4. Haunted Halloween pattern 

A beautiful Halloween pattern features smiling pumpkins, adorable white ghosts, black bats, tiny spiders, candy corn, and orange maple leaves. The dark background makes the bright decorations stand out beautifully. 

Download

5. Halloween pumpkin field 

A mist-covered pumpkin field stretches beneath an orange sunset. Glowing jack-o’-lanterns, a distant scarecrow, and skeletal trees make it a scene from a supernatural film.

Download

6. Minimalist Halloween twilight 

Next is a minimalist wallpaper with a crescent moon and scattered bats against a dramatic sky. I loved how the twisted tree and distant mountains complete this simple yet striking Halloween scene. 

Download

7. Rain-soaked Jack-o’-Lantern 

If your Halloween means pumpkin decoration, this wallpaper is ideal. A carved pumpkin glows intensely on a rain-soaked porch with reflections across the pavement. It creates a dramatic autumn-night setting. 

Download

8. Rainy autumn candlelight 

Here is a rainy Halloween evening with a perfect romantic setting. Flickering candles, miniature pumpkins, old books, and a steaming mug create a comforting autumn sanctuary. 

Download

9. Smoldering Jack-o’-Lantern  

Looking for spooky dark wallpaper? A menacing carved pumpkin emerges from near-total darkness, creating a haunting, high-contrast design for horror lovers. 

Download

10. Violet crystal Jack-o’-Lantern   

Another Jack- o’-Lantern wallpaper, but this time it’s a glossy, crystal-like pumpkin shining with vivid violet reflections. Its dramatic dark backdrop gives a futuristic fantasy Halloween aesthetic. 

Download

11. Blood Moon Haunted Valley 

The massive red moon is a main character in a Halloween wallpaper, surrounded by the twisted branches of a sinister dead tree. The flying bats, distant mountains, and misty valleys deepen the supernatural sense of dread on my screen. 

Download

12. Dark vintage Halloween scene 

Let’s bring back the vintage aesthetic of Halloween! This wallpaper depicts the study of an ancient alchemist filled with weathered spellbooks, a human skull, dried roses, and flickering candles.  

Download

13. Enchanted haunted cottage 

A crooked cottage with glowing green windows hides deep within a misty forest of twisted trees. I feel like entering a secret world of witchcraft and forgotten magic.

Download

14. Gothic roses and bones 

If you love gothic romance with a haunting memento mori aesthetic, download this one. A skeletal hand rises beautifully from deep burgundy roses, dried flowers, and dark foliage. 

Download

15. Lantern path through the mist 

A rain-soaked pathway winds through forest trees, guided by glowing orange lanterns. Thick fog obscures the distant figure and faint moon, creating a suspenseful, immersive night scene. 

Download

16. Moonlit gothic manor  

Another Halloween wallpaper inspired by the gothic theme, showing an eerie manor above a fog-filled mountain. Flying bats, full silver moon, and warm glowing windows blend gothic architecture with supernatural fantasy. 

Download

17. Neon phantom

A ghost takes shape through luminous orange, pink, and violet neon outlines against a pitch-black background. The minimalist design gives a modern, cyberpunk-inspired Halloween look.

Download

18. Jack-O’-Lantern glow up

Transport yourself to the spooky Autumn atmosphere with a lit jack-o’-lantern resting on the steps with autumn leaves.

Download

19. Halloween in comic book style

If you love reading comics, this Halloween wallpaper is a must-have for flexing. It features haunted bookshelves, cute ghosts, jack-o’-lanterns, and creepy crawlies all in a chill orange-and-black aesthetic.

Download

20. Monsters in a full moon night

Under the eerie light of a full moon, mystical creatures awaken to conquer the night. It’s spooky, magical, and totally vibey for your iPhone screen.

Download

21. Halloween celebration in a little town

This Halloween wallpaper gives total spooky small-town vibes that look straight out of a witchy fairytale. It adorns your iPhone with a cute but creepy and cozy Halloween look.

Download

22. Spooky Halloween HD wallpaper

This backdrop is perfect for anyone who wants their iPhone to be a canvas of dark magic. Tap the download button to elevate your Halloween spirit with this spooky wallpaper for iPhone.

Download

23. Cool soulless Bloodborne

It’s time to redefine Halloween chic. Transform your phone with a blend of cool aesthetics and a touch of macabre. Embrace the fusion of sophistication and spookiness this season.

Download

24. Ghost house

While you’re busy making your house spooky like Satan’s, let us help you bring the same feel to your iPhone. Here’s an eerie and fun Halloween haunted house wallpaper for you.

Download

25. Eerie glow

You’re sure to get a fright every time you look at your home screen with this chilling Halloween wallpaper featuring a menacing glowing jack-o’-lantern. The misty forest and ominous hooded man add to the spookiness. It’s the perfect Halloween wallpaper for those looking to embrace the haunted and mysterious vibes of the season.

Download

26. Haunted alley

This atmospheric wallpaper captures the eerie beauty of a cloaked figure wandering down a misty alleyway. It’s perfect to add a touch of mystery to your phone screen. It’s ideal for those who don’t want their Halloween wallpaper to be too creepy.

Download

27. Haunted carnival

Carnivals are fun, but they can also be haunting. Step into a horror scene with this lone ghost figure who’s lurking near a Ferris wheel. Screams of joy have surely turned into screams of terror! The autumn leaves and pumpkins with glowing eyes surely add to the creepiness quotient of this wallpaper.

Download

28. Ghostly guardian

This Halloween wallpaper has an oddly peaceful vibe. It’s as if the ghostly figure is watching over you like a guardian. The glowing jack-o’-lantern and smoky atmosphere add to the mystery and eerie appeal of the scene.

Download

29. Someone’s watching over you

Check out yet another haunting Halloween scene depicting a ghostly figure standing atop a hill, watching over everything. I love the fantastical vibe of this wallpaper that feels as if you’ve stepped into a movie scene. Despite the spookiness, there’s something beautiful about it too.

Download

30. Zombied out animated

Here’s the perfect zombie wallpaper for fans of the living dead. I appreciate that this one is not quite terrifying but instead strikes a balance between the spooky and the playful. Moreover, the unique and stylized art style is reminiscent of manga or anime wallpapers, don’t you think?

Download

31. Blood moon night

Although somewhat spooky, this one is also a great fall wallpaper that captures the raw and untamed beauty of autumn, with its bare trees and cold, silent nights. The large, blood-red moon and bats flying around are sure to bring out the witch or wizard in you.

Download

32. Depth effect masked farmer

The farmer, like no other, can drill hysteria into our bones and veins. This goosebump-raising depth effect wallpaper is a must-have in your Halloween wallpaper series.

Download

33. Aesthetic Halloween

It shouldn’t be all about spooky and scary wallpaper; there should be some aesthetically appealing ones in the mix. Hence, we bring you this masterpiece to light up your iPhone screen.

Download

34. Pumpkin mask

Another pumpkin wallpaper keeps the spooky spirit alive on your iPhone’s screen. It is beautiful, vibrant, and funky! This is among my personal favorite wallpapers.

Download

35. Pumpkin scarecrow

I can’t guarantee how well this pumpkin scarecrow will scare away the prying eyes, but this surely scares away those nosy children from your phone. Don’t believe me; tap the download button and discover it yourself.

Download

All treats and no tricks!

I hope these Halloween wallpapers will add to the fun you have on the spookiest night of the I hope these Halloween wallpapers add a little extra fun and spooky charm to your iPhone on the scariest night of the year.

Let me know in the comments below which wallpaper is your favorite, and don’t forget to share this collection with your friends who love Halloween! Have fun exploring these spooky designs, and enjoy a hauntingly good Halloween!

title.rendered: What is Optimized Battery Charging on iPhone and how do I use it?

content.rendered:
No matter how advanced your iPhone’s processor or camera may be, all those cutting-edge features are only as good as your battery. You’re not alone if you’ve ever reached for a charger sooner than you’d like. Every lithium-ion battery gradually loses capacity, which means less time between charges as the months go by. The good news? Apple has your back with Optimized Battery Charging. This clever iOS feature is built to help slow down battery aging so you can enjoy your iPhone for longer without worrying about constant battery replacements.

In this guide, I’ll explain everything you need to know about Optimized Battery Charging: what it is, how it works, the pros and cons, and how you can set it up to fit your daily routine. Whether you’re a longtime iPhone user or just curious about getting the most out of your device, you’ll find practical tips to help your battery stay healthier and last longer.

What is Optimized Battery Charging?

Think of Optimized Battery Charging as your iPhone’s way of looking out for you and itself. This innovative feature is designed to help your battery last longer by cutting down on your phone’s time sitting at a full 100% charge. Once you turn it on, your iPhone learns your charging habits and determines the best time to finish charging so your battery isn’t under unnecessary stress. After all, letting a lithium-ion battery linger at 100% for too long can speed up its aging process, but with this feature, your device does the heavy lifting to help keep your battery healthy for the long haul.

Note: While this feature is currently designed for iPhones, similar battery optimization features are available on some Android devices and laptops. And if you use an Apple Watch, you can learn how to manage its optimized charging settings in our dedicated Apple Watch guide.

Optimized Battery Charging vs. standard charging

Figuring out the difference between traditional charging and Optimized Battery Charging can help you make the smartest choice for your daily routine and your iPhone’s long-term health.

If you’re the type who always needs your phone to hit 100% as fast as possible, no matter what time it is, standard charging is probably your best bet. It’s quick and predictable, but keep in mind that always rushing to full charge can wear out your battery faster over time. On the other hand, Optimized Battery Charging takes a more thoughtful approach. It might hold off on that last bit of charging sometimes, but it’s doing so to help your battery last longer, so you can keep your phone running strong day after day.

How does Optimized Battery Charging work?

Here’s how the feature operates:

  1. Learns Your Routine: Your iPhone uses on-device machine learning to understand when you typically charge and unplug your device.
  2. Charges Normally Up to 80%: The battery charges at regular speed until it reaches 80%.
  3. Pauses Charging: Once at 80%, charging is paused to avoid prolonged time at full charge.
  4. Completes Charge Before You Need It: Based on your routine, your iPhone finishes charging to 100% just before you usually unplug it.

Example: If you typically plug in your iPhone at 10 PM and unplug it at 7 AM, the device will charge to 80% quickly, then wait. Around 6:30 AM, it will resume charging so you have a full battery when you wake up.

Charge Limit options on iPhone 15 and later

Charge Limit is available on iPhone 15 and later. That covers the iPhone 15, 16, and 17 series, iPhone Air, iPhone 16e and 17e, and the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max. Pick any limit from 80% to 100%, in 5% steps, and your iPhone will generally stop charging at that number. For instance, if you choose 85%, your phone will stay around that level instead of topping up to 100%.

Apple added this option to give you more control over your battery’s health and long-term performance. It’s a good way to slow battery aging even further. Remember, though, that a lower limit means your iPhone might not last quite as long between charges as it would at 100%. Even with a limit set, your iPhone will occasionally charge to 100% to keep its battery readings accurate. It’s all about finding the best balance for your daily routine!

Impact on device performance and battery health

1. Slowing battery aging and preserving capacity

When you let Optimized Battery Charging do its thing, your iPhone spends less time sitting at 100%, and that’s a big win for your iPhone battery’s health. This simple tweak helps slow down the chemical aging process, so you’re less likely to need a battery replacement anytime soon and can enjoy smoother performance from your device for longer.

The numbers can vary, but studies and real-world user experiences show that constantly keeping your battery at 100% can speed up capacity loss, sometimes by as much as 20% over two years! Optimized Battery Charging gives your phone a better shot at holding onto its original capacity so that you can get more life out of every charge.

2. Maintaining peak performance

A healthy battery helps your iPhone maintain peak performance. When battery health declines, iOS may activate performance management features (sometimes called “throttling”) to prevent unexpected shutdowns. Optimized Battery Charging can help your device avoid slowdowns and deliver a more consistent user experience by maintaining battery health.

Users who consistently use this feature often report higher battery health percentages (as seen in Settings > Battery > Battery Health) even after a year or more, compared to those who disable the feature.

3. Compatibility with fast charging

Optimized Battery Charging works seamlessly with fast charging technologies. Your iPhone will still fast-charge up to 80%, then pause as needed to protect battery health. This means you get the convenience of rapid charging without sacrificing long-term performance.

4. Benefits across device generations

The effectiveness of Optimized Battery Charging may be even greater on newer iPhones (iPhone 15 and later) thanks to more advanced battery chemistry and the added option to set custom charging limits. However, even older iPhones benefit from reduced wear and more stable performance over time.

5. Impact on resale and trade-in value

Maintaining higher battery health can directly impact your iPhone’s resale or trade-in value. Devices with a battery health above 85% are more desirable and may fetch higher prices on the secondhand market.

Benefits of Optimized Battery Charging

  1. Reduces Battery Wear: By minimizing the time your iPhone spends at 100%, you slow down the chemical aging process of the battery.
  2. Preserves Battery Capacity: Helps maintain your iPhone’s battery health and performance for a longer period.
  3. Delays Battery Replacement: With less wear, you’re less likely to need a battery replacement as soon.
  4. Convenient and Automatic: Once enabled, the feature works in the background without requiring any extra effort from you.

Why does this matter?

Lithium-ion batteries degrade faster when kept at full charge, especially in warm conditions. Reducing time at 100% helps preserve your battery’s ability to hold a charge.

How to enable, customize, or disable Optimized Battery Charging on iPhone

For iPhone 15 and later:

  1. Open Settings > Battery.
  2. Tap Charging.
  3. Choose a charge limit between 80% and 100%, in 5% steps.
  4. Set the limit to 100%. You can then also turn on Optimized Battery Charging.

For iPhone 14 and earlier:

This covers iPhone 11 through iPhone 14, including both iPhone SE models. Charge Limit starts at iPhone 15, so these models only get the on/off switch.

  1. Open Settings > Battery.
  2. Tap Battery Health & Charging.
  3. Toggle Optimized Battery Charging on or off.

Temporary override:

If you need a full charge sooner than usual, touch and hold the charging notification on your Lock Screen and tap “Charge Now.” That finishes charging sooner instead of waiting for your usual unplug time.

Default setting:

Optimized Battery Charging is on by default when you set up your iPhone.

When should you disable Optimized Battery Charging?

In most cases, leaving Optimized Battery Charging enabled is best. However, you might want to disable it if:

  1. You have irregular charging schedules (charging at different times each day).
  2. You need your phone fully charged earlier than usual (for example, before early travel).
  3. You have an emergency and need a quick full charge.

Tip: If you’re leaving for the airport at 4 AM instead of your usual 7 AM, consider turning off Optimized Battery Charging the night before to ensure a full charge.

General tips for battery health

  1. Avoid Extreme Temperatures: Charging in very hot or cold environments can accelerate battery aging.
  2. Use Approved Chargers: Stick to Apple-certified or high-quality chargers for safe, efficient charging.
  3. Don’t Let Your Battery Drain Completely: Try to recharge before your battery drops to 0% for optimal longevity.

Example: Avoid charging your iPhone in direct sunlight or leaving it plugged in inside a hot car.

Let your iPhone charge the smart way

Optimized Battery Charging is a powerful tool for extending your iPhone’s battery lifespan and maintaining long-term performance. By learning your routine and managing the charging process, it helps you get the most out of your device with minimal effort. For most users, leaving the feature enabled is the best way to keep your iPhone running smoothly for years to come. If your needs change, Apple makes it easy to customize or disable the feature as needed.

FAQs

Does Optimized Battery Charging slow down charging?

No. Your iPhone charges at normal speed up to 80%. The last 20% is intentionally delayed to protect battery health, but you can override this if needed.

Does it work with fast charging?

Yes. Fast charging is supported up to 80%. The optimization only affects the timing of the final portion of the charge.

Is it safe to leave on all the time?

Absolutely. For most users, keeping the feature enabled is the best way to preserve battery health. If your needs change, you can always disable it.

What if my routine is unpredictable?

The feature works best with consistent charging habits. If your schedule varies, you may not see the full benefits, but it won’t harm your device.

mainEntity.name: Does Optimized Battery Charging slow down charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your iPhone charges at normal speed up to 80%. The last 20% is intentionally delayed to protect battery health, but you can override this if needed.

mainEntity.name: Does it work with fast charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Fast charging is supported up to 80%. The optimization only affects the timing of the final portion of the charge.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to leave on all the time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. For most users, keeping the feature enabled is the best way to preserve battery health. If your needs change, you can always disable it.

mainEntity.name: What if my routine is unpredictable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The feature works best with consistent charging habits. If your schedule varies, you may not see the full benefits, but it won't harm your device.

keyPoints.title: What is Optimized Battery Charging?
keyPoints.explanation: It's an iOS feature designed to slow battery aging by reducing the time your iPhone spends at a full 100% charge, learning your habits to finish charging just before you need to use your phone.

keyPoints.title: Optimized Battery Charging vs. Standard Charging
keyPoints.explanation: While standard charging quickly reaches 100% and maintains it, optimized charging pauses at around 80% and finishes just before you typically unplug, helping extend battery lifespan.

keyPoints.title: How Does Optimized Battery Charging Work?
keyPoints.explanation: It learns your routine, charges to 80%, pauses, then resumes charging to 100% just before you usually unplug, ensuring minimal stress on the battery.

keyPoints.title: New Charging Limit Options in iOS 18+
keyPoints.explanation: On iOS 18 and later, especially on iPhone 15/16, you can set specific maximum charge levels (like 80%, 85%, etc.) to further protect battery health.

keyPoints.title: Benefits and Impact on Battery Health
keyPoints.explanation: Optimized charging reduces battery wear, maintains performance, and can even increase resale value by preserving higher battery health over time.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
"The founder of iGeeksBlog, Dhvanesh, is an Apple aficionado, who cannot stand even a slight innuendo about Apple products. He dons the cap of editor-in-chief to make sure that articles match the quality standard before they are published."

About Dhvanesh

Ever since teenage years, gadgets and technology have held a special place in Dhvanesh's heart. This fascination with gadgets and their inner workings fueled a lifelong passion for exploration and troubleshooting. Disassembled electronic items scattered around the house became a familiar sight during his younger years, a testament to this insatiable curiosity.

From SEO Expert to Apple Evangelist

After completing his IT engineering diploma, Dhvanesh's professional journey began with a 4.5-year stint as an SEO executive, honing valuable digital marketing skills. However, the desire to share tech knowledge and connect with a like-minded community proved stronger. In 2012, Dhvanesh embarked on a new adventure, founding iGeeksBlog. This blog became a haven for Apple enthusiasts and tech aficionados seeking insightful and in-depth information about everything Apple.

A Decade of iGeeksBlog: Leading the Apple Charge

In the past 12 years, Dhvanesh has donned multiple hats at iGeeksBlog. As the founder, he has steered the blog’s vision, ensuring it remains a trusted resource for Apple users worldwide. Additionally, he has been serving as the CEO of iGeeks Media Private Limited for the past 4 years, overseeing the company's growth and development.

Beyond Writing: A Multifaceted Approach

Dhvanesh isn't just a prolific writer, having penned hundreds of articles for iGeeksBlog. He has also served as the blog’s Editor-in-Chief and Content Strategist, ensuring a consistent flow of high-quality content that caters to the diverse needs of the Apple user base. The passion for exploration extends beyond the written word. He has created numerous YouTube videos for iGeeksBlog, providing visual demonstrations and engaging directly with the audience.

Staying Connected with the Apple Ecosystem

Dhvanesh's dedication to the Apple community goes a step further. Currently, he also manages the iGeeksBlog+ weekly newsletter, delivering curated Apple news, gadgets, apps, tips and tricks straight to subscribers' inboxes. This unwavering commitment to Apple technology and a genuine desire to empower fellow users make him a valuable asset to the iGeeksBlog team.

content.rendered:
If you have just bought a new Apple Watch, you will likely notice at least one icon, known or unknown, at the top center of its display. Some appear at the top of the screen, others sit inside the Control Center, and many appear during workouts, charging, or system alerts. While you might already be familiar with a few, some icons can be confusing, especially if you are a new Apple Watch user. Therefore, knowing what each symbol means helps you use your watch with confidence and avoid confusion when unexpected events occur.

To help you out, I’ve prepared this definitive guide on the meanings of all the Apple Watch icons and symbols.

Apple Watch status icons

Status icons appear at the top of the Apple Watch screen and give you a quick snapshot of what your watch is doing. They help you understand connectivity, active features, and alerts at a glance before you dive into the detailed meanings.

1. Red dot icon

The Red Dot icon at the top center of your Apple Watch signifies that you have at least one unread notification. To access the notification center, swipe down on your Watch Face or long-press the top edge of the screen, then swipe down if you are within an app.

2. Green Lightning icon

The green lightning or flash icon indicates that your Apple Watch is currently connected to a charger and successfully charging.

3. Red Lightning icon

The Red Lightning icon appears when your Apple Watch’s battery is low. To use it again, you must attach it to its charging cradle. The icon usually appears when your Apple Watch battery falls well below the Low Power mode mark, i.e., 10%.

4. Lock icon

If you notice a Lock icon, it means your Apple Watch is locked with the passcode you set up during initial setup. With wrist detection enabled, the Passcode Lock automatically activates when you remove the Apple Watch from your wrist. Without wrist detection, you’ll need to manually activate the lock from the Control Center.

Simply enter your passcode to unlock your Apple Watch.

5. Water drop icon – Water Lock

The Water Drop or Water Lock appears when you turn on the Water Lock feature in the Apple Watch’s Control Center. When activated, it prevents your Apple Watch from responding to display touches, helping prevent accidental exposure to water.

To deactivate this feature, simply press and hold the Digital Crown until the display says Unlocked. A series of tones then plays to eject the water from the Apple Watch’s speaker.

6. Crescent moon icon

The Crescent Moon appears when you activate Do Not Disturb mode in the Control Center on your Apple Watch or the paired iPhone, if the Share Across Devices setting is on. Once enabled, Do Not Disturb mode silences all calls and other alerts; however, alarms will still ring.

7. Airplane mode

If you see the Airplane icon on your Apple Watch, it means Airplane Mode is active, and all features that require a wireless connection are unavailable.

8. Dual Face Mask icon

The Dual Face Mask represents Theater Mode, which can be enabled or disabled in the Control Center. As the name suggests, the mode is intended for use in places that require zero distractions. The mode restricts your Apple Watch from lighting up whenever a new notification arrives and also disables the Always-on Display if your Apple Watch supports it.


9. Workout icon

This icon appears when your Apple Watch detects that you are in a workout session, or when you manually start a workout in the Workout app. Tapping the icon takes you to the workout-tracking screen in the Workout app, where you can pause and resume the workout.


10. Red cross icon

This status icon indicates that your GPS + Cellular Apple Watch has lost its cellular network connection.

11. iPhone disconnected icon

Represented by an iPhone with a slash over it, the iPhone Disconnected icon indicates that your Apple Watch has lost connection to the paired iPhone. To fix the issue, try bringing your Apple Watch and the paired iPhone close together, disabling Airplane Mode if it is active, or restarting your Apple Watch.


12. iPhone icon

Represented by a green iPhone symbol, this icon appears at the top center of the Control Center whenever the Apple Watch is connected to the paired iPhone.

13. Location indicator icon

This Apple Watch icon signifies an app or the Watch face that requires location services to display information, such as weather details, or is currently using your location.

14. Wi-Fi icon

As you can see, the Wi-Fi icon appears when you connect your Apple Watch to a Wi-Fi network.

15. Wireless activity icon

This icon appears when wireless activity is taking place or when an active process is running.

16. Mic icon

The orange Mic icon appears when an app or service uses the Apple Watch’s mic to listen to external audio. This icon usually pops up when using Siri, recording a voice memo, and more.


17. Now Playing icon

Represented by a striped play button, the Now Playing icon appears when music is playing on the Apple Watch or the paired iPhone. Tapping the icon takes you to the Now Playing screen, where you can control media playback.

18. LTE icon

The LTE icon represents the cellular signal strength on your GPS + Cellular Apple Watch model.

19. Call icon

The green phone icon appears when you are on an active call, on either the Apple Watch or the paired iPhone. Tapping the icon will take you to the calling screen, where you can transfer calls between your iPhone and Apple Watch.

20. Maps icon

Appears when the Apple Watch is being used to provide directions using the Apple Maps app.

21. Navigation icon

It appears when a third-party app is being used to provide directions on the Apple Watch.

22. Car icon

This car appears when you enable Car Focus on the paired iPhone, and the Share Focus Across Devices setting is enabled on it.

24. Yellow circle (Low Power mode) icon

The yellow circle represents the Low Power Mode icon on the Apple Watch, which can be enabled or disabled via the Control Center or the battery settings on the watch.

Apple Watch Control Center specific icons

Status icons appear at the top of the Apple Watch screen and give you a quick snapshot of what your watch is doing. They help you understand connectivity, active features, and alerts at a glance before you dive into the detailed meanings.

25. Cellular icon

Tapping this icon enables or disables cellular connectivity on your Apple Watch with eSIM functionality.

26. Wi-Fi icon

Tapping the Wi-Fi icon toggles Wi-Fi connectivity on your Apple Watch.

27. Ping iPhone

This Control Center icon helps you quickly locate your misplaced paired iPhone. When you tap this icon, the paired iPhone makes a loud beeping sound, which you can hear to locate the iPhone.

28. Battery percentage

This icon shows the current available battery level on your Apple Watch. Moreover, you can enable low power mode on your Apple Watch by tapping this icon and choosing the appropriate option.

29. Silent icon

As the name suggests, tapping this icon puts your Apple Watch in Silent Mode. Once enabled, the bell icon will transform into a crossed bell icon and vice versa.

30. Flashlight

This Control Center button transforms your Apple Watch display into a flashlight. There are three flashlight modes, and you can switch between them by simply swiping across the display.

31. AirPlay icon

The AirPlay icon in the Control Center lets you choose the audio output device for your Apple Watch.

32. Sleep mode icon

As you might expect, the icon indicates that your Apple Watch is in sleep mode. When in this mode, the display will turn off, and when you tap the screen, the sleep timer will appear. You can set the sleep mode time in the Settings app.

33. Work Focus mode icon

Appears when Work Focus is enabled on your Apple Watch or any of your Apple devices. This Focus is aimed at limiting distractions caused by the Apple Watch during your work hours, and the Work Focus icon appears at the top center and in the Control Center when enabled.

34. Personal Focus mode icon

Similar to Work Mode Focus, Personal Focus also appears when enabled on your Apple Watch or other Apple devices. The icon shows up on your Watch Face and in the Control Center.

35. Double A icon

This icon represents the Dynamic Type feature, which lets you choose the text size displayed on your Apple Watch.

36. Bell with wavy lines icon

This icon represents the Siri Announce feature, which reads all incoming notifications aloud when the Apple Watch is connected to supported headphones (AirPods or certain Beats models). However, you must allow Siri to announce notifications in the Apple Watch and paired iPhone settings.

37. Ear-Shaped icon

This icon on the Apple Watch indicates the Hearing Devices options that appear when the headphone volume exceeds a certain threshold, which could affect your hearing.

38. Compass icon

This icon appears when you use the Backtrack feature on the supported Apple Watch models. The feature helps you backtrack your steps and traveled routes in case you are lost.

Signing off…

And that’s it; these were all the icons and symbols you might have noticed on your Apple Watch at one point or another. While most icons are self-explanatory, some, like the Location Indicator or Red Dot, can confuse new Apple Watch users. We tried covering almost all the icons and symbols that may appear on your Apple Watch screen. If we missed anything, please let us know in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Does Optimized Battery Charging slow down charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your iPhone charges at normal speed up to 80%. The last 20% is intentionally delayed to protect battery health, but you can override this if needed.

mainEntity.name: Does it work with fast charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Fast charging is supported up to 80%. The optimization only affects the timing of the final portion of the charge.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to leave on all the time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. For most users, keeping the feature enabled is the best way to preserve battery health. If your needs change, you can always disable it.

mainEntity.name: What if my routine is unpredictable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The feature works best with consistent charging habits. If your schedule varies, you may not see the full benefits, but it won't harm your device.

Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Apple sets October 28 event titled ‘Pro and tell’

content.rendered:
Apple has scheduled a special event for October 28, with the tagline “Pro and tell.” The event starts at 10 a.m. Pacific time in Los Angeles. The report doesn’t name a venue or say whether the event will be streamed.

It is Apple’s second event this month

The October 13 Welcome home event in New York introduced the $299 HomeView smart display, the HomePod mini 2, and a new Apple TV 4K. October 28 is the second event in the month.

The tagline is a play on “show and tell.” The report doesn’t describe the invitation artwork. Apple’s Greg Joswiak posted a teaser, “Can’t wait to pro and tell next week,”.

Can’t wait to pro and tell next week. https://t.co/3wUkxwq35i

— Greg Joswiak (@gregjoz) October 19, 2026

Bloomer’s Gurman points to a touchscreen MacBook Pro and a new iPad mini

Bloomer’s Mark Gurman has reported that the lineup could include a touchscreen MacBook Pro in 14- and 16-inch sizes. Gurman says it would use OLED displays, have a Dynamic Island for the first time, and be “significantly lighter,” with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.

He also reports a revamped iPad mini with an OLED screen, a new speaker system, and a relocated FaceTime camera. Gurman reports that the OLED iPad mini will cost considerably more than today’s $599 model, possibly close to $799. A new iMac and an entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip are also expected to “look like their current versions.”

Most of the rumored lineup is Mac and iPad hardware, and Apple hasn’t confirmed any of these products. For the rest of Apple’s 2026 pipeline, see the upcoming Apple products list.

The touchscreen MacBook Pro date is not settled

Gurman has also said on a podcast that the touchscreen MacBook Pro could launch on Friday, November 6. If that date is right, the product would go on sale about nine days after the October 28 event.

The date, time, location, and tagline are the only details 9to5Mac says Apple has confirmed. Treat the product list as rumor until Apple announces it. If you plan to buy an iPad mini soon, the current $599 model is the price to compare against.

excerpt.rendered: Apple’s “Pro and tell” media event takes place in Los Angeles on October 28 at 10 a.m. Pacific Time. A touchscreen MacBook Pro and an OLED iPad mini remain unconfirmed.

title.rendered: John Ternus is still hands-on with Apple’s design teams

content.rendered:
Apple CEO John Ternus has spent multiple days a week in the studio with the company’s industrial-design and human-interface teams, according to TIME’s reporting. Andrew R. Chow interviewed him for TIME in September, after Ternus took over from Tim Cook on September 1.

TIME published the interview on October 15, ahead of its Best Inventions of 2026 issue, which goes on sale October 26. The full video went up on YouTube on October 20, and 9to5Mac’s writeup of it focused on the design comments. The interview also covers the iPhone Duo, memory shortages, and AI.

Ternus pushed the Duo team to keep working while rivals shipped

Richard Dinh, Apple’s VP of product design, recounts a moment when he asked Ternus whether the team should use a surface material similar to competitors’. Ternus replied, “Look, Rich, you’ll know when it’s the right thing.” According to TIME, that answer gave the team the confidence to push further. Ternus also encouraged the team to invest more time and effort even as rivals reached the market first. Tim Cook, now executive chairman, has said separately that he is not meddling with Ternus.

Hardware and software teams built the Duo together

The iPhone Duo folds to about passport size and opens into a tablet-sized screen. TIME names Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold8 as its closest rival, and early testers say the crease is barely noticeable. TIME cites those testers without independent tests.

TIME reports that hardware and software teams worked together on the Duo’s display engine and on moving the main controls to the right side of the screen. The hinge has more than 100 small interior parts, and the Duo’s surface is matte and light-deflecting.

Design decisions on the Duo have drawn other reports. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple dropped a shorter Apple Pencil for the Duo before production.

Dinh credits Ternus with the collaboration: “John was really at the center of driving the spirit of collaboration across the company.”

An engineer who filed a foldable patent in 2011

Ternus studied mechanical engineering and joined Apple in 2001 as an engineer. In 2011, he and five other engineers filed a patent for foldable devices. That puts his interest in foldables more than a decade before the Duo.

In the full video, Ternus says he has worked hand in hand with industrial designers since he joined Apple, according to 9to5Mac’s writeup. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman had already reported in October 2025 that Ternus was the leading candidate to succeed Cook, nearly a year before the handoff.

On rival foldables, Ternus told TIME, “The other examples in the world felt kind of cheap and crappy.”

He also said Apple doesn’t have to make every part of a product itself. He said the company tries to “constrain ourselves to the stuff that matters most.”

The Duo’s success is far from guaranteed

TIME calls the Duo’s success “far from guaranteed” and says many buyers may balk at its price.

title.rendered: Perplexity Computer can now run fully locally on Mac

content.rendered:
Perplexity says its Computer agent can now run fully locally on Mac. The model, the agent harness, and task execution all run on the device, so personal files and apps can be handled without sending that data to the cloud. The feature is called Local Computer on Mac, and it is available now to Pro, Max, and Enterprise subscribers.

Perplexity’s example is a portfolio analysis that combines private holdings with downloaded market data. It is the kind of task people may not want to send to a cloud service. Local Computer builds on Personal Computer for Mac, which launched in May and gave Computer access to local files and native Mac apps.

Planning, reasoning, and files stay on the Mac

In fully local mode, planning, reasoning, and file processing run on the device. The model is either Qwen 3.6 or PPLX Pro, which Perplexity describes as a post-trained version of Qwen. Code and tool execution run in isolated sandbox environments with controlled access to files and connected apps. Computer works across local files and supported apps, including Notes, Messages, Mail, and Numbers.

Web and connected-app tasks still use the cloud

Tasks that need current information, browser use, or cloud-connected apps need the user’s approval before they go to the cloud. The local orchestrator can also call one of more than 15 frontier models for harder reasoning. Perplexity doesn’t say how often that happens in local mode, so “fully local” describes the on-device default. It is not a promise that no cloud model is involved.

Perplexity also doesn’t say how many credits a local run uses. Users choose where each task runs and how to spend their credits.

Perplexity recommends 36GB of memory

Perplexity says the feature works on “supported Apple silicon Macs” but doesn’t name the models. It gives no minimum memory or macOS version. It does recommend 36GB or more for running Computer locally. Perplexity points to the new Mac mini as an example of a supported machine. The M6 Mac mini tops out at 32GB of unified memory, which falls short of that recommendation. Buyers who want local mode should check the memory configuration before they buy.

Big local models need a lot of memory

Local AI depends on memory. Meta says two M5 Ultra Mac Studios can host its 816-billion-parameter Muse Spark Open model. Moonshot’s Kimi K3 open weights take up roughly 1.56TB, which puts them out of reach for most MacBooks. Perplexity hasn’t said how large its local models are, so the 36GB figure is the best guide for now.

Who gets it and how to set it up

Local Computer on Mac is available to Pro, Max, and Enterprise subscribers. Perplexity doesn’t mention Free users or give a price for the feature. The setup has three steps:

  1. Download and open the latest Perplexity Mac app.
  2. Follow the in-app instructions to download a local model.
  3. Choose the fully local option for a task.

What Perplexity hasn’t said

Perplexity hasn’t given a minimum memory figure, a macOS version, a full list of supported Macs, or any speed or accuracy data. It also doesn’t say how Qwen 3.6 differs from PPLX Pro or how to choose between them. The privacy claims come from Perplexity, and there are no independent tests yet. Until someone runs it on a smaller Mac, plan around 36GB.

mainEntity.name: Does Optimized Battery Charging slow down charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your iPhone charges at normal speed up to 80%. The last 20% is intentionally delayed to protect battery health, but you can override this if needed.

mainEntity.name: Does it work with fast charging?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Fast charging is supported up to 80%. The optimization only affects the timing of the final portion of the charge.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to leave on all the time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. For most users, keeping the feature enabled is the best way to preserve battery health. If your needs change, you can always disable it.

mainEntity.name: What if my routine is unpredictable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The feature works best with consistent charging habits. If your schedule varies, you may not see the full benefits, but it won't harm your device.

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Turbo Soccer Codes on October 28, 2026

Looking for Turbo Soccer codes? Well, you’ve come to the right place! In this Roblox game, you’ll be driving cars around the pitch to score goals and outplay your opponents. However, you’ll need the best fields, cards, and cars if you want to wreck the competition. Luckily, Turbo Soccer codes can help you unlock free rewards! With that said, let’s take a look at all the codes you should redeem right now.

All working Turbo Soccer codes

  • TY100KLIKES: 5 Epic Packs (NEW)
  • PUMPKIN: 2 Epic Packs (NEW)
  • HALLOWEEN: 2 Epic Packs (NEW)

As of now, this is the only active Turbo Soccer code available. Make sure to redeem it as soon as possible, as codes can expire without warning, leaving you unable to claim their rewards.

Expired Turbo Soccer codes

85KLIKES, BONUS10, PACK, SORRY

How to Redeem Turbo Soccer codes in Roblox

Knowing the active codes isn’t enough, gamers! You also need to know how to redeem them and claim your free rewards. Thankfully, the process only takes a few minutes. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to redeem Turbo Soccer codes:

  1. Fire up Turbo Soccer on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Click on the Options button and find Codes.
  4. Paste a working code and hit Redeem to claim your reward.
  5. Once you’ve redeemed the rewards, they should be added to your inventory automatically.

Why aren’t My Turbo Soccer codes working?

If your Turbo Soccer codes aren’t working, double-check that you’ve entered them exactly as listed above. Keep in mind that these codes are case-sensitive, so make sure there are no extra spaces before or after them. You can simply copy and paste the codes directly from our list. If a code still doesn’t work, it might’ve expired, or you may have already redeemed its rewards.

How to get more Turbo Soccer codes?

The developers don’t follow a fixed schedule for releasing new Turbo Soccer codes. Most codes are released to celebrate major game updates, seasonal events, or community milestones.

To stay updated, you can:

  • Join the official Discord server: Visit the Turbo Soccer Discord server to find announcements and newly released codes.
  • Follow the Roblox game page: Check the game’s official Roblox page for updates, announcements, and potential code releases.
  • Bookmark this page: We’ll update this guide whenever new Turbo Soccer codes become available, so you can easily find the latest rewards in one place.

If you’re looking for more Roblox freebies, check out our latest Shigaku codes, Smash a Piggy codes, and our complete Roblox Game Codes hub.

FAQs

What rewards can you get from Turbo Soccer codes?

Turbo Soccer codes can reward players with free bonuses and packs that can be used to customise rides and unlock cosmetic rides.

How do you customize your car in Turbo Soccer?

Your vehicle can be customised through the Garage menu in Turbo Soccer. You will be able to change a car’s paint colour, toppers, boost effects, trails, and much more.

How do you get Coins in Turbo Soccer?

Coins can be earned in Turbo Soccer by participating in matches and progressing through the game.

Expired Shigaku codes

How to redeem Shigaku codes in Roblox

Knowing the active codes isn’t enough, gamers! You also need to know how to redeem them and claim your free rewards. Thankfully, the process only takes a few minutes. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to redeem Shigaku codes:

  1. Fire up Shigaku on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Click on the Menu button and then open Settings.
  4. Find the Codes box.
  5. Paste a working code and hit Redeem to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed the rewards, they should be added to your inventory automatically.

Why aren’t my Shigaku codes working?

If your Shigaku codes aren’t working, double-check that you’ve entered them exactly as listed above. Keep in mind that these codes are case-sensitive, so make sure there are no extra spaces before or after them. You can simply copy and paste the codes directly from our list. If a code still doesn’t work, it might’ve expired, or you may have already redeemed its rewards.

How to get more Shigaku codes

The developers don’t follow a fixed schedule for releasing new Shigaku codes. Most codes are released to celebrate major game updates, seasonal events, or community milestones.

To stay updated, you can:

  • Join the official Discord server: Visit the Shigaku Discord server to find announcements and newly released codes.

  • Bookmark this page: We’ll update this guide whenever new Shigaku codes become available, so you can easily find the latest rewards in one place.

If you’re looking for more Roblox freebies, check out our latest Kaiju Alpha codes, Smash a Piggy codes, Turbo Soccer codes and our complete Roblox Game Codes hub.

FAQs

What rewards can you get from Shigaku codes?

Shigaku codes are used to obtain free Rerolls, which allow you to change your character’s appearance, fighting abilities, surname and more. Some codes can also provide Cash.

Do Shigaku codes expire?

Shigaku codes expire after a certain date. Codes are released to celebrate major milestones or updates, so their availability is limited.

Some of the best fighting styles in Shigaku are Karate and boxing. These styles are all about being aggressive and applying forward pressure on your enemies.

title.rendered: How to unlock and find Finger Guns in Fortnite

content.rendered:
Finger Guns are back in Fortnite, thanks to their surprise addition in the October 15 update, the final major content drop for the Fortnite Override season. This dual-wielded weapon originally debuted in the game on April Fools’ Day 2026 to a rather positively stirring reception, making their comeback a notable highlight.

In itself, Finger Guns are not really ‘guns’ that you can equip. Upon selecting the weapon, the game just makes your character gesture his fingers in roughly the form of a gun that fires bullets with a humorous “Pew! Pew!” sound, as the same thing also appears on the screen like comic book text.

In this guide, you can learn how to unlock and then find Finger Guns in Fortnite. Additionally, you can also check out other items in the loot hack pool below.

How to unlock Finger Guns in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Override tab.
  2. Under Loot Hack, highlight the Finger Guns item.
  3. Lastly, press and hold the Unlock/Upgrade button to add Finger Guns to your loot pool.

How to find Finger Guns in Fortnite

Once you have unlocked the Finger Guns loot item, you can find it by opening chests. To boost your chances of finding it via this method, it is recommended to use any of the Loot Hacker sprites available in the game.

In addition, as you gather enough Sprite Dust through sprite extractions or Fortnite Lobby Hacks, make sure to keep upgrading Finger Guns from the aforementioned Loot Hack tab. Doing so will further increase the likelihood of getting this weapon from chests, with almost every successive upgrade—two of these levels unlock higher rarity for Finger Guns instead of a better spawn rate.

Given below is how the Finger Guns spawn rate changes at each of its five upgrade levels.

  • Upgrade 1: 5% drop rate when opening a chest
  • Upgrade 2: Epic rarity as the highest possible tier
  • Upgrade 3: 8% drop rate when opening a chest
  • Upgrade 4: 10% drop rate when opening a chest
  • Upgrade 5: Legendary rarity as the highest possible tier

Other Loot Hacks in Fortnite Override right now

Similar to how Finger Guns is a part of the new lineup of loot hacks in Fortnite Override, there are other items as well on the same list. These range from sniper rifles to health consumables and are listed below.

1. All sprite variants

2. Gatekeeper Shotgun

3. Hunting Rifle

4. Thorne’s Vampiric Blade

5. Slap Splash

Final thoughts

While they may seem hilarious on the surface, Finger Guns are no joke when it comes to dealing damage and a reasonable rate of fire. Hence, it would be a good decision if this item is one of the first things that you unlock and max out using Sprite Dust. It’s also worth remembering that even if you have already unlocked or upgraded an item, you can always undo that decision and re-allocate the spent Sprite Dust per your whim.

Finger Guns, in the current Loot Hack pool of Fortnite, are perhaps only second to the Thorne’s Vampiric Blade, which is a highly powerful melee weapon. So, according to your playstyle, you should upgrade one or the other as a priority.

It will be interesting to see which of these two emerges as the more popular item in the Fortnite community, as more players get accustomed to them. In any case, once you have both items maxed out, you will more or less be well-prepared for both close-range and medium-range face-offs—that’s a given.

title.rendered: All Droid Fusion recipes in Fortnite Star Wars Droid Tycoon

content.rendered:
Since its release in May, as part of a major collab between Fortnite and Star Wars, the Star Wars Droid Tycoon map has received significantly positive reception from fans and continues to attract a sizable audience compared to other third-party Fortnite maps. Then, in August, its developer FOAD rolled out a new update that threw droid fusion into the mix, which essentially introduced new droids for players to add to their collection.

Since then, players have been trying different combos and learning about which ‘recipe’ works for generating which kind of droid. While it may seem like a mostly hit-and-trial process, there are actually fixed recipes out in the community that provide a specific droid when put into action. All such fusion recipes are shared later in this article.

How Droid Fusion works in Star Wars Droid Tycoon

The fusion feature in Star Wars Droid Tycoon involves combining three different droids to either obtain a variant of a higher rarity or a new droid itself. It goes without saying that the droids used to construct a new one will be permanently lost.

This gameplay mechanic is only accessible to players who have reached Rebirth 3 on the progression chart, which is quite convenient to reach. This Rebirth level requires a player to have 975K credits along with base A-LT, base B-U4D, and gold R9 droids. Eligible players can take part in droid fusion by visiting the Fusion Lab, which is sandwiched between the landing zone of your base and the workshop location.

All Droid Fusion recipes in Star Wars Droid Tycoon

The list below encompasses all the droids you can create via droid fusion in Star Wars Droid Tycoon. From droids of the Rare tier to those of the Mythic tier, you will find the respective recipe to construct each of them.

Rare Droids

Epic Droids

Legendary Droids

Mythic Droids

Wrapping up

In its heyday, Star Wars Droid Tycoon used to pull tens of thousands of concurrent Fortnite players daily. While that has now dropped to around 20K peak concurrent players in a day, the game is still on the higher side on the list of Fortnite UEFN maps that get the most user engagement.

In fact, the game’s popularity has enabled FOAD to ship regular updates so far, including one from last month that optimized the experience for mobile users. This should naturally rope in more players and give some boost to the footfall that this Fortnite map gets. However, only time will tell if the newly gained audience stays over the long term.

title.rendered: What is Apple Watch for Your Kids and how does it work?

content.rendered:
Apple Watch for Your Kids, formerly known as Family Setup, lets a parent set up a cellular Apple Watch for a child or older family member who doesn’t have an iPhone. The parent manages the watch from their own iPhone. Here’s what it does, what you need now, and how to set it up.

What is Apple Watch For Your Kids?

With Apple Watch for Kids, a parent or guardian can set up Apple Watch with cellular for kids or older people who do not have their own iPhones. The parent can use their iPhone to manage the kids’ Apple Watch.

Once set up, kids can use the Apple Watch freely without needing an iPhone. They can go to school, sports practice, a picnic, and anywhere without any concern, and the parent can know their whereabouts.

What can kids do with Apple Watch For Your Kids?

  • Make and receive FaceTime audio calls and standard phone calls.
  • Send and receive messages and emails.
  • Connect Apple Watch to AirPods or any Bluetooth earphones & speaker and use Apple Music.
  • Use Apple Cash Family (US only): This lets parents load money to kids’ Apple Watch, which they can utilize wherever Apple Pay is accepted.
  • Have kid-oriented personalized Activity goals/Activity rings.
  • Use custom Memoji right from the Apple Watch using its Memoji app.
  • Use safety and everyday features without needing an iPhone, like Emergency SOS, Maps, Siri, Alarms, and the App Store.

What family members can do with their Apple Watch?

Receive emergency SOS notifications

If the parents or guardians are set as emergency contacts (which they should be), they’ll be notified in emergencies. Kids can look at their Medical ID for relevant information. Plus, the guardian can also view the health and activity of their family members using the iPhone’s Health app.

Set Schooltime Schedule

During Schooltime, the kid’s Apple Watch shows a yellow circle on the watch face. This helps the teachers in the classroom (or parent tutoring at home) easily recognize the apps whose access is restricted, plus Do Not Disturb can be enabled on the kid’s Apple Watch.

Apple Cash Family

This lets the parents load money to the kid’s watch via Apple Pay and choose to receive notifications when they spend it. The parent can even see the kid’s purchases in the Wallet app on the iPhone. This is a fine example of training the young generation for the coming cashless future!

Other Features

  • Parents can allow certain contacts, and kids will be able to communicate only with these approved persons.
  • Set content restrictions and Ask to Buy: This lets the parents manage which category of apps are available for download on the kid’s Apple Watch. Ask to Buy sends the parent an approval notification when the kid tries to purchase an app or make an in-app purchase.
  • Share the kid’s location through Find My, so you can see where they are on your iPhone. Parents can also get location notifications, such as when the kid reaches school or basketball practice.

How to set up an Apple Watch for a family member

Before You Begin:

  • Make sure the iPhone runs iOS 27, and the watch supports watchOS 27. The model list is in the compatibility section below.
  • Turn ON Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on the iPhone.
  • Erase the Apple Watch if it isn’t new.
  • Make sure you have an Apple Account for yourself (the parent or guardian). The child gets their own phone number and Apple Account with the watch.
  • Family Sharing: Setup creates a group if you don’t have one. The child must be in your Family Sharing group with a Child Account.
  1. Have your child put on the Apple Watch and press and hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears.
  2. Bring the watch near the iPhone. Wait for a moment, and you should see “Use your iPhone to set up this Apple Watch” on the iPhone screen. Tap on Continue. After this, tap on Set Up for a Family Member → Continue. If you don’t see this, open the Watch app on iPhone, go to My Watch → All Watches, and tap Add Watch.
  3. Point the iPhone over the animation on the Apple Watch screen. You will see a message that says the Apple Watch is successfully paired.
  4. Agree to the terms and conditions (if you do), select text size, and set a passcode for the Apple Watch.
  5. Select a family member from the screen or tap on Add New Family Member. Now, enter the kid’s (or the family member’s) Apple Account and password, then proceed. It is a good idea to tap on Turn on Ask to Buy. (more about it above)
  6. If your carrier supports Apple Watch for Your Kids, you can add the watch to your plan during this step. If it doesn’t, or you want a different carrier, tap Not Now and contact a supported carrier to set up the plan. Then set up Wi-Fi and turn on other options like location, Siri, Apple Cash Family, Health data, etc. You can also set up Schooltime and shared contacts. Once you are done, tap on OK. Now, the kid can start using the Apple Watch.

Family Setup compatible Apple Watch and iPhone

Family Setup is available on cellular models of Apple Watch Series 4 and later running watchOS 7. You can pair the watch with iPhone 6s and later running iOS 14.

Note: Apple says that ‘a cellular plan isn’t required to set up an Apple Watch for a family member, but is necessary for some features.’

Compatible Apple Watch and iPhone models

Apple recommends the Apple Watch SE 3 with GPS + Cellular. The watch has to be a cellular model that runs watchOS 27: Series 9 or later, SE 3, or Ultra 2 or later. Older models, including Series 8 and SE (2nd generation), can’t run watchOS 27, so check the model before you reuse an old watch.

The iPhone needs iOS 27 for watchOS 27. Apple’s requirement is an iPhone 11 or later, or an iPhone SE (2nd generation) or later.

Note: You don’t need a cellular plan to finish setup. The watch does need an active plan to connect to a cellular network, though, and some features depend on it.

Regions and carriers that support Family Setup

At launch, 18 carriers in 12 countries and regions support Family Setup. This is a carrier support-oriented feature (separate phone number, data plan, etc.) Thus, in the coming months, it will expand to other regions and carriers as well. For more information, like availability and pricing, contact your carrier.

Views on Family Setup

What are your thoughts on Apple Watch Family Setup? Is this something you are excited about? Are you planning to use it in your family? Please let us know in the comments down below.

In my opinion, this is a great feature. Now, you can give the kid an affordable Apple Watch SE or your old Series 5, and they get the power to stay safely connected to people that matter.

One thing that I feel strange is that Apple discontinued Series 4 and 5 but kept Series 3. And unfortunately, Family Setup requires Series 4 and above. So, that’s a bummer!

Now, instead of giving a smartphone, it is convenient to have a powerful tiny computer on the child’s wrist (that they won’t misplace) when at baseball practice or a friend’s house. Likewise, it lets you keep track of older people more conveniently.

Overall, I think it’s a smart move to get Apple Watch to more people in an affordable way!

title.rendered: WhatsApp is building an in-app browser for links in iPhone chats

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is developing an in-app browser for iPhone that would open any link shared in a chat inside the app, WABetaInfo reported on October 19. The site found the feature in WhatsApp beta for iOS 26.41.10.72 on TestFlight. It is not yet available to beta testers, and WhatsApp has not announced it.

WABetaInfo says WhatsApp will make the browser available to some beta testers in a future update. No public release date has been given.

Links would open without leaving the conversation

Tapping a link in a chat would load the page inside the conversation screen instead of switching to Safari or another browser. According to WABetaInfo, the browser runs in a session separate from the chat. The three-dot menu would still open the page in your default browser.

WABetaInfo describes this as an expansion of an earlier feature that covered only certain business links. That version appeared in iOS beta 25.14.10.72 in May 2025, and WABetaInfo says it reached the Android beta first. Sites had to use HTTPS and meet other technical requirements, and WhatsApp applied its own business criteria, so some businesses were left out. The October 19 report does not say whether that version has since reached everyone.

A setting would turn it on and clear its data

Users would turn the browser on from an "In-app browser" option in WhatsApp’s settings. A bottom sheet would explain the feature the first time it is enabled. A Browser settings section would let people clear cookies and cache from sites they opened in WhatsApp, and they could restore the default browser at any time.

The privacy claims come from WABetaInfo

WABetaInfo says WhatsApp cannot see the links shared in a conversation, and that neither WhatsApp nor Apple can see which links users open. It also says browsing data is stored on the device, as it is in Safari. WhatsApp has not confirmed any of it.

It follows a run of WhatsApp changes to chats and links

WhatsApp has been changing the iPhone chat screen this month. A Liquid Glass menu in the chat header began rolling out on October 9, and its shortcuts include media, links, and docs. On October 14, WhatsApp launched guest calling, where a host shares a call link and people without an account join from a computer browser.

WhatsApp has set no timeline for the browser

The report covers WhatsApp for iOS and does not mention Android. The gap between a build and a rollout can be short. The Liquid Glass progress bar for the video player was in development in an August beta and not available to testers, and WABetaInfo reported it rolling out on October 6, less than two months later. WhatsApp has given no schedule for the browser.

The report does not describe any warning for suspicious links. WhatsApp’s scam tools so far, such as the alerts it has tested when you message someone who is not in your contacts, apply to contacts and groups. If the browser opens every link in a chat, the first thing to check when it ships is whether it warns you about risky pages.

title.rendered: Apple reportedly plans a larger HomeView with a 9-inch screen on a robotic arm

content.rendered:
Apple is planning a higher-end HomeView with a 9-inch screen that swivels a full 360 degrees on a robotic arm, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. He wrote in his October 18 Power On newsletter that he expects the device to launch in 2027 or 2028. Apple has not announced it, and no name or price has been reported.

The current HomeView is the one Apple announced on October 13. It has a 7-inch screen on a domed speaker base, and a hinge tilts the display up or down. It costs $299 and ships November 13.

The reported model adds a bigger screen and an arm that turns

The model Gurman describes would put a 9-inch display on a robotic arm that can turn it through a full circle. The current HomeView’s screen only tilts.

iClarified and The Apple Post, both summarizing the newsletter, add two details. The device carries the internal codename J595, and it would use voice recognition to work out who is speaking and turn the screen toward that person.

Both describe the device as an addition to the lineup that sits above the $299 model. The Apple Post compares the turning screen to Center Stage, which the current HomeView uses in FaceTime calls to keep participants framed. The reports do not mention the new model’s chip or camera.

Gurman expects 2027 or 2028 and has only floated names

The launch window covers two years. Gurman suggested the names HomeView Max, HomeView Ultra, and HomeView 360, and the names are speculative. Apple has not used any of the three.

No price has been reported. iClarified’s summary says Gurman suspects Apple kept the current HomeView at $299 by building units early, before this year’s memory shortage raised component costs. A bigger screen, a motor, and a place above the $299 model point to a higher price.

Pre-orders for the 7-inch model are open now, and Apple’s October 13 announcement does not mention a larger one.

Bloomberg has tracked a robotic-arm device since 2024

Gurman reported in August 2024 that Apple was developing a tabletop device that uses a thin robotic arm to move a large screen. Actuators would tilt the display up and down and spin it 360 degrees. It was described as a smart home command center, a video-calling machine, and a remote-controlled home security tool.

In August 2025, Bloomberg reported that the tabletop robot was targeted for 2027. That report described a display of about 7 inches on a motorized arm that could extend about six inches from its base. It placed a stationary smart home hub ahead of the robot, in 2026, and that hub arrived this month as HomeView.

Set against those reports, the new one raises the screen from about 7 inches to 9 and adds 2028 as a possible launch year.

The first hub slipped more than a year, so dates can move

HomeView was originally meant to launch in March 2025, alongside Siri’s AI overhaul. Gurman reported that Siri’s problems pushed the hub to 2026. Apple announced it on October 13 with Siri AI still in beta. The larger model is built around voice recognition, so its date could depend on Siri as well.

Early size reports have moved before

Bloomberg’s September 30 report on the display that became HomeView put its screen at 6 inches. Apple announced a 7-inch display on October 13. A size reported this far ahead of a launch is a plan that can still change, and Apple has not confirmed the 9-inch figure or anything else in the report.

title.rendered: Gurman says Apple made a “major mistake” with iPhone Duo pre-orders

content.rendered:
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says Apple made a "major mistake" by opening iPhone Duo pre-orders on Friday, October 16, despite knowing manufacturing problems would leave supply severely constrained. He made the claim in his Power On newsletter on October 18.

Pre-orders for Apple’s first foldable iPhone, which starts at $1,999, opened at 5 a.m. Pacific. Within 30 minutes, Apple’s U.S. online store showed January 25 delivery for every configuration. Apple has not publicly addressed Gurman’s claim. It has said pre-order demand was "nothing short of extraordinary."

Gurman says Apple put an early launch ahead of inventory

Gurman writes that Apple could have waited for more stock before taking orders. He says it prioritized having the phone out early in its fiscal first quarter, which covers the holiday period, over meeting demand. He expects the shortage to disappoint early adopters.

The claim about Apple’s reasons is Gurman’s reading. Apple has not said how many phones it had when pre-orders opened or whether it expected demand to outrun supply.

The risk was public beforehand. Bloomberg had reported that Apple expected limited availability at launch and had worried that manufacturing constraints could push some sales into November. Nikkei Asia reported in early September that production was only a few hundred units a day in late August. With those warnings out for weeks, delivery dates slipping within minutes was predictable.

Pre-orders opened in 70-plus countries at once

According to Gurman, Apple originally planned to launch the iPhone Duo only in the U.S. and China, with other countries following later. It opened pre-orders in more than 70 countries and regions instead, which spreads the available stock across far more markets.

Apple’s September announcement already listed those markets for the October 23 launch, with 28 more countries and regions on October 30. The wide rollout was public before pre-orders began.

Delivery dates passed Christmas within half an hour

Buyers who ordered at about 5 a.m. Pacific were promised delivery on October 23, launch day. By 5:30 a.m., Apple’s U.S. store listed January 25 for Star White and Night Sky in 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB. 9to5Mac reported that estimates in some countries, including Brazil, moved into early February.

MacRumors notes that Apple tends to underpromise, so some customers may receive their phones a little before the listed date. Apple’s online store can no longer deliver before Christmas.

Anyone who needs a foldable before then has one already on sale: Google’s Pixel 11 Pro Fold starts at $1,899 for 256GB.

Walk-in stock on October 23 looks unlikely

MacRumors reported on October 17 that Apple Store employees were told there will likely be no iPhone Duo stock for walk-in customers on launch day. Staff were told to discourage people without pre-orders from coming in. MacRumors says it is unclear how firm the guidance is or whether it applies to every store. Apple has not said publicly whether any stores will have walk-in stock.

Apple briefly offered store pickup during pre-orders, then turned it off. Its online store now says to check back on Saturday, October 24, for pickup availability. That message does not promise stock on that day.

Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile took pre-orders too, and Best Buy sells the phone, so their delivery dates are separate from Apple’s online store. For pickup on October 24, check Apple’s website or the Apple Store app.

title.rendered: HomePod mini 2 vs Echo Studio: Which speaker should you buy?

content.rendered:
Most of this decision comes down to two things: which phone you use, and how much speaker you want. The HomePod mini 2 is the small option. It costs $149, weighs 335 g, and sits on a shelf without taking over. The Echo Studio (2025) is the big one. It costs $219.99, weighs 1.63 kg, and doubles as a smart home hub with Zigbee, Thread, and Matter built in.

If you’re on an iPhone and want something small, the HomePod mini 2 is the one I’d look at first. If you’re on Android, or you want bigger sound and a hub that does more, the Echo Studio is the better fit.

HomePod mini 2 vs Echo Studio at a glance

Start with your phone: iPhone vs Android

The HomePod mini 2 needs an iPhone or iPad for setup, and Apple lists a compatible device as a system requirement. The Echo Studio, on the other hand, works with both Android and iPhone, making it a more flexible choice if your household uses different phone platforms. If you’re on Android and don’t have access to an iPhone or iPad, the HomePod mini 2 isn’t the right option for you.

But compatibility goes beyond initial setup. With the HomePod mini 2, you’ll get the best experience if you’re already invested in Apple’s ecosystem, especially if you use Apple Music, the Home app, and other Apple devices. You can use Siri to control supported smart home accessories, manage music playback, and access other Apple services.

The Echo Studio is a better fit for households that prefer Alexa, use Android phones, or rely on Alexa-compatible smart home devices. You can manage Alexa settings and connected devices through the Alexa app, without needing to own an iPhone.

My take: If you already use an iPhone and other Apple devices, the HomePod mini 2 makes more sense. But if you want a smart speaker that fits into an Android household just as easily, the Echo Studio is the more practical choice. Your existing phone and smart home setup should be the first things you consider before deciding between these two speakers.

Size and sound

The Echo Studio is nearly five times heavier than the HomePod mini 2. Amazon’s 2025 model is about 40% smaller than the original Echo Studio, but it’s still a big speaker that needs a shelf of its own.

Reviews split on bass. Tom’s Guide says the Echo Studio makes a lot of bass for its size. Expert Reviews says the bass isn’t as strong as the original Echo Studio’s, but it calls the speaker better than anything else in Amazon’s range for filling a room, and it praises the wide sound with Dolby Atmos music from Amazon Music.

Reviews of the HomePod mini 2 were hard to find at the time of writing, and Apple doesn’t publish driver size or power. Wait for reviews before you judge its sound against the Echo.

Which is the better smart home hub?

The Echo Studio connects Zigbee devices without a separate bridge, and it handles Thread and Matter too. It also has presence detection built in.

The HomePod mini 2 covers Thread networking for HomeKit and Matter accessories, and it adds temperature and humidity sensors. Apple’s spec page doesn’t list Zigbee, so Zigbee devices need another hub.

The HomePod mini 2’s Sound Recognition listens for smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. Apple warns that detection may not be reliable, so keep your real alarms in place.

Alexa+ vs Siri AI: Which assistant is ready now?

Alexa+ is live on the Echo Studio today. Amazon says it’s included at no extra cost with Prime. Without Prime, full access costs $19.99 a month, and a limited text chat is free on Alexa.com and in the Alexa app.

Siri AI is still coming to the HomePod mini 2. Apple says it arrives as a free software update, but it hasn’t given a date. The homeowner needs an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad with Siri AI turned on, and it isn’t available in the EU on iOS or iPadOS at first. Don’t buy the HomePod mini 2 for Siri AI alone.

Price: is the Echo Studio worth $70 more?

The Echo Studio costs about $70 more than the HomePod mini 2. If sound and size matter more than price, Apple’s closer match is the full-size HomePod, which went from $299 to $349 in June 2026.

Which one should you buy?

  • HomePod mini 2: iPhone and iPad owners who want a small speaker, Thread support, and humidity sensing for $149. Skip it if you run Zigbee devices or use Android.
  • Echo Studio (2025): Android owners, Zigbee smart homes, and anyone who wants Dolby Atmos and presence detection. Make sure the listing says 2025, since the original 2019 Echo Studio is a bigger, cylindrical speaker.

Start with your phone, then think about how much room you have. That usually settles it.
