title.rendered: How to manage downloads in Safari on iPhone or iPad

content.rendered:
Safari, Apple’s native browser, offers a wide range of features. Like other browsers, it also lets you download files (PDFs, images, and others) from the web with ease. While downloading with Safari is typically easy, many still don’t know how to manage these Safari downloads on iPhone and iPad.

But your daunting thought of how to manage Safari downloads on iPhone and iPad stops here. I’ll discuss everything you should know about downloading files on Safari in this piece. Let’s begin!

Understanding Safari’s download manager

Apple added the download manager in Safari with the release of iOS 13. Thanks to it, you can easily download files from the web and manage them directly from within the Safari browser on your iPhone and iPad.

Here are some key features of Safari’s download manager:

  • Download tracking
  • Download list
  • Pause, resume, or cancel downloads
  • File management
  • Automatic deletion of the download list
  • Compatibility with cloud services like iCloud Drive and Dropbox

Where are Safari downloads stored on an iPhone or iPad?

Your download items on Safari are stored in either iCloud Drive or on your iPhone’s local storage. However, you can choose the preferred location to store them through the Settings app. I’ll cover the steps to do that in a subsequent section of the piece.

Why should you manage downloads in Safari?

Here are some reasons why you should manage your downloads in Safari on your iPhone or iPad:

  • Avoid clutter: If you download a lot of files in Safari, the folder where you save all your downloads can be the most cluttered location in the Files app. But if you regularly manage your downloads by choosing different download locations for some file types, you can better organize your downloads and make them easy to find.
  • Save storage space: Downloads often accumulate a lot of storage space on your devices, and a lot of the time they are those you no longer need. Hence, it’s important to manage them. That way, you can get rid of unnecessary files and free up some storage.
  • Maintain privacy: If you share your iPhone or iPad with someone, managing your downloads is a great way to keep the personal files you’ve downloaded online properly saved or deleted from prying eyes. With the help of features like auto-deletion, you can ensure no one knows the files you’ve downloaded on your device over time.
  • Keep your device secure: You might unintentionally download harmful files online, but by regularly keeping a tab on your downloads, you can easily notice such files and quickly remove them to protect your device from threats.

How to manage Safari download items on iPhone or iPad

Now that you’re familiar with the Safari download manager, let’s see how you can use it to manage your downloads effectively.

Access and view downloads in Safari

You can access and view your downloaded files in both Safari and the Files app. Here’s what the process looks like on each of them.

On Safari:

  1. Tap the Downloads button next to the search field.
  2. Tap Downloads to see your downloaded files.
  3. Tap the downloaded file to open it. Or tap the search icon next to it to open its location in the Files app.

Note: This works if you’ve just downloaded a file via Safari and the download list has not been cleared.

In the Files app:

  1. Launch the Files app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Select Browse, tap iCloud Drive, then open the Downloads folder. If you changed the download location, open that folder instead.

Pause, resume, and cancel downloads in Safari

You can also pause, resume, and cancel downloads in Safari. Here’s how:

  1. In Safari, tap the arrow inscribed in a circle in the left corner of the address bar and select Downloads.
  2. Tap the X icon on your ongoing download to pause it.
  3. To resume the download, tap the curved arrow on the download.
  4. While there’s no dedicated button to cancel a download, if you want to do it anyway, swipe left on an ongoing download and select Delete.

Change the download location in Safari on an iPhone or iPad

Safari lets you store your downloads in iCloud or local storage by default. But you can choose any other location, too. Here’s how:

  1. Head to the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Navigate to Apps, then tap it and select Safari from the app list.
  3. Tap Downloads under General.
  4. On the resulting page, choose where you wan to save your downloads from the available options: iCloud Drive, On My iPhone/iPad, or Other.

Note: Choosing iCloud Drive means your downloads will sync across all devices connected to iCloud.

Delete Safari downloads on an iPhone

You can delete Safari downloads on your iPhone and iPad by going to the location it’s saved in the Files app and deleting the file there. Here are the steps to do that:

  1. Open the Files app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Go to the location where your Safari downloads are saved.
  3. Tap the three-dot menu in the top-right corner.
  4. Next, tap Select, then select the downloaded files you want to delete and tap the trash icon at the bottom.

If you want to delete download items in Safari, you can do that, too.

Delete an individual download:

  1. Go to Downloads in Safari as described earlier.
  2. Swipe left on the downloaded file you want to delete.
  3. Finally, tap the Delete button.

Delete all downloads:

  1. Go to the Downloads page on Safari.
  2. Tap Clear in the top-right corner of the Downloads page.

Auto-delete downloads on an iPhone or iPad

Safari has an auto-delete feature that clears downloaded items after a while. Here’s how to enable it:

  1. Launch the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Scroll down and select Apps.
  3. Select Safari, then tap Downloads under General.
  4. On the resulting page, tap Remove Download List Items.
  5. Here, you’ll be able to choose to remove Safari downloads After One day, Upon Successful Download, or manually. Select either of the first two options to automatically delete your Safari download list items.

Note: This feature only deletes the downloaded items from your Safari downloads manager and not the actual files on your iPhone or iPad.

How to troubleshoot an issue with your Safari downloads on an iPhone and iPad

It’s possible that your Safari downloads are getting stuck or you’re having issues with downloading files via the Safari app on your iPhone or iPad. Here are some ways to fix such issues:

  • Ensure you have a stable internet connection.
  • Restart Safari.
  • Clear Safari cache: This can help fix download issues in the Safari browser. Find more details on how you can clear Safari cache on iPhone and iPad.
  • Ensure you have enough storage space on your iPhone or iPad.
  • Change the download location.
  • Update iOS (and the Safari app) on your iPhone or iPad.

Signing off…

Having discussed how you can manage Safari downloads on iPhone and iPad, I believe you can now easily organize, locate, and delete your Safari downloads.

Also, the troubleshooting tips discussed will be helpful in case you face issues with downloading files on Safari. Let us know if you have any other questions in the comments section.

FAQs

Can I transfer downloads from an iPhone to an iPad?

You can send your downloads from an iPhone to an iPad using AirDrop. However, if you choose to save your downloads on your iCloud Drive, it’ll sync across all devices connected to your iCloud, including your iPad, if it’s connected to iCloud.

Does Safari on iPhone download files in the background?

Yes, Safari on iPhone downloads files in the background.

Do Safari downloads go to iCloud?

Yes, your Safari downloads can go to iCloud, but you have to choose iCloud Drive as your download location for that.

  • How to use Safari’s Distraction Control feature on an iPhone
  • How to use Safari iCloud tabs on iPhone, iPad and Mac

@graph.name: How to Access and View Downloads in Safari
@graph.description: Learn how to quickly access and view your downloaded files in Safari on your iPhone or iPad with just a few taps.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad with Safari browser

step.name: Open the Page Settings menu
step.text: Tap the Page Settings button located at the left corner of the Safari address bar.

itemListElement.text: Locate the Page Settings icon on the left side of the Safari address bar.
Tap the icon to open the menu.

step.name: Access your downloads
step.text: Select Downloads from the menu to see your recently downloaded files.

itemListElement.text: Tap Downloads from the list of options.
Browse the files you have downloaded recently.

step.name: Open or locate a file
step.text: Tap any downloaded file to open it directly, or tap the search icon next to it to view its location in the Files app.

itemListElement.text: Tap the downloaded file to open it within Safari.
Alternatively, tap the search icon next to the file to open its location in the Files app.

@graph.name: How to Manage Safari Download Items on the Files App
@graph.description: Learn how to find and manage your Safari downloads in the Files app on your iPhone or iPad for easy access and organization.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad with Safari downloads

step.name: Open the Files app
step.text: Launch the Files app on your iPhone or iPad to access your stored downloads.

itemListElement.text: Find and open the Files app from your Home Screen or App Library.
Wait for the app to load your file locations and folders.

step.name: Browse to your download location
step.text: Select Browse at the bottom of the screen, then navigate to the folder where your Safari downloads are saved. You’ll see the downloaded file or files listed there.

itemListElement.text: Tap Browse from the bottom menu to view all file locations.
Select iCloud Drive, On My iPhone, or any other folder where your downloads are stored.
Locate the file you downloaded from Safari.

@graph.name: How to Pause, Resume, and Cancel Downloads in Safari
@graph.description: Learn how to pause, resume, or cancel downloads in Safari on your iPhone or iPad with simple taps and gestures.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad with Safari browser

step.name: Open the Downloads list in Safari
step.text: In Safari, tap the arrow icon enclosed in a circle at the left corner of the address bar and select Downloads to view your ongoing and completed downloads.

itemListElement.text: Open Safari on your iPhone or iPad.
Tap the arrow icon inside a circle on the left side of the address bar.
Select Downloads from the menu to see all your current downloads.

step.name: Pause an ongoing download
step.text: Tap the X icon next to an active download to pause it.

itemListElement.text: Find the download currently in progress.
Tap the X icon beside it to pause the download instantly.

step.name: Resume a paused download
step.text: To resume a paused download, tap the curved arrow icon next to the paused file.

itemListElement.text: Locate the paused download in the list.
Tap the curved arrow icon to resume the download.

step.name: Cancel a download
step.text: Although Safari doesn’t have a dedicated cancel button, you can cancel a download by swiping left on it and selecting Delete.

itemListElement.text: Swipe left on the active download you want to cancel.
Tap Delete to remove and cancel the download completely.

@graph.name: How to Change the Download Location in Safari on iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Learn how to change where Safari saves your downloaded files on your iPhone or iPad using the Settings app.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad running iOS or iPadOS

step.name: Open the Settings app
step.text: Head to the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad to manage Safari’s preferences.

itemListElement.text: Locate and tap the Settings icon on your Home Screen.
Scroll down to the list of apps available in Settings.

step.name: Open Safari settings
step.text: In the Apps list, find Safari and tap it to access its settings options.

itemListElement.text: Scroll until you find Safari in the list of installed apps.
Tap Safari to open its settings page.

step.name: Open the Downloads settings
step.text: Under the General section, tap Downloads to view your current download location and available options.

itemListElement.text: Scroll to the General section within Safari settings.
Tap Downloads to open the download management screen.

step.name: Select a new download location
step.text: Choose where you want Safari to save your downloaded files: iCloud Drive, On My iPhone/iPad, or Other.

itemListElement.text: Select iCloud Drive if you want your downloads to sync across Apple devices.
Choose On My iPhone or On My iPad to save files locally on your device.
Tap Other to set a custom download folder of your choice.

@graph.name: How to Delete Safari Downloads on iPhone
@graph.description: Learn how to remove Safari downloads from your iPhone or iPad using the Files app to free up storage space quickly.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad with Safari downloads

step.name: Open the Files app
step.text: Launch the Files app on your iPhone or iPad to access your Safari downloads.

itemListElement.text: Find and open the Files app from your Home Screen or App Library.
Allow the app to load your available file locations.

step.name: Navigate to your Safari downloads
step.text: Go to the folder where Safari saves your downloads, usually in iCloud Drive or On My iPhone under the Downloads folder.

itemListElement.text: Tap Browse at the bottom of the Files app screen.
Open iCloud Drive or On My iPhone depending on where your downloads are saved.
Navigate to the Downloads folder.

step.name: Open the selection menu
step.text: Tap the three-dot menu icon in the top-right corner to open the file options.

itemListElement.text: Look for the three-dot icon in the upper-right corner of the Files app.
Tap it to display additional file management options.

step.name: Select and delete downloads
step.text: Tap Select, choose the downloaded files you want to remove, and then tap the trash icon at the bottom to delete them.

itemListElement.text: Tap Select from the menu options.
Choose one or more files you want to delete.
Tap the trash icon at the bottom of the screen to delete the selected files.

@graph.name: How to Auto-delete Downloads on an iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Learn how to set Safari to automatically delete your download list items on your iPhone or iPad to keep your device clean and organized.

supply.name: iPhone or iPad with Safari browser

step.name: Open the Settings app
step.text: Launch the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad to begin adjusting Safari’s download settings.

itemListElement.text: Locate and tap the Settings icon on your Home Screen.
Wait for the Settings menu to open completely.

step.name: Access Safari settings
step.text: Scroll down, select Apps, and tap Safari to open the Safari settings page.

itemListElement.text: Scroll through the list of installed apps under Settings.
Tap Safari to open its preferences.

step.name: Open the Downloads section
step.text: Under the General section of Safari settings, tap Downloads to manage download-related preferences.

itemListElement.text: Locate the General section inside Safari settings.
Tap Downloads to proceed to download preferences.

step.name: Set automatic download deletion
step.text: Tap Remove Download List Items, then choose After One Day or Upon Successful Download to let Safari auto-delete download list items automatically.

itemListElement.text: Tap Remove Download List Items from the available options.
Select After One Day to automatically clear downloads daily.
Or choose Upon Successful Download to remove items right after they finish downloading.

keyPoints.title: Safari’s Download Manager Features
keyPoints.explanation: Introduced with iOS 13, Safari's download manager allows users to track, pause, resume, cancel, and manage downloaded files seamlessly within the browser.

keyPoints.title: Where Safari Downloads Are Stored
keyPoints.explanation: Downloads from Safari are stored either in iCloud Drive or locally on your device, with the preferred location adjustable through the Settings app.

keyPoints.title: Reasons to Manage Downloads
keyPoints.explanation: Managing downloads helps avoid clutter, save storage space, maintain privacy, and protect your device from harmful files.

keyPoints.title: Managing Downloads on iPhone and iPad
keyPoints.explanation: You can access downloads directly in Safari via the downloads list or through the Files app, where you can view, pause, resume, delete, and change download locations.

keyPoints.title: Troubleshooting Safari Download Issues
keyPoints.explanation: If downloads are stuck or failing, ensure a stable internet, clear cache, check storage, update iOS, or change download settings to resolve problems.

title.rendered: I bought an iPhone unlocked vs. through a carrier: Here’s which option is actually better

content.rendered:
When buying a new iPhone, I made the same mistake most people make: I looked at the deal’s price. Apple shows the iPhone at its full retail price, while the carrier deals offer something like “$0/month” or “Get up to $1,200 off.”

At first glance, purchasing from a carrier may seem like a no-brainer. But once you start looking at trade-in requirements, monthly bill credits, financing terms, and what happens if you want to switch carriers, the comparison becomes much more interesting.

Here’s which one you should buy, an unlocked or a carrier-locked iPhone, before chasing the biggest discount.

What does “Unlocked” vs. “Carrier” iPhone mean?

Before comparing prices, I think it is worth clearing up one confusing part of the iPhone buying process: “unlocked” and “carrier” don’t always describe where you bought the phone. They depend on how it was financed.

An iPhone purchased directly from Apple is generally unlocked. If you pay in full or finance it through Apple Card Monthly Installments, you receive an unlocked model that can be activated with a compatible carrier. Even if you choose a carrier when purchasing, you can change carriers later and use a different carrier’s SIM or eSIM.

However, if you finance the iPhone through AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon’s installment programs, whether at Apple or on the carrier’s website, the phone remains locked to that carrier until it is paid in full. Apple applied this rule to T-Mobile and Verizon financing in July 2026; before that, only Financed iPhones bought from Apple were locked.

There’s another option that deserves its own category: Apple Upgrade, Apple’s new leasing program run by Klarna, which replaced the iPhone Upgrade Program in July 2026. An iPhone leased through Apple Upgrade is always unlocked, even if you choose a carrier when enrolling. Just remember it’s a lease: you don’t own the iPhone unless you pay off the remaining balance at the end of the term.

I compared the real cost, not just the advertised price

I don’t care whether an advertisement says an iPhone is “$0/month” until I know what I have to do to get that $0 price.

Carrier promotions can be extremely generous, offering hundreds of dollars in credits. For the iPhone 18 Pro, AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon are advertising up to $1,200 off, depending on the deal, trade-in, and eligibility. Their financing can also spread the cost over 24 or 36 months at 0% APR.

That can be a fantastic deal. But the headline price isn’t the number you should use to compare an unlocked iPhone with a carrier iPhone.

The actual iPhone cost calculation

I think about it like this:

Total cost = phone payments + required plan costs + fees − trade-in value − promotional credits

For example, you can:

Buy unlocked

  • Pay the full price of the iPhone.
  • Keep your existing phone plan.
  • Trade in your old phone if you want.
  • Switch carriers whenever you need.

Or you can:

Buy through a carrier

  • Finance the iPhone.
  • Trade in your old phone.
  • Receive monthly bill credits.
  • Keep an eligible carrier plan for the required period.

The second option might look dramatically cheaper. But if you wouldn’t have chosen that carrier or plan without the iPhone promotion, don’t count the discount as pure savings.

The monthly payment can hide the real commitment

A carrier can reduce the effective monthly cost of an iPhone by offering promotional credits over time. But those credits are generally connected to the financing and promotional terms.

That means the discount isn’t necessarily sitting in my pocket on day one. I’m earning it month after month.

Therefore, if you’re perfectly happy staying with that carrier for the entire promotional period, it can be a very smart way to buy an iPhone. But if you like changing carriers whenever a better deal appears, that “$0 iPhone” doesn’t look quite as free.

Why carrier iPhone deals look almost too good to be true

I’ll give carriers credit here: they know how to make an iPhone promotion look irresistible. For instance, “Get an iPhone for free,” “Get $1,000 off,” or “Get your new iPhone for $X per month.”

Those offers can be real. The catch is that the discount usually comes with conditions. The basic structure is often something like this:

  1. Choose an eligible iPhone.
  2. Trade in an eligible device, if required.
  3. Finance the new iPhone.
  4. Select a qualifying carrier plan.
  5. The carrier applies promotional credits to your bill over time.

The important phrase is “over time.” It’s not an instant discount, which makes switching carriers more complicated.

The biggest advantage of buying an unlocked iPhone is freedom

This is where I think the unlocked iPhone wins decisively. It’s not necessarily the cheapest option. It’s the least complicated option, with the following benefits.

1. Switch carriers whenever you want

This is the biggest advantage for me. If another carrier suddenly offers a better price, coverage, or data plan, I can switch.

This way, you don’t have to calculate how many promotional credits you’re about to lose, ask whether the remaining iPhone balance will become due, or decide whether saving $20 a month on your wireless plan is worth giving up $400 in remaining phone credits.

2. Use a travel eSIM

Apple says that if your iPhone is unlocked, you can use a travel eSIM at your destination. That means I can buy a local or travel eSIM instead of relying entirely on my home carrier’s international roaming option.

Of course, unlocked doesn’t mean universally compatible. The carrier still needs to support the iPhone, its bands, and its eSIM capabilities.

3. Have more freedom when you sell it

This is another advantage I don’t think about until it’s time to upgrade.

An unlocked iPhone is easier to hand to another buyer because the buyer isn’t tied to my old carrier.

4. Control upgrade schedule

I also like not having my upgrade decision dictated by a promotional calendar.

If you want to keep the iPhone for four years, sell it after two years, or find a great trade-in deal next year, you can consider all of these options.

There’s one big downside of an unlocked iPhone

There’s no way around it: An unlocked iPhone can cost you more upfront.

Carrier promotions can be incredibly aggressive because the carrier is using the phone deal to attract or retain customers. If you don’t want that commitment, you may have to give up some of those promotional savings. That’s the trade-off.

I’m essentially choosing between maximum discount and maximum flexibility. For some people, the discount wins. For me, the answer depends on how much flexibility I expect to use.

Want to upgrade early on a carrier deal? You may have to pay off the remaining device balance, lose future credits, or meet specific upgrade conditions. That’s why I always look at the upgrade terms before I call a carrier iPhone “cheap.”

The trade-in trap: Don’t look only at the iPhone discount

This is probably my biggest piece of advice. Don’t get hypnotized by the trade-in number.

A carrier might advertise a huge discount for trading in your current phone. That sounds fantastic. But don’t stop there; compare what you’re actually giving up.

Let’s say my old phone is worth $500 on the private market.

A carrier might advertise a larger promotional credit, but that credit may require me to:

  • Choose a qualifying plan.
  • Finance the new iPhone.
  • Remain with the carrier.
  • Wait months or years to receive the entire promotional amount.

If a carrier’s promotional deal requires you to move from a $50 monthly plan to a $90 plan, don’t pretend that extra $40 doesn’t exist. Over two years, that’s potentially $960 in additional service costs.

Meanwhile, another retailer or Apple might give me a smaller but immediate trade-in credit toward a new iPhone, and I can stay on the same $50 monthly plan. Overall, that can lower the total cost for the way you actually use your phone.

My final verdict: Which one should you buy?

After looking at the price, financing, carrier locks, trade-in promotions, and flexibility, I wouldn’t give everyone the same answer.

Buying through a carrier actually makes more sense if you:

  • Are already happy with the carrier and plan to keep the same plan anyway.
  • Like the coverage and service.
  • Get a strong trade-in promotion.
  • Don’t need to pay significantly more for the required plan.
  • Don’t plan to upgrade early.
  • Pay a genuinely lower total cost than you would by buying the iPhone unlocked.

I would buy the iPhone unlocked instead if you:

  • Switch carriers frequently.
  • Want to use a cheaper mobile plan.
  • Travel internationally and want to use travel eSIMs.
  • Don’t want promotional credits controlling when you can leave.
  • Want to sell the iPhone whenever you choose.
  • Don’t want to commit to a carrier for several years.
  • Value flexibility more than the maximum possible discount.

For me, this is the safer default. Which one are you going for? Let us know in the comments below!

title.rendered: Fortnite’s One Wish Willow Sprite is here: How to find it

content.rendered:
The Fortnite x Obsession collab has finally dropped and, as a result, the One Wish Willow Sprite has become the latest addition to the sprites lineup. This inclusion puts to bed long-running speculations about when this particular crossover with the hit 2025 film, which was first teased back on July 20, would arrive.

One Wish Willow Sprite and Honey Sprite, which rolled out today as well, take the multiplayer game’s unique sprite count to 27. If we count the variants as well, the total number of these critters shoots to a whopping 157, giving the players who are into sprite-hunting some reasonable amount of work to indulge in.

For a quick head start, you can check out the ability and upgrade boosts of the One Wish Willow Sprite in Fortnite. Plus, a few different ways using which you can make the process of catching this sprite seamless are also given below.

One Llama Luck, how may we assist you? https://t.co/H2NGniAHvv

— Fortnite (@Fortnite) July 20, 2026

What the One Wish Willow Sprite does in Fortnite

Similar to any sprite, One Wish Willow Sprite does have its own unique ability, which is to automatically extract the sprites equipped by the player you eliminate in a match. However, unlike other sprites, it also has a secondary ability and another distinct trait that takes inspiration from Obsession’s female lead character Nikki.

While One Wish Willow Sprite’s secondary ability involves pushing everything away when taking damage, its Nikki-esque behavior is basically getting ‘upset’ when unequipped and consequently marking you on the opponents’ map as a punishment for the same. Owing to the latter behavior, it’s the first Fortnite sprite of its kind to not only give the player an advantage but also a disadvantage, depending on whether or not you choose to switch sprites.

Additionally, One Wish Willow Sprite is a Mythic sprite, and it comes in all sprite variants except the Quack variant.

Ways to claim the One Wish Willow Sprite in Fortnite

Activating cheat codes

Given that One Wish Willow Sprite is a Mythic-tier item, it’s best to only target the golden Legendary Cheat Codes and the pink Epic Cheat Codes for eventually extracting this one. You can either use a Cheat Code Locator gizmo to mark a nearby cheat code during a match or simply search locations that have a dense population of these sprite-spawning panels.

Among the best places to look for cheat codes are Heatwave Harbor, Cluster Coast, Shaken Sanctuary, and Sunken Shores. Moreover, if you are looking to stock up on Cheat Code Locators before your visit, you may want to give certain Fortnite Lobby Hacks a try, as some of them provide gizmos of that kind for free.

Locating Pumpkin Chests

Since the introduction of Pumpkin Chests, they have become one of the main ways to obtain sprites in Fortnite Override, arguably only behind Cheat Codes. These Halloween-inspired chests that were rolled out for Fortnitemares 2026 exclusively grant sprites that are related to the horror theme of this ongoing event.

While Pumpkin Chests are not as prevalent in Fortnite Battle Royale as the standard chests are, certain locations that house multiple of these chests do exist. These locations include Nightmare Neighborhood, Freaky Fields, Freddy Fazbear’s Pizzeria, and Stone Sanctum. Since they aren’t as commonly available, expect competing players to be there when you approach one of these Pumpkin Chest locations.

Hunting for Rare Chests

After Fortnite Runners, Rare Chests have stopped being a likely source of sprites. However, they still have some chance of offering you one, especially if you have the corresponding loot hack unlocked.

For boosting your chances, you can upgrade the Sprite Loot Hack all the way to its maximum spawn rate. On top of that, you can equip a Loot Hacker variant sprite when opening chests, as it increases the chances of one of your loot hack unlocks triggering.

Once you’ve got the aforementioned figured out and are ready to go, you may scour Fortnite map locations with the highest number of Rare Chests. Some of these highly contested areas are Nightmare Neighborhood, Stone Sanctum, the three Pac-Man islands, and the maze to the southeast of Stone Sanctum. Since all the mentioned places are usually swarming with players, it’s best to start chest-hunting only after you have picked up fairly powerful weapons and enough consumables.

Indexing with the help of a friend

As is obvious, an efficient way of adding a new sprite such as the One Wish Willow Sprite into your collection is by temporarily borrowing it from another player. You can find like-minded Fortnite users on the game’s official Discord.

This method requires you and your friend to join two matches together. The first one will involve the other player dropping the sprite for you to pick up and extract. On the other hand, the second match will involve you returning the sprite.

After that, you can go to the Override tab and, from the Sprites section, recall the One Wish Willow Sprite by spending some Sprite Dust. In case you don’t have enough of that, refer to the previously mentioned Lobby Hacks to get some for free.

Wrapping up

One Wish Willow Sprite is certainly an innovation in this particular gameplay aspect of Fortnite. Prior to this, we had never encountered a critter like this that provides a buff but also a sort of de-buff when you decide to ditch it.

That particular element of this Obsession-inspired sprite thoroughly captures the essence of the Inde Navarrette-starrer feature film. Now, it’s only a matter of how many players think that’s enough to make this sprite a popular choice among them.

title.rendered: Apple’s regulatory listing may point to a redesigned iPad mini

content.rendered:
Apple’s French regulatory website has a listing for an unreleased iPad mini Smart Folio case, according to MacRumors, which reported it on October 15. The case carries model number A3632. MacRumors says that number matches no current or past iPad mini case. The listing sits alongside iPhone 18 Pro accessories that Apple added in September, and it has no specs, price, or launch date. Apple has not announced a new iPad mini.

A new case number may mean a new design

Apple’s current iPad mini Smart Folio is sold for the A17 Pro model. MacRumors reads the new number as a sign of a redesign that could make today’s iPad mini cases incompatible. Nothing in the listing confirms the fit, so that question stays open until Apple shows the device.

The OLED link comes from reporting, not the listing

MacRumors says the case could be for the OLED iPad mini that Bloomberg has reported. The listing itself does not mention a display. Today’s 8.3-inch mini uses an LCD panel, and OLED screens can show deeper blacks and higher contrast. MacRumors also lists a more water-resistant design among the rumored details. Earlier, MacRumors matched code identifiers in macOS 26.7 to the same OLED model. Neither piece confirms the screen.

Price and timing come from Bloomberg’s earlier reports

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has said the OLED model will cost considerably more than today’s mini, possibly close to $799. Apple has not set a price for the new model. Apple’s current model starts at $599 for the 128GB Wi-Fi version, after a price increase earlier this year moved it up from $499. At $799, the mini would sit $50 above the 11-inch iPad Air, which starts at $749.

Bloomberg has pointed to a launch on or around October 27, the same window it gives for OLED MacBook Pro models. Before Bloomberg’s October 8 report, MacRumors had called the mini’s timing unclear and placed it in neither of Apple’s two reported October launch waves. Apple’s October 13 press release introduced HomeView, a 7-inch smart home display priced at $299 in the U.S. with sales starting November 13. It did not mention an iPad mini.

What to do if you need a case or a mini now

The current iPad mini starts at $599. Apple’s newsroom and store pages will show the model name, price, and any compatible cases once it announces the device. If you are buying a case for a future mini, wait for that listing, since a changed design could change which cases fit.

title.rendered: Touchscreen MacBook Pro could launch on November 6

content.rendered:
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said on a podcast that Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook Pro could launch on Friday, November 6. MacRumors reported the date on October 15. Apple has not announced the laptop, a date, or a price, so November 6 is a reported possibility.

The same report says Apple is planning to introduce the OLED models on October 27 or 28. It does not explain how that introduction relates to a November 6 launch.

November 6 rests on a podcast remark and a store schedule

Apple’s retail stores apparently have a “big floor reset” scheduled for the evening of Thursday, November 5, running into Friday, November 6. Gurman says that could be preparation for the new Macs. A floor reset shows when stores plan to change their displays. It does not show when a product goes on sale.

Earlier reports pointed to October 27

A Bloomberg report that MacRumors covered on October 8 said Apple would introduce OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro models “on or around” Tuesday, October 27, along with an OLED iPad mini. Bloomberg said the October events would include an online video presentation and a hands-on session for members of the media.

Gurman has also said the laptop could come as early as October and slip to November. He added that Apple is testing the laptops in a macOS 27.2 beta, which he expects to be released toward the end of October.

The reports center on an OLED screen that takes touch

The new models would use OLED screens instead of mini-LED, and the reports describe 14-inch and 16-inch sizes. Touch would work alongside the keyboard and trackpad. Earlier Bloomberg-based reporting described larger touch targets and gestures such as pinch-to-zoom. Reports say macOS 27 may enlarge menus and controls when touch is detected.

Reports also describe a hole-punch camera cutout in place of the notch, paired with a Dynamic Island-style interface.

The OLED models could be sold alongside the current mini-LED MacBook Pro models as a higher-end option, according to the October 15 report. Reports say touch would not reach the MacBook Air at first.

Chip reports conflict, and no price has been reported

The October 15 report says the OLED models would use the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips already in current MacBook Pros. Earlier reports named M6 Pro and M6 Max chips instead.

No price has been reported. Macworld expects a higher starting price because OLED panels cost more to make.

Apple has not confirmed the name, date, or price

Earlier reporting suggested the model could be called the MacBook Ultra, a tier above the MacBook Pro. Bloomberg’s recent reporting puts the 14-inch and 16-inch models in the MacBook Pro family instead. Apple has not said which name it will use.

Earlier reporting put the launch in late 2026 or early 2027, and supply constraints were cited as a reason it could slip into 2027.

The October 15 report includes no Apple statement. An Apple announcement would be the first confirmed source for the date, name, and price. Until then, the reports point to two dates: October 27 or 28, and November 6.

title.rendered: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, an 816B model that runs on two Mac Studios

content.rendered:
Meta released the weights for Muse Spark Open on October 15. The model has 816 billion parameters, with 42 billion active for each token, and a 1-million-token context window. In its announcement, Meta says the model runs on two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios. One Mac Studio cannot hold the whole model.

Two 512GB Mac Studios are needed to hold the model

Each M5 Ultra Mac Studio can give its integrated GPU up to 512GB of unified memory. Meta’s post says the pair works like one machine with about a terabyte of memory, and that the chip’s 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth is fast enough to read the small slice of the model each token needs. The post does not say how the two machines are connected. Apple says Mac Studios can be clustered over Thunderbolt 5.

A smaller model needs far less memory. An Ollama setup runs on a Mac with 8GB of RAM.

Meta says it ran agentic workflows entirely on-device with Muse Code, its coding agent, powered by Muse Spark Open. The tests included iOS fixes and new features for Ice Cubes, an open-source Mastodon client. In a DaVinci Resolve test, the model reviewed footage frame by frame and cropped clips to vertical format.

The 512GB configuration is due in late October

Apple lists $5,499 as the starting price of the M5 Ultra Mac Studio. The 512GB configuration is coming in late October. Meta’s model card puts the NVFP4 version at 700GB of memory, so the two-machine setup likely needs that top option.

The Information reported that demand for local AI hardware pushed Apple’s August refresh forward. Apple has not confirmed that.

A comparison of the M6 Mac mini and M5 Ultra Mac Studio finds the Mac mini the better choice for most people. The Studio suits heavier work such as large-scale AI.

Hugging Face needs a login, and large API resellers need a Meta deal

The weights are on Hugging Face in BF16 and NVFP4 versions. The page asks users to log in and review the conditions before they can access the model. Meta’s model card says running the model on your own system requires at least 700GB of GPU memory for NVFP4 and 2TB for BF16. The card does not say which version the Mac setup uses.

The model ships under the Muse Model License. Meta says its commercial terms are limited and let many developers use the model for free. The license sets a revenue threshold for hosted services. A company that gives third parties API access to the model must sign a separate written agreement with Meta once its combined gross revenue passes $20 million in any 12-month period. Internal use and research are exempt.

Readers without two Mac Studios can use hosted API providers, including Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter, and Together AI. Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden, and Microsoft Foundry Models also offer the weights for download.

Meta’s own numbers put it top on MCP-Atlas but behind some rivals overall

Meta’s model card compares Muse Spark Open with other open-weight models. It scores 39 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, behind Qwen3.8 at 40, Kimi K3 at 44, and GLM 5.3 at 45. It scores 89.2 on MCP-Atlas, a test of agent tool use, the highest score in that table.

Because the weights are open, Meta added extra safety training, and the model met the release thresholds in its Meta Superintelligence Scaling Framework. A full evaluation report is “available soon.”

Meta said in April it hoped to open future Muse models

Meta launched Muse Spark in April to power the Meta AI app and meta.ai. The April post said Meta hoped to open-source future versions of the model. The Muse Spark Open model card describes the release as an open-weights version with additional safety post-training. Meta’s announcement does not give a date for the next open release.

To help you out, we’ve compiled a list of all the active Smash a Piggy codes that you can redeem for free rewards, including Dust, Luck Potions, and more. These freebies can give you a helpful boost, making it easier to find better loot and progress through the game.

All working Smash a Piggy codes

  • Release: 1 Luck Potion (NEW)

As of now, these are the only active Smash a Piggy codes available. Make sure to redeem them as soon as possible, as codes can expire without warning, leaving you unable to claim their rewards.

Expired Smash a Piggy codes

Currently, all available codes are valid and can be redeemed. Keep in mind that developers may remove them when new codes are issued, so it’s best to redeem them promptly.

How to redeem Smash a Piggy codes in Roblox

Knowing the active codes isn’t enough, gamers! You also need to know how to redeem them and claim your free rewards. Thankfully, the process only takes a few minutes. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to redeem Smash a Piggy codes:

  1. Fire up Smash a Piggy on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Click on the Shop button.
  4. Paste a working code and hit Redeem to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed the rewards, they should be added to your inventory automatically.

Why aren’t My Smash a Piggy codes working?

If your Smash a Piggy codes aren’t working, double-check that you’ve entered them exactly as listed above. Keep in mind that these codes are case-sensitive, so make sure there are no extra spaces before or after them. You can simply copy and paste the codes directly from our list. If a code still doesn’t work, it might’ve expired, or you may have already redeemed its rewards.

How to get more Smash a Piggy codes

The developers don’t follow a fixed schedule for releasing new Smash a Piggy codes. Most codes are released to celebrate major game updates, seasonal events, or community milestones.

To stay updated, you can:

  • Join the official Discord server: Visit the Smash a Piggy Discord server to find announcements and newly released codes.
  • Follow the Roblox game page: Check the game’s official Roblox page for updates, announcements, and potential code releases.
  • Bookmark this page: We’ll update this guide whenever new Smash a Piggy codes become available, so you can easily find the latest rewards in one place.

If you’re looking for more Roblox freebies, check out our latest Kaiju Alpha codes, Drop a Fruit codes, Turbo Soccer codes and our complete Roblox Game Codes hub.

FAQs

Do you need to join the group to redeem codes?

No, you don’t need to join any group to redeem Smash a Piggy codes. Simply open up the game on Roblox, and follow the steps mentioned above to redeem your rewards.

How often do new codes come out?

New codes for Smash a Piggy often drop alongside major game updates or milestones. There’s no fixed release schedule, so expect the codes to arrive at any time.

What does the Luck Potion do?

Luck Potion in Smash a Piggy increases your luck, which in turn improves your chance of obtaining better loot when smashing piggy banks.

Update: Verified the latest Kaiju Alpha Codes on October 23, 2026

Looking for Kaiju Alpha codes? Then you’re in the right place! In order to upgrade your Kaiju and make it as powerful as possible, you’ll need plenty of Tokens and other resources. However, farming these items can prove to be quite challenging, especially if you’re new to the game.

However, there’s no need to worry, as we’ve compiled a list of the active Kaiju Alpha codes that you can redeem for free Tokens and other in-game rewards to speed up your progression.

All working Kaiju Alpha codes

  • NOLIMITTOTHELARVA: Redeem for 20 Levels (Requirement: play for 30 minutes) (NEW)
  • 1MILLIONMEMBERS: 50 Levels, Cell and Exp boost (lasts 5 hours), and 500k Cells ( Join the group and play for an hour to redeem)

As of now, this is the only active Kaiju Alpha code available. Make sure to redeem them as soon as possible, as codes can expire without warning, leaving you unable to claim their rewards.

Expired or unverified Kaiju Alpha codes

BADSONGLEE, DEAWYGIGACHAD, KAONTOP, ROSE, SINGULARITY, SRRYFORBUG, SRRYFORBUGGUYS, SRRYFORBUGS, SRRYFORREVERTLEVEL, XECRETISREAL

How to redeem Kaiju Alpha codes in Roblox

Knowing the active codes isn’t enough, gamers! You also need to know how to redeem them and claim your free rewards. Thankfully, the process only takes a few minutes. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to redeem Kaiju Alpha codes:

  1. Fire up Kaiju Alpha on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Click on the Options button.
  4. Paste a working code and hit Enter to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed the rewards, they should be added to your inventory automatically.

Where to find more Kaiju Alpha codes

The developers don’t follow a fixed schedule for releasing new Kaiju Alpha codes. Most codes are released to celebrate major game updates, seasonal events, or community milestones.

To stay updated, you can:

  • Join the official Discord server: Visit the Kaiju Alpha Discord server to find announcements and newly released codes.
  • Follow the Roblox game page: Check the game’s official Roblox page for updates, announcements, and potential code releases.
  • Bookmark this page: We’ll update this guide whenever new Kaiju Alpha codes become available, so you can easily find the latest rewards in one place.

If you’re looking for more Roblox freebies, check out our latest Drop a Fruit codes, Anime Dice codes, Turbo Soccer codes and our complete Roblox game codes hub.

FAQs

Why Are My Kaiju Alpha Codes Not Working?

Make sure you’ve entered the code exactly as shown in our list, including the correct spelling, capitalisation, and special characters. If a code still doesn’t work, it may have expired or already been redeemed on your account. You can also try restarting the game and entering the code again.

What Rewards Can You Get From Kaiju Alpha Codes?

Kaiju Alpha codes can give you a variety of rewards such as Cells, EXP boosts, Tokens, and instant levels. These help you to unlock upgrades, level up Kaiju and progress faster.

title.rendered: How to get the Dollie skin in Fortnite | Lost Dolls bundle items list

content.rendered:
Fortnite has been consistently shipping spooky cosmetics into the Item Shop, in line with the Halloween-themed Fortnitemares event, and Dollie is one of the original skins created for this very occasion. In the Lost Dolls category, besides Dollie, there are Mineko and Peppa Pinns as well.

Unlike a chunk of the skins released recently, these cosmetics aren’t the result of any third-party collab but are original designs created by Fortnite devs. Additionally, this is their first stint in the online multiplayer title, having only debuted on October 9.

While the aforementioned three skins can be purchased individually for 1,200 V-Bucks each, you can alternatively grab the Lost Dolls Bundle, which comes with extras, for 2,300 V-Bucks. Moreover, these items are only available in the Shop until October 15, 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET.

Steps to claim the Dollie skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Shop tab.
  2. Next, scroll down to the Fortnitemares section and select it.
  3. Then, scroll down to the Locker of Horrors category and select your desired skin.
  4. Finally, press and hold the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

All Lost Dolls bundle items in Fortnite

The following cosmetics are all the items that are included in the Lost Dolls Bundle. Their individual prices and respective bundled freebies are also listed below.

1. Dollie

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Also includes: Doll Eyes wrap

2. Mineko

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Also includes: Glowing Blossom wrap

3. Pippa Pinns

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Also includes: Baneful Blaster wrap

4. Dollie’s Dark Portrait back bling

Price: 300 V-Bucks

5. Baneful Bunbun back bling

Price: 400 V-Bucks

6. Sakura Shamisen pickaxe and back bling

Price: 800 V-Bucks

7. Music Box Mannequin emote

Price: 400 V-Bucks

8. Glowing Blossom wrap

Price: 500 V-Bucks

9. Doll Eyes wrap

Price: 500 V-Bucks

10. Baneful Blaster wrap

Price: 500 V-Bucks

Wrapping up

Fortnitemares 2026 has turned out to be a rather remarkable rendition this time, at least in terms of cosmetics content. From original skins such as Dollie to major third-party collab skins such as Sora (Kingdom Hearts) and Joker (Persona), cosmetic items have come out at a consistent cadence and also feature an intriguing amount of variety among them.

Over the final few weeks of Fortnitemares and Fortnite Override itself, both of which will run till October 31, a few more popular collabs are set to make their way into the Item Shop. This forthcoming lineup features names such as Hazbin Hotel, Obsession, and The Purge. It will be interesting to see how the players, a sizable section of whom have been excitedly awaiting a few of these IPs, receive the content drop once it’s out.

  • How to get the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Lucy skin in Fortnite
  • How to get the Inoxtag skin in Fortnite

title.rendered: Fortnite x Yeat crossover: Release time, items, and price

content.rendered:
Yeat is joining Fortnite’s Icon Series, and his bundle hits the Item Shop on October 15, 2026, at 8:00 PM ET (5:00 PM PT). It’s the rapper’s first full set of outfits in the game; until now he only had two Icon emotes, GEEK TIMË and COMË N GO.

Epic confirmed the collab on October 14 with the “Real Lyfe” trailer, which shows two Yeat outfits set to “If We Being Real.” The drop lines up with the v42.40 update, the last major patch of Chapter 7 Season 4, and lands in the middle of Fortnitemares 2026.

When does the Fortnite x Yeat collab release?

The Item Shop resets at 00:00 UTC, so anyone east of the Americas gets Yeat on October 16.

Everything in the Fortnite x Yeat icon series bundle

Epic hasn’t published an item list. Leaker ShiinaBR and esports.gg report the set below; the trailer backs up the outfits, wrap and kicks.

  • 2 Outfits: one with an Alternate Style, one with a Reactive Style
  • 2 Back Blings
  • 1 Pickaxe
  • 2 Emotes
  • 1 Microphone (Festival instrument)
  • 1 Wrap
  • 1 Kicks

Three Jam Tracks are coming, but only one sits in the bundle

Yeat brings three songs to Fortnite Festival: If We Being Real, Money So Big and Get Busy. According to Beebom, one is packed into the bundle and the other two sell separately in the Item Shop.

If Jam Tracks follow their usual pricing, each standalone track will cost 500 V-Bucks.

Epic hasn’t confirmed the price yet

No price has been announced. Based on recent Icon sets, expect each outfit at around 1,500 V-Bucks and the full bundle at roughly 3,000–3,500 V-Bucks.

The closest comparison is Madison Beer’s bundle from September. It had two outfits, a mic, emotes and Jam Tracks, and it sold for 3,400 V-Bucks (our Madison Beer guide lists every item price).

We’ll update this post with exact prices once the shop goes live.

There’s no free way to get Yeat right now

Some Icon sets launch with an Icon Cup that awards the outfit early, as Madison Beer’s did. Epic hasn’t announced one for Yeat, so the Item Shop is the only confirmed route. For other options, see our free Fortnite skins guide.

Wrapping up

Yeat lands as Chapter 7 Season 4 winds down, alongside v42.40’s new Honey and Obsession Sprites. Epic hasn’t said how long the bundle will stay in the shop; Madison Beer’s set stayed for about ten days, so don’t wait too long.

Festival Season 15 is still headlined by Lil Tecca, so Yeat isn’t this season’s Festival Icon. Watch the Season 16 reveal for the next music collab.

Are you picking up the Yeat bundle, or just the Jam Tracks? Let us know in the comments.

FAQs

Is Yeat the Fortnite Festival Season 15 Icon?

No. Lil Tecca is the Season 15 Festival Icon. Yeat joins through the Icon Series in the Item Shop.

Can you get the Yeat skin for free?

title.rendered: Anime Zero: All accessories and how to unlock them

content.rendered:
Accessories are a crucial aspect of Anime Zero, as they allow you to amp up your weapon’s strength and take on tougher dungeons packed with enemies. However, crafting them can cost valuable resources, so it’s crucial to know which stat boosts each accessory brings to the table before committing to one. Not only that, but knowing your options also helps you decide whether there’s a better alternative worth investing in.

On top of that, the latest Update 3 (Void Arbiter) added 13 new accessories, bringing the total to 27. So, to make things easier, here’s a complete list of all the accessories in Anime Zero and how you can unlock each of them easily!

Complete list of accessories in Anime Zero

Keep in mind that each Anime Zero accessory requires different crafting materials. They all offer unique stat boosts, such as weapon damage, HP, EXP, drop rates, and others. With that out of the way, here’s a complete list of all the accessories in the game, with the ones added in Update 3 marked as (New)

Also check out: Anime Zero codes

How to unlock accessories in Anime Zero

Of course, the next big question is: how do you unlock accessories in Anime Zero? To do so, you’ll need to craft them using specific resources. Simply go out and collect all of the materials required for the accessory you want to obtain, as we’ve mentioned above. You can farm them in Story and Infinite Mode runs, or buy some of them from the Shop tab in the crafting menu.

Once you have everything, open the Areas option and choose Crafting from the menu. Then, head to Yugi the Forger, select the accessory from the Craft tab, and hit Quick Craft.

Keep in mind that you can equip up to four accessories at once, one each in the head, face, neck, and back slots. So, instead of crafting accessories at random, pick the best option for each slot.

Wrapping up

There are 27 accessories in Anime Zero, and each of them offers different stat boosts to improve your weapons. Crafting these accessories is important for progressing through the game, as they can help you steamroll dungeons and defeat enemies.

title.rendered: Universal Monsters skins return to Fortnite after nearly four years

content.rendered:
The Mummy, Frankenstein’s Monster, and Frankenstein’s Bride from the Universal Monsters franchise are back in Fortnite. The three skins first arrived in October 2021 and were last sold in the Item Shop in November 2022. That makes this return their first in nearly four years, timed for the ongoing Halloween event, Fortnitemares 2026.

Each skin costs 1,200 V-Bucks. The Mummy and Frankenstein’s Monster each come with a free back bling, while Frankenstein’s Bride is sold on her own. The Mummy is also part of the Mummy Bundle for 1,600 V-Bucks.

At the time of writing, the Universal Monsters cosmetics are listed in the Item Shop until October 16, 5 PM PT / 8 PM ET. If you’ve waited years for one of these classic monsters, use the steps below before they rotate out.

Steps to get the Universal Monsters skins in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, go to the Shop tab.
  2. Scroll down to the Universal Monsters section and select the skin you want.
  3. On the next screen, press and hold the Purchase button to complete the transaction.

If you want The Mummy along with his pickaxe and wrap, the Mummy Bundle is the better pick. It includes The Mummy, Smallcophagus, Ancient Staff, and Mummified for 1,600 V-Bucks.

All Universal Monsters cosmetics in Fortnite

1. The Mummy (outfit)

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Comes with: Smallcophagus back bling
Also available in: Mummy Bundle

Frankenstein’s Monster (outfit)

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Comes with: Monster Mind back bling

Frankenstein’s Bride (outfit)

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks

Ancient Staff (pickaxe)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: Mummy Bundle

Grave Robber (pickaxe)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

Smallcophagus (back bling)

Comes with: The Mummy skin
Also available in: Mummy Bundle

Monster Mind (back bling)

Comes with: Frankenstein’s Monster skin

Mummified (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: Mummy Bundle

Stitched Up (wrap)

Price: 300 V-Bucks

Wrapping up

Throughout Fortnite Override, recognizable IPs have brought both cosmetics and gameplay content into the game. For Halloween, that run has turned to horror. Five Nights at Freddy’s opened Fortnitemares on October 1, followed by Freddy Krueger and 99 Nights in the Forest.

With Chapter 7 Season 4 expected to wrap up around October 31, Epic has roughly two weeks left for more Halloween drops. Fortnitemares is in full swing, so more horror franchises could still join Fortnite’s long list of collabs before the month ends.

FAQs

Can I get a Universal Monsters skin in Fortnite for free?

No. The Universal Monsters skins are sold only in the Item Shop for V-Bucks. There is no quest or event reward that unlocks them. If you’re short on V-Bucks, see our guide on ways to get free Fortnite skins.

Can I get all three Universal Monsters skins in one bundle?

No. In this rotation, only The Mummy has a bundle, the 1,600 V-Bucks Mummy Bundle. Frankenstein’s Monster and Frankenstein’s Bride are sold individually.

When did the Universal Monsters skins first come to Fortnite?

All three debuted during Fortnitemares 2021. Frankenstein’s Monster arrived first in early October, followed by The Mummy and then Frankenstein’s Bride later that month.

Which other horror collabs are in the Fortnite Item Shop right now?

As of this week’s shop, you can also buy cosmetics from Five Nights at Freddy’s, A Nightmare on Elm Street (Freddy Krueger), Stranger Things, and 99 Nights in the Forest.

blockGraphs.question: Can I get a Universal Monsters skin in Fortnite for free?
blockGraphs.answer: No. The Universal Monsters skins are sold only in the Item Shop for V-Bucks. There is no quest or event reward that unlocks them. If you're short on V-Bucks, see our guide on ways to get free Fortnite skins.

blockGraphs.question: Can I get all three Universal Monsters skins in one bundle?
blockGraphs.answer: No. In this rotation, only The Mummy has a bundle, the 1,600 V-Bucks Mummy Bundle. Frankenstein's Monster and Frankenstein's Bride are sold individually.

blockGraphs.question: When did the Universal Monsters skins first come to Fortnite?
blockGraphs.answer: All three debuted during Fortnitemares 2021. Frankenstein's Monster arrived first in early October, followed by The Mummy and then Frankenstein's Bride later that month.

blockGraphs.question: Which other horror collabs are in the Fortnite Item Shop right now?
blockGraphs.answer: As of this week's shop, you can also buy cosmetics from Five Nights at Freddy's, A Nightmare on Elm Street (Freddy Krueger), Stranger Things, and 99 Nights in the Forest.

title.rendered: iPhone Duo repair fees: $999 for the inner display, $1,499 for other damage

content.rendered:
Apple listed out-of-warranty repair fees for the iPhone Duo on October 14, according to MacRumors. Without AppleCare+, replacing the inner display costs $999, and the highest fee for other accidental damage is $1,499. With AppleCare+, both of those repairs cost $99.

Without AppleCare+, the inner display repair costs $999

The Duo’s two displays are priced as separate repairs, and the inner one is the most expensive screen fix on the list. The fees below are the ones MacRumors reported from that listing. They are U.S. prices, with the AppleCare+ fee in the last column.

The listing calls $1,499 the maximum for other damage, so it marks the top of that range. At $999, the inner display repair alone is half the Duo’s $1,999 starting price. The cover layer is the only repair under $100 without the plan, at $49. Battery service costs $229 without the plan. With AppleCare+, the battery is replaced at no charge when capacity drops below 80 percent.

One inner display repair makes the AppleCare+ plan cheaper

AppleCare+ with Theft and Loss for iPhone Duo costs $19.99 a month, $199.99 a year, or $399 upfront. Apple says the plan covers accidents like drops and spills, battery replacement, and theft and loss on eligible products, with priority support from Apple Experts.

With the plan, one inner display repair costs $498 in total: the $399 upfront price and the $99 fee. Without it, the same repair costs $999. That makes one inner display repair enough for the upfront plan to come out cheaper. The plan prices do not say how long the coverage lasts, so the $498 figure assumes one repair within the plan’s term. A theft or loss claim carries a $149 fee.

AppleCare One is a separate monthly plan that covers more than one device.

Duo fees run about double the iPhone 17 Pro’s without a plan

Apple’s 2025 fee list for the iPhone 17 Pro put other damage at $749 and the front screen at $329, both without AppleCare+. The Duo’s $1,499 for other damage is about double that. Its $999 inner display is about three times the iPhone 17 Pro front screen fee.

Both phones pay $99 with AppleCare+ for other accidental damage, so the difference for that repair sits entirely in the no-plan column.

Some repairs have no plan price, and the fees are estimates

The reported list has no AppleCare+ fee for rear camera damage, which costs $229 without the plan. It also has no plan fee for outer display and back glass damage together, which costs $509 without it. MacRumors reports that Apple calls the figures estimated repair fees, so check the current prices on Apple’s repair page before you decide.

Pre-orders open October 16, and the phone goes on sale October 23

The Duo starts at $1,999 in the US, or $83.29 a month for 24 months through Apple Card Monthly Installments. Pre-orders begin at 5 a.m. PT on October 16, general availability starts October 23, and 28 other countries and regions get it on October 30.

Must read:

  • What to do immediately if your iPhone Duo display is cracked

title.rendered: WhatsApp guest calling lets people without an account join a call

content.rendered:
WhatsApp announced guest calling on October 14. A WhatsApp user can now send a call link to someone who doesn’t have WhatsApp. That person joins from a computer browser after the host lets them in. WhatsApp’s examples are colleagues, classmates, and tutors, and the post says hosts don’t have to worry about which apps those people use.

Guests need only a link and a browser

Only people with a WhatsApp account can create a call link, so the host must have one. The host does three things:

  1. Opens the Calls tab and taps the + icon.
  2. Creates a call link and sends it.
  3. Admits the guest from the waiting room.

Guests type a name and wait until the host lets them in. The host can remove a guest at any time. The call-link panel in WhatsApp’s announcement artwork warns that anyone with the link can use it, so share it only with people you trust.

Apple’s FaceTime follows a similar pattern for Android and Windows users. The Apple user creates the link, and the guest joins in Chrome or Edge without being able to start a call. The setup is in how to use FaceTime on Android or PC.

Guests can share their screen but can’t invite others

Guests can share their computer screen to review materials, react with a thumbs up or heart, and raise a hand. They can’t see other participants’ phone numbers or send messages. They also can’t add anyone to the call directly.

Calls have no time limit and a 32-person cap

WhatsApp describes guest calls as free, end-to-end encrypted, and without time limits. That means no abrupt cutoffs, so nobody has to restart the call or wait for everyone to rejoin. One-to-one and group calls can include up to 32 people once the host admits them. A study group or a small team fits under that cap. Regular WhatsApp group calls also top out at 32 people, and how to make audio and video WhatsApp calls on iPhone, Mac, and web covers the group steps.

Zoom’s free Basic plan allows 100 people per meeting but caps each meeting at 40 minutes, according to Zoom’s pricing page. For a long call with up to 32 people, WhatsApp removes that limit. For 33 to 100 people, WhatsApp can’t hold the call, and Zoom’s free plan can.

Some coverage frames the launch as a challenge to Zoom and Google Meet. WhatsApp’s post names neither service, so this article compares only Zoom.

Calendar links are due later this year

WhatsApp plans calendar integrations for Google Calendar and Outlook later this year. Users will install a WhatsApp plugin, connect their account, and add a call link to an invite. Invitees can join with or without a WhatsApp account. Until those integrations launch, the call link has to go into the invite by hand. iPhone users can already schedule a WhatsApp call from the iPhone Calendar app.

Countries and phone access are still unclear

WhatsApp’s post doesn’t name the countries where guest calling is available. It also doesn’t say whether every account has the option yet. It describes guests joining from a computer browser and doesn’t say how a guest on a phone would join.

title.rendered: OpenAI reportedly agrees not to use Apple’s alleged trade secrets while the case runs

content.rendered:
According to Bloomberg, OpenAI has agreed not to use the trade secrets Apple accuses it of misusing, for as long as the lawsuit is pending. The commitment came at a hearing on Wednesday, October 14, before U.S. District Judge Edward Davila in San Jose. OpenAI denies the allegations, and the court has not ruled on whether they are true.

Apple sued OpenAI in July, naming OpenAI, io Products, and former Apple employees Tang Tan and Chang Liu. The case is Apple Inc. v. Liu in the Northern District of California. Apple alleges that the former employees used its proprietary information to help OpenAI develop hardware, and that they told new OpenAI hires how to avoid scrutiny when leaving Apple.

OpenAI agreed not to use the alleged secrets during the case

Bloomberg describes the commitment as voluntary, and says the judge can enforce it. The reporting does not say whether OpenAI filed it as a stipulation or whether it was entered as an order. The October 13 order does not mention the agreement. No statement from Apple or OpenAI on the agreement was available when this was written.

OpenAI will collect forensic images from 14 employees’ devices

OpenAI also agreed to collect forensic images from the devices of 14 employees that may hold Apple’s confidential information, Bloomberg reported. A forensic image is a full copy of a device’s data that investigators can examine later.

The judge had already flagged the risk of lost evidence. In the October 13 order, he called Apple’s argument that forensic data could be lost or overwritten "well-taken." He pointed to a conversation in which Liu and Alyssa Peng discussed restoring Apple-owned devices.

Apple gets early access to messages and interviews, not R&D files

Under the October 13 order, Apple can get three categories of material before the normal discovery schedule:

  • Forensic images the defendants have already collected
  • Documents used to interview Apple candidates for OpenAI’s hardware group, including scripts and summaries of interviews with Apple employees
  • LINE conversations between Liu and Peng since January 1, 2026

Apple’s request for OpenAI’s research files on metal finishes, power management, and battery functionality was denied. Those files will come through regular discovery. Liu, Tang Tan, and Peng must sit for depositions, and OpenAI and io Products must produce corporate witnesses.

The judge also deferred ruling on requests that use the term "Apple Originated Information." He called it "amorphous as currently defined" and gave Apple five days to propose a tighter version.

The judge is reportedly likely to back Apple on the injunction

Apple has asked for a preliminary injunction that would bar OpenAI from using any confidential information it acquired from Apple while the case goes on. At the hearing, Davila said he was "highly likely" to side with Apple, according to Bloomberg. No ruling has been reported yet.

OpenAI’s motion to dismiss argues that Apple has not identified any specific stolen trade secrets. OpenAI has said it has no need or desire for Apple’s trade secrets.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported in July that the case could make it harder for OpenAI to keep its reported 2027 timeline for its first device. An injunction would limit how that hardware work can use Apple’s information.

The first deadline falls around October 18

Defendants must respond to the expedited requests within 14 days of the order, or within five days for materials they have already collected. The forensic images are in the five-day group, so they are due around October 18. The depositions follow within 30 days after Apple receives those responses.

The reporting gives no date for the injunction ruling.

excerpt.rendered: Bloomberg reports OpenAI agreed not to use Apple’s alleged trade secrets while the lawsuit runs. Judge Edward Davila reportedly leans toward Apple on an injunction.

title.rendered: Apple Intelligence is reportedly coming to China in December without Siri AI

content.rendered:
Apple plans to bring Apple Intelligence to mainland China in December, according to a Bloomberg report published October 14. The first launch would arrive in an iOS 27.3 update and leave out Siri AI, the assistant Apple announced this year. Apple has not confirmed the date or the update number.

Apple Intelligence has not been available in mainland China since it launched in 2024.

The launch would leave out Siri AI and image generation

The report says the first set would include Genmoji, AI notification summaries, Writing Tools, and the Clean Up tool in Photos. Text generation would be limited in some apps. Image Playground and the newer version of Genmoji would be left out, along with Siri AI.

Apple’s October Apple TV 4K announcement says Siri AI is still in beta and launches in English in eight countries and regions. It is not initially available in the EU on iOS or iPadOS.

These are mostly features Apple first introduced in 2024. References in macOS 26.7 code had already pointed to Writing Tools coming to China with content restrictions, but that was code, not an announcement.

Alibaba supplies the models, with a government filter

Alibaba confirmed in July that its Qwen model will power Apple Intelligence features for Chinese users. It gave no timeframe. The report names Qwen and Tongyi Wanxiang as the models, and says the setup includes guardrails, including a filter that lets the government approve ongoing model updates.

Reuters reported in August, citing three anonymous sources, that Apple trained a China-specific AI model with Alibaba’s help.

TechCrunch reported in July that a Baidu spokesperson confirmed the work, but a Reuters-based report says Baidu made no on-record statement. Bloomberg says the work covers search and Siri-related features.

China’s regulator listed Apple’s service in July

On July 15, the Cyberspace Administration of China published a notice listing seven phone on-device generative AI services with completed filings. Apple’s service appears on the list as “Apple智能.” Media called it approval, but the notice is a filing record and gives no launch date.

Permit records for newer iPhones, including the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, reportedly list the Alibaba models.

Apple has not confirmed a date yet

Apple made no announcement in late March, when Apple Intelligence briefly appeared for some iPhone users in mainland China before the update was pulled. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said the rollout was accidental.

Apple has still not announced a China date or commented publicly on the report. Its Apple Intelligence availability page says new Apple Intelligence features will not be available in China while Apple works through regulatory requirements.

The same page says that once Apple Intelligence reaches mainland China, devices bought earlier that support it will be able to switch on a core set of features there. Until Apple names a date, December rests on sources. The reports also do not explain why Siri AI is left out.

title.rendered: HomePod mini 2: Is it worth $149 before Siri AI arrives?

content.rendered:
Apple announced the HomePod mini 2 on October 13, 2026. Pre-orders opened the same day, and the speaker goes on sale in stores on October 30. It costs $149, which is $50 more than the original mini cost when it launched in 2020.

You get a new S10 chip, Thread support, and a light display on top right away. The feature Apple leads with, Siri AI, comes later as a free software update. So the real question is whether the speaker is worth $149 without it.

HomePod mini 2 specs at a glance

Apple’s spec page lists these. Thread matters most if you’re building a smart home, and Wi-Fi 6E only helps if your router supports the 6 GHz band.

HomePod mini 2 vs. Original HomePod mini: What’s new

The original mini shipped with an S5 chip. The S10 is the biggest hardware change, and Apple pairs it with computational audio that analyzes music in real time to adjust dynamic range, loudness, and acoustic performance.

Other changes:

  • Light display: Sound Glow sits on top of the speaker (more on that below).
  • Colors: Pink and green are new. Yellow and orange from the older lineup aren’t on the new list. Red, which Gurman reported Apple had tested, didn’t make it.
  • Sensors: Temperature and humidity sensing is now on Apple’s spec sheet.

How does HomePod mini 2 sound? (and what sound glow does)

Apple gives the speaker a full-range driver, dual passive radiators, and 360-degree sound. It doesn’t publish driver size or power output, so you can’t compare the audio on paper. If sound quality is the main reason to buy, check reviews first.

Sound Glow is the light show on top. It pulses in sync with the music, takes its colors from album art, and can run soundscape animations like rain. It’s fun, but it doesn’t change how the speaker sounds.

Is HomePod mini 2 worth $149?

The original mini was $129 after Apple’s June 2026 price increase, so the new one costs $20 more than that. The full-size HomePod costs $349, so the mini is still the cheaper way into Apple’s speaker lineup.

If you only want a speaker for music and timers, $20 for a faster chip and a light show is hard to justify on specs alone. The math gets better if you want the four-speaker Apple TV setup, which needs a mini 2 or a 2nd-generation HomePod.

When will HomePod mini 2 get Siri AI?

Siri AI debuted with iOS 27. Apple says it comes to the HomePod mini 2 as a free software update in the future, and it hasn’t given a date.

According to Apple, it adds:

  • Personal context, when paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad
  • Voice recognition for up to six people in the house
  • Broader world knowledge from the web
  • Better music discovery and more natural conversation

The limits matter more than the feature list:

  • The owner of the home needs an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad on the latest software, with Siri AI turned on.
  • It starts in English in the US, Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and the UK.
  • It won’t initially be available in the EU on iOS or iPadOS.
  • Some server-side features have daily limits, and Apple says expanded access will cost money later.

Apple hasn’t said whether the original mini gets Siri AI, so don’t assume it will. Apple says Siri requests can use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, and that data processed in Private Cloud Compute isn’t stored or made accessible to Apple or anyone else.

HomePod mini 2 as a smart home hub

The mini 2 works as a home hub for HomeKit and Matter accessories. Once it’s set up with your iPhone or iPad, you can control them from the Home app when you’re away. The accessories themselves are sold separately.

Two things need a caveat:

  • Sound Recognition: It listens for smoke and carbon monoxide alarms and sends alerts to your iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. It needs the updated Home setup and the latest software on every device. Apple says not to rely on it in an emergency, so keep your real alarms in place.
  • Sensors: The temperature and humidity sensors read best between 15°C and 30°C, at 30% to 70% humidity. The speaker needs time to settle after it starts up.

Also Read: Apple HomeView vs HomePod mini 2: What’s the difference, and which one should you buy?

How four-speaker surround sound works with Apple TV 4K

The new Apple TV 4K (4th generation) is the first Apple TV 4K to support four-speaker surround sound. You need four speakers in matching front and rear pairs, using HomePod mini 2 or HomePod (2nd generation). Apple’s setup photo pairs two mini 2s with two full-size HomePods around the TV. The speakers detect where they sit in the room and set timing and levels on their own.

The Apple TV 4K costs $299 and ships November 13, so the setup can’t start before then. If you own one mini, you’d need three more speakers to use it this way.

Stereo pairs, Mac audio, and multiroom AirPlay

Two mini 2s make a stereo pair, but both must be the same model and generation. It also works as a speaker for a Mac with Wi-Fi 6E or later, and it can join multiroom AirPlay with other HomePods or AirPlay speakers.

Should you buy HomePod mini 2 or wait?

  • Buy it if you want a smart home hub that supports Thread and Matter, or you plan to build the four-speaker Apple TV setup.
  • Wait if Siri AI is the main reason. Apple hasn’t given a date, and it hasn’t said whether the original mini will get it.

Final thoughts

HomePod mini 2 is a real upgrade, even before Siri AI arrives. The S10 chip, Thread support, and Wi-Fi 6E make it a better smart home hub than the original. It’s also the cheapest way into Apple’s new four-speaker surround setup with Apple TV 4K. Sound Glow adds some personality, but it doesn’t change how the speaker sounds.

The problem is timing. Apple’s marketing leads with Siri AI, and that feature has no release date. Apple also hasn’t said whether the original mini will get it. That leaves you paying $149 today for hardware upgrades plus a promise.

If you’re building out a Matter or Thread smart home, or you’re planning the Apple TV surround setup after November 13, buy it now. If you mainly want a smarter Siri, your current mini will keep working fine until Apple gives a date. Wait for reviews and the software update before you spend.
