mainEntity.name: Can I disable Smart Stack on my Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Smart Stack is a built-in watchOS feature. Rather than disabling the entire feature, you can remove unwanted widgets, pin the ones you need, and adjust the available suggestion settings.

mainEntity.name: How many widgets can I add to Smart Stack?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple doesn't specify a universal maximum number of widgets in its user guide. The available selection depends on compatible apps and widgets. Add the ones you find useful rather than following an arbitrary widget limit.

mainEntity.name: Can I use third-party widgets in Smart Stack?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Compatible third-party apps can provide widgets for Smart Stack. The available widgets depend on the app and its support for your watchOS version.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Smart Stack and complications?

acceptedAnswer.text: Complications display selected information directly on your watch face. Smart Stack is a separate collection of widgets that you can open to access more information without changing your watch face.

@graph.name: How to Customize the Photos App View on iPhone
@graph.description: Personalize your Photos app home screen by rearranging, replacing, or removing collections and albums on your iPhone.

step.name: Open customization options
step.text: Open the Photos app, scroll to the bottom, and tap Customize & Reorder.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Photos app on your iPhone.
Scroll to the bottom and tap Customize & Reorder.

step.name: Replace an album tile
step.text: Tap the Replace button under any Album tile to change it to a different collection.

itemListElement.text: Tap Replace under the tile you want to change.
Select a new collection to display in its place.

step.name: Reorder album tiles
step.text: Tap and hold any Collection, then drag and drop it to a new position.

itemListElement.text: Tap, hold, and drag a Collection tile to rearrange its order.

step.name: Remove a collection from home screen
step.text: Uncheck any collection you no longer want to appear on the Photos app home screen.

itemListElement.text: Uncheck the box next to any collection to hide it.

step.name: Exit or reset customization
step.text: Tap the X at the top right to exit customization. Or, tap Reset at the top left to revert to default layout.

itemListElement.text: Tap X at the top right to save and exit.
Tap Reset to restore the original layout if needed.

@graph.name: How to Hide People in the People & Pets Section
@graph.description: Easily remove or hide specific individuals from the People & Pets section in your iPhone's Photos app.

step.name: Open the People section
step.text: Open the Photos app, scroll down, and tap on the People section.

itemListElement.text: Open the Photos app on your iPhone.
Scroll down and tap People.

step.name: Select individuals to hide
step.text: Choose the people you want to hide from the People album.

itemListElement.text: Tap on the faces you want to hide.

step.name: Hide selected people
step.text: Tap the three-dot button at the bottom right corner, then select Hide. Confirm by tapping Remove from People Album.

itemListElement.text: Tap the three-dot menu at the bottom right.
Select Hide from the menu.
Tap Remove from People Album to confirm.

step.name: Optional: Create a new group
step.text: You can also create a custom group with selected individuals for easier access.

itemListElement.text: Tap Create New Group at the bottom.
Select the people to include and tap Add.

step.name: Optional: Add more people
step.text: To add someone to the People & Pets section, tap Add People and select from available faces.

itemListElement.text: Tap Add People at the bottom of the People screen.
Select individuals and tap Add in the top-right corner.

@graph.name: How to Modify Pinned Collections in the Photos App
@graph.description: Learn how to customize the Pinned Collection in the Photos app by adding, removing, or creating albums for quick access.

step.name: Open the Pinned Collection
step.text: With the Photos app open, scroll down to the Pinned Collection and tap the Modify button.

itemListElement.text: Open the Photos app on your iPhone.
Scroll down to find the Pinned Collection section.
Tap the Modify button to begin editing.

step.name: Remove albums from the Pinned Collection
step.text: Tap the minus button before an album to remove it from the Pinned Collection.

itemListElement.text: Look for the album you want to remove.
Tap the minus button beside it.

step.name: Add albums to the Pinned Collection
step.text: Tap the plus button before an album to add it to the Pinned Collection.

itemListElement.text: Browse through the available albums.
Tap the plus button beside the album you want to pin.

step.name: Add a new collection or album
step.text: Tap the Add Collection or Album button if you want to add something other than the suggested collections.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Add Collection or Album button at the bottom of the screen.
Choose the album or collection you want to include.

@graph.name: How to Remove Photos from Featured Photos
@graph.description: Easily remove unwanted pictures from Featured Photos in the Photos app to keep your highlights more personalized.

step.name: Open Featured Photos
step.text: With the Photos app open, scroll down and tap on Featured Photos.

itemListElement.text: Open the Photos app on your iPhone.
Scroll down until you see Featured Photos.
Tap Featured Photos to view the collection.

step.name: Select the photos you want to remove
step.text: Tap the Select button, then choose the photos you want to remove from Featured Photos.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Select button at the top.
Tap on each photo you want to remove.

step.name: Remove from Featured Photos
step.text: Once done, tap the three dot button at the bottom right corner, then select Remove from Featured Photos.

itemListElement.text: Tap the three dot button at the bottom right corner.
Choose Remove from Featured Photos from the menu.

keyPoints.title: iOS 18 Photos App Redesign Reversed in iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Apple brought back the classic tab-based structure in the Photos app after user feedback, replacing the system that focused more on system-generated albums.

keyPoints.title: Customizing the Photos App View in iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Users can now reorder collections in the Photos app by entering editing mode in the Collections tab, allowing a more personalized navigation.

keyPoints.title: How to Hide People & Pets in the Photos App
keyPoints.explanation: You can hide specific individuals in the People & Pets section by selecting them and choosing 'Hide', or create new groups for better organization.

keyPoints.title: Modify Pinned Collections for Better Access
keyPoints.explanation: The default pinned collections can be customized by adding or removing albums through the edit options in the Collections tab.

keyPoints.title: Removing Unwanted Photos from Featured Photos
keyPoints.explanation: You can select and remove specific photos from the Featured Photos section, helping curate your favorite memories more easily.

title.rendered: iPhone wallpaper dimensions and sizes: complete guide for all models

content.rendered:
Use your iPhone’s screen resolution as a starting point when choosing a wallpaper. Matching the screen’s shape helps avoid awkward crops; using a larger image keeps it sharp when you zoom in.

If you are not sure which iPhone you have, find the model name and number first.

Why wallpaper dimensions matter

An image with the wrong shape may lose its edges when iOS fills the screen. A file smaller than the display can also look soft after you enlarge it. The chart below groups models that share a resolution, so you can choose the right size without sorting through every launch year.

iPhone screen sizes and resolutions

These are portrait display resolutions. Aspect ratios are approximate; iOS may crop the image slightly when you set it.

Choose a wallpaper that stays sharp

For the sharpest result, use a portrait image at your iPhone’s native resolution or larger, with a similar aspect ratio. There is no universal extra-pixel rule: a larger file gives you more room to zoom, but a close ratio matters just as much because iOS crops the image to fill the screen.

If your image is smaller than the display, it may look blurry when enlarged. If it is much wider or taller, iOS will trim the excess. Keep faces, text, and logos away from the edges so the crop does not cut them off.

Portrait or landscape wallpapers

Portrait images fit an iPhone screen with less cropping. A landscape photo can still work, but iOS must enlarge and crop it to fill the tall display. Choose one with open space around the subject, or use a portrait version if you want to keep the whole scene.

Design a wallpaper that works on the Lock Screen

Keep the main subject clear of the top-centre camera cutout and leave room for the clock and widgets. Their position can vary with your Lock Screen setup, so check the preview before saving. For a Home Screen wallpaper, avoid placing important details where app icons will cover them.

How to set a wallpaper on iPhone

On current iOS, add the image from Settings:

  1. Open Settings and tap Wallpaper.
  2. Tap Add New Wallpaper, then choose Photos.
  3. Select the image and adjust its position.
  4. Tap Add, then choose Set as Wallpaper Pair or Customise Home Screen.

If the image is already open in Photos, the Share menu is a shortcut to the same wallpaper preview:

  1. Open the Photos app and choose the image you want to set as wallpaper.
  2. Tap Share → Use as Wallpaper.
  3. Pinch to zoom or adjust framing.
  4. Tap Add, then choose Set as Wallpaper Pair or Customise Home Screen.

Find an iPhone wallpaper

Browse aesthetic, minimalist, and Dynamic Island wallpapers for designs made around the iPhone’s tall screen. Use the largest download available for your model, then check the Lock Screen preview before applying it.

For most iPhones, matching the portrait shape and keeping the file at or above the screen resolution is enough. Adjust the crop only if the preview cuts off something you want to keep.

Related articles:

  • How to Check Battery Cycle Count on iPhone
  • How to take a screenshot on an iPhone and iPad

title.rendered: Apple schedules Q4 2026 earnings report for November 2

content.rendered:
Apple will report its fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results on Monday, November 2. The company’s Investor Relations calendar lists the results for 1:30 p.m. Pacific, followed by a 2 p.m. conference call with CEO John Ternus and CFO Kevan Parekh.

It will be Ternus’s first earnings call as CEO. Apple announced that he took over the role from Tim Cook on September 1.

The quarter includes launch-week iPhone 18 Pro sales

Apple’s fiscal Q4 ran from June 28 through September 26. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max went on sale September 18, so the results will include the first nine days of sales for the new models. Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4, and AirPods 5 also launched that day.

The iPhone Duo will not appear in the Q4 numbers. Apple says the device goes on sale October 23, nearly a month after the quarter closed. Its sales will be part of the following quarter instead.

Apple’s July outlook sets a benchmark

During its July earnings call, Apple said it expected total revenue for the September quarter to grow 9% to 11% year over year. The company also expected iPhone revenue to grow in the mid-teens, while noting foreign-exchange headwinds and tighter supply for iPhone, Mac, and iPad.

Apple reported $102.5 billion in Q4 2025 revenue. Applying the July growth range to that figure points to about $111.7 billion to $113.7 billion for this quarter. That is a calculation from Apple’s prior-year revenue and guidance, not a new forecast. The previous Q4 results provide the year-over-year baseline.

Apple also forecast a 47% to 48% gross margin for the September quarter. That is below the 50.1% reported for June, although tariff refunds added about two percentage points to the June figure. Apple’s June-quarter revenue grew 16%, but September brought higher memory costs and price increases across parts of the lineup.

The November 2 call will be Ternus’s first earnings call as CEO. July’s earnings call included CFO Kevan Parekh’s comments on slower Services growth.

title.rendered: Report: Apple and LG are developing a smart home device lineup

content.rendered:
Apple and LG have reportedly worked together on seven smart home devices, including a doorbell, thermostat, smart lock, and security cameras. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that the products will carry the LG brand, with LG handling manufacturing and product support while Apple helps shape their design and features.

Apple has not confirmed the partnership or the products. If the report is accurate, the lineup would give Apple a faster way to expand its home ecosystem without manufacturing and supporting every accessory itself.

The reported lineup covers cameras, a lock, and climate control

Bloomberg lists an LG Video Doorbell Wired, LG Smart Deadbolt Lock, LG Smart Thermostat, LG Temperature Sensor, LG Indoor Cam Plug-In, LG Outdoor Cam Plug-In, and LG Floodlight Cam. It reports that many products will support Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Thread, and Matter. The deadbolt reportedly includes ultra-wideband (UWB).

These names also appear in regulatory and product-certification filings LG submitted to the U.S. Federal Communications Commission and UL Solutions, according to Bloomberg. The filings do not mention Apple. Bloomberg says LG asked the agencies to keep product photos and more detailed information confidential until early 2027, so the public record offers little about final specifications.

Matter can connect compatible accessories with different smart home platforms, while Thread is a low-power mesh network for home devices. Bloomberg does not say which models support each standard or whether all seven support Matter. UWB could allow a lock to respond when an authorized device is nearby, but Apple and LG have not explained how that would work.

LG would make and support the accessories

The arrangement would leave the devices under LG’s name, even though Apple reportedly had a hand in their design, features, and engineering. LG would manufacture the products and handle support. That gives Apple a partner with an existing hardware operation for categories such as doorbells, locks, thermostats, and cameras.

Apple already works with third-party companies across its smart home platform. The reported accessories would add more hardware options around Apple’s upcoming home hub and sit alongside the HomeKit devices already available. Bloomberg says the products are designed to complement the hub, but Apple has not confirmed their exact compatibility or whether every accessory will work with Apple Home.

The accessories may arrive months after Apple’s hub

Bloomberg says Apple is expected to introduce a home hub, updated HomePod mini, and updated Apple TV on October 13, part of its reported October product wave. Apple has not announced that date or confirmed the lineup. The LG accessories are not expected to reach consumers for at least a few more months, so they are not part of an immediate rollout even if Apple’s hub appears this month.

Prices, country availability, and launch dates remain unknown. Buyers will also need confirmation of which Apple Home features each device supports, especially for video recording and smart-lock controls. For now, the partnership and device list remain reported plans rather than announced products.

Bloomberg has not reported where the cameras or doorbell would store video, whether recording needs a subscription, or how long LG will provide software support. Those details will shape how the products fit into a home already using Apple’s Home app.

excerpt.rendered: Apple and LG reportedly codeveloped seven smart home devices, with LG handling production and support. Bloomberg says the accessories may arrive in a few months.

title.rendered: Apple overtakes Samsung in Europe’s carrier smartphone sales

content.rendered:
Apple passed Samsung to lead Europe’s smartphone operator channel in Q2 2026, even as phone sales fell across the region. Counterpoint Research says sales through mobile operators fell 4% year over year, compared with an 11% decline in the open market.

The lead applies only to carrier sales. Counterpoint links the channel’s relative strength to its premium-device mix and the pressure rising memory costs have put on cheaper phones.

Carrier sales held up better than retail sales

Total smartphone sales in Europe fell 8% year over year in Q2, according to Counterpoint. Sales through operators declined by 4%, while the open market, which includes sales outside carrier channels, fell 11%. That gap helped operators gain share of the market, even though they also sold fewer phones than a year earlier.

The channel mix helps explain why. Counterpoint says carrier sales tend to include more high-end phones and premium brands because more devices are bought on contract. Meanwhile, higher memory costs have hit the low end of the market particularly hard. The operator channel has weathered the downturn better, but its sales still fell.

Apple moved ahead of Samsung in the operator channel

Apple’s share of smartphone sales through European operators rose from 33% in Q2 2025 to 37% in Q2 2026, according to Counterpoint figures cited by 9to5Mac. Samsung’s share fell from 39% to 34% over the same period. Apple gained four percentage points while Samsung lost five.

Those shares show each brand’s portion of operator sales, not the number of phones it sold. Since the channel shrank 4%, Apple’s bigger share alone cannot show whether it sold more phones through carriers. Counterpoint’s public summary does not give brand-level unit totals.

Those figures apply only to carrier sales. Counterpoint’s separate estimate of all European smartphone shipments put Apple and Samsung at 34% each in Q2. Shipments and sales through operators measure different parts of the market, so Apple’s carrier-channel lead does not mean it led overall European shipments. In the global market, Q2 shipment rankings also put Samsung ahead of Apple.

Counterpoint also says vivo and Motorola helped the operator channel, with both brands growing faster than the market. The public report does not break out the country-level figures or say which phone models drove Apple’s gain.

Memory costs may keep shifting the channel mix

Counterpoint expects the operator channel to continue gaining share over the next few quarters if memory-price pressure keeps hurting lower-cost phones. Independent retailers have increased promotional activity, however, which could soften price increases and help the open market recover some demand.

The Q2 data show Apple’s lead in one sales channel, not a wider recovery in Europe’s smartphone market. They also do not tell buyers whether one carrier has better iPhone deals; Counterpoint tracks channel sales, not individual offers.

title.rendered: How to find and use the Skeleton Key in Fortnite

content.rendered:
Fortnitemares is back, bringing the spooky season with a bunch of exciting crossovers, new game modes, weapons, and more! However, one exciting addition this time around is the Skeleton Key. What does it do? It’s a special Nightmare Neighbourhood item that can be used to unlock Secret Rooms, which pack some seriously game-changing loot. So, if you’re wondering how to get your hands on one and make the most of it, here’s everything you need to know about the Skeleton Key in Fortnite.

Here’s how to find the Skeleton Key in Fortnite

In order to find the Skeleton Key in Fortnite, head over to Nightmare Neighbourhood and make your way to the graveyard. You will come across three different mausoleums here, but only two of them can contain a chest.

Once you enter a mausoleum, equip your pickaxe and dig in front of the tombstone to reveal a hidden chest. Open it, and there’s a chance you’ll find the Skeleton Key inside. Keep in mind that only two Skeleton Keys can spawn in a typical round.

The Skeleton Key cannot be found anywhere else on the island. So, if you’re looking to find one, the graveyard in Nightmare Neighbourhood is the place to go.

Here’s how to use the Skeleton Key in Fortnite

Once you’ve found the Skeleton Key, head to the mansion located just outside the graveyard. Before entering, make sure you have Visualised Sound enabled in your settings, as this is going to come in handy.

Enter the mansion, and from the ground floor, open the door to the first room. Make your way down the stairs until you reach an area with three different doors. You can use the Skeleton Key to unlock any of these rooms, with each one containing a random selection of loot.

There isn’t a specific door that’s better than the others, as the loot is randomised in every match. However, having Visualised Sound enables you to make the right call. Stand outside each room and listen for the audio hints, which can give you an idea of whether or not the room contains a chest before you use your Skeleton Key.

Rounding up

The Skeleton Key is a special item in Fortnite that allows players to unlock secret doors inside the mansion at the Nightmare Neighbourhood POI. You can find it in the area’s graveyard, where it can give you access to rooms filled with loot. Alongside the FNAF and Obsession crossover, the Skeleton Key is one of the many unique additions of Fortnitemares 2026.

title.rendered: How to check iPhone battery cycle count (fast & easy)

content.rendered:
Your iPhone’s cycle count tracks how much of its battery capacity you have used. On iPhone 15 or later, you can find it in Settings. iPhone 14 and earlier show battery health there, but not the cycle count.

The number is one clue about battery wear, not a replacement deadline. Check maximum capacity, service alerts, and how long your iPhone lasts between charges too.

What is the battery cycle count in an iPhone?

A cycle adds up to 100% of the battery’s capacity used, even across several partial charges. Use 50% today, recharge, then use another 50% later, and that adds up to one cycle.

A cycle count rises with use, not each time you plug in your iPhone.

Why check your iPhone’s battery cycle count?

Apple rates iPhone batteries to retain up to 80% of original capacity after a set number of full cycles under ideal conditions. That number differs by model, but it is not a deadline for replacing the battery:

  1. iPhone 14 and earlier: Designed to retain up to 80% capacity after 500 complete cycles under ideal conditions.
  2. iPhone 15 and later: Designed to retain up to 80% capacity after 1000 complete cycles under ideal conditions.

Cycle count is most useful when you are comparing a used iPhone or investigating shorter battery life. A high number alone does not tell you whether the battery needs service.

How to check battery cycle count on iPhone 15 and later

On iPhone 15 or later with iOS 17.4 or later, the cycle count is in Battery Health:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Battery.
  3. Tap Battery Health.
  4. Read Cycle Count. The same screen also shows maximum capacity, manufacture date, and first use.

If Cycle Count is missing, check that your iPhone is a 15 or later model and is running iOS 17.4 or later. iPhone 14 and earlier do not show it in Settings.

How to check battery cycle count on iPhone 14 and later

On iPhone 14 and earlier, Settings shows Battery Health & Charging and Maximum Capacity, but not Cycle Count. You can try the analytics methods below; they work only when the log contains the cycle-count field. For a more direct option, connect the phone to a Mac or PC and use iMazing.

Method 1: Using the PowerUtil shortcut

  1. Download the PowerUtil shortcut and tap Add Shortcut.
  2. Open Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.
  3. Tap Analytics Data and open the latest log.
  4. Tap Share, then choose PowerUtil.
  5. Review the shortcut’s requested access before allowing it.
  6. Look for the cycle-count value. If it is missing, try the manual search below or use a computer tool.

Tip: Only run shortcuts you trust, and review their requested access before continuing.

Method 2: manually checking analytics data

To search the log yourself, copy its text into Notes and look for the cycle-count field:

  1. Open Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.
  2. Tap Analytics Data and open the latest log.
  3. Tap Share, copy the data, and paste it into Notes.
  4. In Notes, use Find in Note to search for last_value_CycleCount.
  5. If the field appears, the number beside it is the cycle count. If it is missing, that log cannot provide the number.

Using third-party apps to check battery cycle count

For an older iPhone, iMazing can show charge cycles from a connected Mac or Windows computer. Connect your iPhone, select it in iMazing, open Overview > Battery Health > Details, then look for Charge Cycles. This is a desktop option; iPhone 15 and later show the count in Settings.

Video: how to check iPhone 15 battery cycle count

When should you replace your iPhone battery?

A high cycle count by itself is not a reason to replace a battery. Look for these signs instead:

  1. Service warning: Settings says service is recommended, or maximum capacity has fallen enough to affect your day.
  2. Short runtime: You need to charge more often even though your routine has not changed.
  3. Unexpected shutdowns: Your iPhone turns off before the battery reaches zero.
  4. Slower performance: iOS may limit peak performance if an aged battery cannot deliver enough power.

Tips to help your iPhone’s battery last longer

Heat wears a battery faster, so keep your iPhone out of hot cars and direct sun while charging. On iPhone 15 or later, open Settings > Battery > Charging to set a Charge Limit. On iPhone 14 or earlier, leave Optimised Battery Charging on under Settings > Battery > Battery Health & Charging.

Keep an eye on your iPhone’s battery health

Cycle count is easy to find on iPhone 15 and later. On older models, check Battery Health & Charging first; use the analytics log or a connected computer only if you need the exact count. If Settings shows a service warning or your phone no longer lasts through the day, have the battery checked.

FAQs

What if I don’t see Cycle Count in my Settings?

Cycle Count appears under Settings > Battery > Battery Health on iPhone 15 or later with iOS 17.4 or later. iPhone 14 and earlier do not show it in Settings.

Is a high cycle count always bad?

No. Check Maximum Capacity, any Service warning, and whether the battery lasts through your usual day. Cycle count alone is not a replacement deadline.

Can I trust third-party apps for battery stats?

Use Settings on iPhone 15 or later, or a trusted desktop diagnostic tool on an older model. Avoid uploading analytics files to unfamiliar services.

How do I keep my iPhone battery health at 100%?

You can’t keep battery health at 100% forever. Heat and charging habits affect battery ageing; see our guide to maintaining iPhone battery health for ways to slow it down.

mainEntity.name: What if I don't see Cycle Count in my Settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cycle Count appears under Settings > Battery > Battery Health on iPhone 15 or later with iOS 17.4 or later. iPhone 14 and earlier do not show it in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Is a high cycle count always bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Check Maximum Capacity, any Service warning, and whether the battery lasts through your usual day. Cycle count alone is not a replacement deadline.

mainEntity.name: Can I trust third-party apps for battery stats?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use Settings on iPhone 15 or later, or a trusted desktop diagnostic tool on an older model. Avoid uploading analytics files to unfamiliar services.

mainEntity.name: How do I keep my iPhone battery health at 100%?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't keep battery health at 100% forever. Heat and charging habits affect battery ageing; see our guide to maintaining iPhone battery health for ways to slow it down.

@graph.name: How to Check Battery Cycle Count on iPhone 15, iPhone 16, and iPhone 16e
@graph.description: View the battery cycle count on your iPhone 15, iPhone 16, or iPhone 16e directly from the Settings app to monitor battery health.

step.name: Open Settings
step.text: Unlock your iPhone and open the Settings app from your home screen.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Settings icon.

step.name: Go to About section
step.text: Navigate to General and then tap About to view your device information.

itemListElement.text: Tap General.
Tap About.

step.name: Locate battery cycle count
step.text: Scroll down to the Battery section and find Cycle Count to see how many battery cycles your device has completed.

itemListElement.text: Scroll to Battery section.
View Cycle Count.

@graph.name: How to Check Battery Cycle Count on iPhone 14 or Earlier using PowerUtil Shortcut
@graph.description: Find your iPhone's battery cycle count on iPhone 14 or earlier models by using the PowerUtil shortcut with analytics data from your device.

step.name: Download PowerUtil shortcut
step.text: Download the PowerUtil shortcut on your iPhone and tap Add Shortcut to add it to your Shortcuts app.

itemListElement.text: Download the PowerUtil shortcut.
Tap Add Shortcut.

step.name: Open Analytics settings
step.text: Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.

itemListElement.text: Open Settings.
Navigate to Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.

step.name: Select latest analytics file
step.text: Tap Analytics Data and choose the latest file with today’s date.

itemListElement.text: Tap Analytics Data.
Select the latest file.

step.name: Share with PowerUtil
step.text: Tap the Share icon, choose PowerUtil from the Share Sheet, and grant any necessary permissions.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Share icon.
Select PowerUtil.
Allow necessary permissions.

step.name: View cycle count
step.text: The shortcut will display your battery’s cycle count and other relevant battery stats.

itemListElement.text: Read the displayed cycle count.

@graph.name: How to Check Battery Cycle Count on iPhone 14 or Earlier via Manually Checking Analytics Data
@graph.description: Manually find your iPhone's battery cycle count on iPhone 14 or earlier models by checking analytics data through the Settings app.

step.name: Open Analytics settings
step.text: Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements, then tap Analytics Data and select the latest file with today’s date.

itemListElement.text: Open Settings.
Navigate to Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.
Tap Analytics Data and select the latest file.

step.name: Copy analytics data
step.text: Tap the Share icon and copy the contents of the analytics file.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Share icon.
Copy the text.

step.name: Paste into Notes
step.text: Open the Notes app and paste the copied analytics data into a new note.

itemListElement.text: Open Notes app.
Paste the copied text.

step.name: Find cycle count entry
step.text: Tap the three-dot icon, select Find in Note, and search for last_value_CycleCount. The number next to it is your battery’s cycle count.

itemListElement.text: Tap the three-dot icon in Notes.
Select Find in Note.
Search for last_value_CycleCount.

keyPoints.title: Understanding iPhone Battery Cycle Count
keyPoints.explanation: The cycle count tracks how many full charges your battery has gone through, with every partial charge adding to this total, indicating overall battery wear.

keyPoints.title: Importance of Monitoring Cycle Count
keyPoints.explanation: Keeping an eye on your cycle count helps assess your battery’s health, decide when to replace it, and ensure your iPhone continues to perform well.

keyPoints.title: How to Check Cycle Count on iPhone 15 and Newer Models
keyPoints.explanation: For iPhone 15 or later running iOS 17.4+, you can easily find the cycle count in Settings > General > About > Battery.

keyPoints.title: Checking Cycle Count on Older iPhones
keyPoints.explanation: Older models require using shortcuts like PowerUtil, analyzing analytics data, or third-party apps to view the cycle count due to limited iOS support.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
"The founder of iGeeksBlog, Dhvanesh, is an Apple aficionado, who cannot stand even a slight innuendo about Apple products. He dons the cap of editor-in-chief to make sure that articles match the quality standard before they are published."

About Dhvanesh

Ever since teenage years, gadgets and technology have held a special place in Dhvanesh's heart. This fascination with gadgets and their inner workings fueled a lifelong passion for exploration and troubleshooting. Disassembled electronic items scattered around the house became a familiar sight during his younger years, a testament to this insatiable curiosity.

From SEO Expert to Apple Evangelist

After completing his IT engineering diploma, Dhvanesh's professional journey began with a 4.5-year stint as an SEO executive, honing valuable digital marketing skills. However, the desire to share tech knowledge and connect with a like-minded community proved stronger. In 2012, Dhvanesh embarked on a new adventure, founding iGeeksBlog. This blog became a haven for Apple enthusiasts and tech aficionados seeking insightful and in-depth information about everything Apple.

A Decade of iGeeksBlog: Leading the Apple Charge

In the past 12 years, Dhvanesh has donned multiple hats at iGeeksBlog. As the founder, he has steered the blog’s vision, ensuring it remains a trusted resource for Apple users worldwide. Additionally, he has been serving as the CEO of iGeeks Media Private Limited for the past 4 years, overseeing the company's growth and development.

Beyond Writing: A Multifaceted Approach

Dhvanesh isn't just a prolific writer, having penned hundreds of articles for iGeeksBlog. He has also served as the blog’s Editor-in-Chief and Content Strategist, ensuring a consistent flow of high-quality content that caters to the diverse needs of the Apple user base. The passion for exploration extends beyond the written word. He has created numerous YouTube videos for iGeeksBlog, providing visual demonstrations and engaging directly with the audience.

Staying Connected with the Apple Ecosystem

Dhvanesh's dedication to the Apple community goes a step further. Currently, he also manages the iGeeksBlog+ weekly newsletter, delivering curated Apple news, gadgets, apps, tips and tricks straight to subscribers' inboxes. This unwavering commitment to Apple technology and a genuine desire to empower fellow users make him a valuable asset to the iGeeksBlog team.

title.rendered: AirPods volume too low? 14 Ways to make AirPods louder on iPhone in iOS 27

content.rendered:
If your AirPods sound quieter than they used to, don’t worry—you may not need to replace them just yet. I’ve used AirPods for years, and I’ve found that low volume can be caused by something as simple as blocked speaker grills, an iPhone setting, a poor fit, or one of the newer AirPods features that automatically adjusts volume.

In this guide, I’ll show you the easiest ways to make your AirPods louder on an iPhone running iOS 27. I’ll also cover the latest AirPods models and settings, so you can find the cause of the low volume and fix it without compromising your hearing.

Before you start: Check these basics

Before changing any settings, I recommend checking these simple things.

Turn up the media volume

Start playing music or a video and then:

  1. Press the Volume Up button on your iPhone.
  2. Or open Control Centre and drag the volume slider upward.
  3. You can also ask Siri to increase the volume to set it around 75% to 100%.

On newer AirPods models, you may also be able to adjust the volume directly from the AirPods. For example, AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging case, AirPods Pro 2, and AirPods Pro 3 let you swipe up or down on the stem to change volume.

Make sure your AirPods have enough charge

Put your AirPods in the charging case and check their battery level from your iPhone.

A very low battery isn’t normally the first thing I’d blame for low volume, but checking the charge level eliminates an easy variable before you start troubleshooting.

1. Adjust Reduce Loud Audio settings

This is one of the first settings I’d check on iOS 27.

Your iPhone can automatically reduce headphone audio when it reaches the maximum decibel level you’ve configured.

  1. Open Settings and go to Sounds & Haptics.
  2. Tap Headphone Safety.
  3. Look for Reduce Loud Audio.
  4. If it is enabled, check the selected decibel limit.

If you want your iPhone to stop reducing audio at your current limit, you can adjust this setting.

However, I don’t recommend disabling hearing-protection features simply to listen louder. Apple warns that listening to headphones at high volume for extended periods can damage your hearing. In some countries or regions, certain headphone-safety controls may also be required and cannot be disabled.

My recommendation: If your AirPods suddenly became quieter, check this setting first. If the limit is already appropriate, don’t simply remove it to force a higher volume.

2. Check Personalized Volume

If you have newer AirPods, this is one of the most important checks. Personalised Volume automatically adjusts your media volume based on your surroundings and your previous listening habits.

Apple currently supports Personalised Volume on models including AirPods 4 with ANC, AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2.

  1. Put your AirPods in your ears.
  2. Make sure they’re connected to your iPhone.
  3. Open Settings and tap Bluetooth.
  4. Tap the ⓘ button next to your AirPods.
  5. If necessary, tap Audio & Routing.
  6. Toggle off Personalized Volume temporarily and test your music again.

If the volume suddenly feels normal after disabling it, you’ve found the reason iOS was changing your listening level.

3. Turn off Conversation Awareness

Another newer feature that can make AirPods seem unusually quiet is Conversation Awareness.

When Conversation Awareness detects that you’re talking, it automatically lowers your media volume and makes voices around you easier to hear. Once the conversation ends, the media volume returns to its previous level.

This feature is available on newer AirPods models, including AirPods 4 with ANC, AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2.

To check it:

  1. Connect your AirPods.
  2. Open Control Center.
  3. Touch and hold the volume control.
  4. Check Conversation Awareness.
  5. Turn it off temporarily.

Now play the same song again. If the volume no longer drops whenever you speak, Conversation Awareness was responsible.

4. Check your music app’s sound settings

If your AirPods only sound quiet when you’re listening to Apple Music, the AirPods themselves may not be the problem.

  1. Open Settings, scroll down, tap Apps.
  2. Select Music.
  3. Find Sound Check.
  4. Turn it off temporarily and test your music.

Sound Check normalises the loudness of different songs, so some tracks may sound quieter than others. I found the differences between stereo songs and Dolby Atmos tracks noticeable.

You can also go to the EQ option and set it to Off temporarily. If the problem disappears, your selected EQ profile was changing the sound signature rather than your AirPods failing.

5. Check the AirPods’ custom EQ

If you have a newer supported AirPods model, there is another EQ setting that is separate from Apple Music’s EQ.

In iOS 27, you get a three-band custom equalizer on AirPods 4 or later, AirPods Pro 2 or later, and AirPods Max 2.

To check it:

  1. Connect your AirPods.
  2. Open Settings.
  3. Tap the name of your AirPods near the top.
  4. Tap Audio & Routing and go to Equaliser.
  5. Select Recommended instead of Custom, or adjust the Low, Mid, and High sliders.

Apple says custom EQ settings are stored on the AirPods and carry over to other paired devices. So, I use this method when my AirPods sound noticeably different across devices.

6. Use Headphone Accommodations

If your AirPods don’t sound loud or clear enough because certain frequencies are difficult for you to hear, Headphone Accommodations may be more useful than simply increasing the master volume.

Apple’s current compatibility list includes:

  • AirPods 2
  • AirPods 3
  • AirPods 4
  • AirPods 4 with ANC
  • AirPods Pro 1
  • AirPods Pro 2
  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods Max
  • AirPods Max 2
  • Several supported Beats models

To set it up:

  1. Open Settings and go to Accessibility.
  2. Tap Audio & Visual.
  3. Select Headphone Accommodations.
  4. Toggle on Headphone Accommodations.
  5. Tap Customise Audio below.
  6. Follow the audio test on screen.
  7. Apply the recommended custom settings.

You can also manually adjust amplification, tone, Audio Tuning, and other audio characteristics, play a sample, and decide what sounds best to you.

However, this is not an actual “hack” that would amplify the volume of your AirPods. Rather, it will make the quiet frequencies audible, helping you hear the music, speech, and podcasts better without simply raising the overall volume.

7. Check the left-right audio balance

If one AirPod sounds quieter than the other, don’t immediately reset the AirPods. The audio balance may have been moved accidentally.

Go to Settings > Accessibility > Audio & Visual and find Balance and make sure the slider is centred. If the balance is heavily shifted to one side, move it back to the centre and test both AirPods again.

Observation: For some local tracks on my iPhone, enabling Mono Audio seemed to increase the volume, though the experience may not be delightful.

8. Check the fit and seal of your AirPods Pro

As I have tested different AirPods, I have noticed that the physical fit of the AirPods Pro can make a surprisingly big difference in perceived volume and bass.

A poor seal lets outside sound leak in, making your music seem quieter even though the AirPods are producing the same volume.

For AirPods Pro 1 and Pro 2, Apple provides an Ear Tip Fit Test and AirPods Pro 3 has a newer Acoustic Seal Test.

To check:

  1. Put your AirPods Pro in your ears.
  2. Open Settings.
  3. Tap Bluetooth.
  4. Tap the ⓘ button next to your AirPods.
  5. Choose Ear Tip Fit Test or Test Acoustic Seal, depending on your model.
  6. Follow the instructions.

If the test indicates a poor seal, try another ear-tip size.

Apple specifically recommends using the ear tips designed for your AirPods Pro model because the tip design differs between generations.

9. Check your listening mode instead of simply turning ANC off

There is no universal principle that turning off ANC will automatically increase headphone volume. In a noisy environment, Active Noise Cancellation can actually make music easier to hear because it reduces the competing background noise.

Instead, try the available listening modes and see which one works best for your environment.

For supported models:

  1. Connect your AirPods.
  2. Open Control Center.
  3. Touch and hold the volume control.
  4. Tap Listening Mode.
  5. Try Noise Cancellation, Transparency, or Adaptive as appropriate.

On supported newer AirPods, Adaptive Audio automatically balances noise cancellation and transparency according to your surroundings.

If you’re in a loud environment, I’d generally try ANC before increasing the volume dramatically.

10. Check Loud Sound Reduction

Newer AirPods have additional hearing-protection features that can affect how much environmental sound you hear.

On compatible AirPods, Loud Sound Reduction can reduce exposure to loud environmental noise while using Transparency or Adaptive Audio. Apple notes that this feature is associated with Hearing Protection on AirPods Pro 2 and AirPods Pro 3.

If your issue is that outside sounds are overpowering your music, do not rush to turn off the protection feature. Instead, try switching to Noise Cancellation in a safe environment and see whether the perceived loudness improves.

I would prioritise protecting your hearing over forcing the AirPods to play louder.

11. Clean your AirPods

If you’ve been using your AirPods for years, cleaning the mesh is worth doing before you assume the hardware has degraded.

Earwax, dust, and debris can partially block the acoustic mesh and reduce perceived volume. Apple also notes that debris can affect sound and noise-control performance.

I would especially check this if:

  • One AirPod is quieter than the other.
  • Bass has disappeared.
  • Volume gradually decreased over time.
  • ANC performance has become worse.
  • You frequently use your AirPods while exercising.

However, be careful when cleaning. I would remove the old recommendation to use a toothpick. Don’t poke the speaker mesh with a sharp object or use abrasive materials. Get a dedicated cleaning kit for your AirPods.

Follow the correct cleaning procedure according to your particular model and keep liquids, cleaning products, and compressed air away from the acoustic openings.

12. Check the audio source

Sometimes your AirPods aren’t actually producing low volume—the content itself is quiet.

This can happen with:

  • YouTube videos
  • Downloaded movies
  • Recorded videos
  • Podcasts
  • Older music files
  • Poorly encoded audio
  • Videos converted from other formats

Try playing the same AirPods with several different sources.

For example, compare Apple Music, YouTube, a locally stored video, and a different streaming service. If only one app or file sounds quiet, the AirPods probably aren’t the problem.

13. Update your AirPods firmware

AirPods receive firmware updates that can include bug fixes and improvements.

You don’t manually install these updates from a normal Software Update screen. Apple delivers them automatically while your AirPods are charging and within Bluetooth range of an iPhone, iPad, or Mac connected to Wi-Fi.

  1. Connect your AirPods.
  2. Open Settings.
  3. Tap Bluetooth.
  4. Tap the ⓘ button next to your AirPods.
  5. Scroll to the About section.
  6. Check the Firmware Version.

Now, compare the version with the recently released AirPods firmware update.

14. Forget and reset your AirPods

If you’ve tried the settings above and your AirPods still sound unusually quiet, resetting them is a reasonable next step.

First, forget the AirPods:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Bluetooth.
  3. Tap the ⓘ button next to your AirPods.
  4. Tap Forget This Device.

Then reset the AirPods according to their model.

AirPods 1, 2, 3 and AirPods Pro 1 or 2

  1. Put the AirPods in their case.
  2. Close the lid.
  3. Wait 30 seconds.
  4. Open the lid.
  5. If necessary, forget the AirPods from Bluetooth settings.
  6. Press and hold the setup button on the back of the case for about 15 seconds.
  7. Wait for the status light to flash amber and then white.
  8. Pair the AirPods again.

AirPods 4, AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3

The reset procedure is different because these newer charging cases don’t use the same physical setup-button workflow.

Put the AirPods in the case, close the lid, wait 30 seconds, then open the lid and follow Apple’s current reset instructions for your model.

Finally, re-pair your AirPods to your iPhone and check the sound again.

Why your AirPods may sound quieter over time

If you’ve owned the same AirPods for several years, physical wear can absolutely become part of the problem. But I wouldn’t automatically say that every pair loses volume after two years.

A gradual reduction in perceived volume can have several causes:

  • Debris blocking the acoustic mesh
  • Worn or poorly fitting ear tips
  • Changes in the way the AirPods seal in your ears
  • Hearing-protection settings
  • Personalized Volume
  • Conversation Awareness
  • EQ changes
  • Audio balance settings
  • A problem with one AirPod
  • Firmware or software problems
  • Battery or hardware degradation

If cleaning and troubleshooting don’t restore the sound, the AirPods may need service rather than another software tweak.

When should you replace your AirPods?

If your AirPods are several years old and none of the troubleshooting steps above make a meaningful difference, replacement may eventually make more sense than continuing to chase software settings.

But before spending money on a new pair, I’d do these three things first:

  1. Clean the AirPods properly.
  2. Check the iPhone’s audio and hearing-safety settings.
  3. Test the AirPods with another iPhone or audio source.

That last test is particularly useful.

If the same AirPods sound quiet on another device, the problem is more likely to be with the AirPods themselves. If they sound normal on another device, I’d look at the original iPhone’s settings instead.

Final thoughts

When AirPods sound quieter than expected, I wouldn’t immediately crank the volume to 100% or assume they’re dying.

With iOS 27 and the latest AirPods models, more factors now control your listening experience. Personalised Volume can automatically adjust media, Conversation Awareness can temporarily lower it, Headphone Safety can limit loud audio, and custom EQ or Headphone Accommodations can change how you perceive certain frequencies.

And if you’re tempted to solve the problem simply by listening louder, I’d resist that temptation. A clearer, better-fitting AirPod at a moderate volume is much better than constantly pushing the volume slider toward maximum.

Did you successfully make your AirPods sound louder and fix volume issues?

mainEntity.name: What if I don't see Cycle Count in my Settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cycle Count appears under Settings > Battery > Battery Health on iPhone 15 or later with iOS 17.4 or later. iPhone 14 and earlier do not show it in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Is a high cycle count always bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Check Maximum Capacity, any Service warning, and whether the battery lasts through your usual day. Cycle count alone is not a replacement deadline.

mainEntity.name: Can I trust third-party apps for battery stats?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use Settings on iPhone 15 or later, or a trusted desktop diagnostic tool on an older model. Avoid uploading analytics files to unfamiliar services.

mainEntity.name: How do I keep my iPhone battery health at 100%?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't keep battery health at 100% forever. Heat and charging habits affect battery ageing; see our guide to maintaining iPhone battery health for ways to slow it down.

title.rendered: Meow Madness codes (October 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Meow Madness Codes on October 07, 2026

Get ready to play a chaotic game of tag as a cat in Meow Madness! You’ll take on the role of either a Runner or a Tagger, with both sides going against each other to come out on top. If you want to dominate the competition, you’ll need to get your hands on the strongest cats, which means having plenty of Fish to upgrade them.

Getting enough of this resource can prove to be tricky, but thankfully, the developers have released several codes that can give you Fish and other rewards for free. So, let’s take a look at the complete list of all working Meow Madness codes you can redeem right now.

All working Meow Madness codes

  • HAT – Free Hat
  • Fish – 500 Fish

As of now, these are the only active Meow Madness codes available. Make sure to redeem them as soon as possible, as codes can expire without warning, leaving you unable to claim their rewards.

Expired or unverified Meow Madness codes

No Meow Madness codes have expired yet, but stay up to date with the codes above so you don’t miss one.

How to redeem Meow Madness codes

Now that you know all the active codes, it’s also crucial to know how to redeem them. Luckily, the process is quite simple and only takes a few minutes. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to redeem Meow Madness codes:

  1. Fire up Meow Madness on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Click on More on the left side of the screen.
  4. Open Codes.
  5. Paste a working code and click Confirm to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed the rewards, they should be added to your inventory automatically.

Where to find more Meow Madness codes

The developers don’t release new Meow Madness codes on a fixed schedule. Most new codes appear alongside major game updates, seasonal events, or community milestones.

To stay updated, you can:

  • Join the official Meow Madness Discord server for announcements.
  • Follow the game’s Roblox page for update notifications.
  • Bookmark this page, as we’ll keep it updated whenever new codes are released.

If you’re looking for more Roblox freebies, check out our latest Blue Lock Farm codes, Soccer Zero codes, Hypershot codes, and our complete Roblox Game Codes hub.

FAQs

What are Fish used for in Meow Madness?

Fish is the primary in-game currency in Meow Madness, which you can spend on upgrading your cat or purchasing cosmetics.

Why is my Meow Madness code not working?

Make sure you’ve entered the right code as displayed above. If it’s still not working, the code might’ve expired or already been redeemed.

mainEntity.name: What if I don't see Cycle Count in my Settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cycle Count appears under Settings > Battery > Battery Health on iPhone 15 or later with iOS 17.4 or later. iPhone 14 and earlier do not show it in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Is a high cycle count always bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Check Maximum Capacity, any Service warning, and whether the battery lasts through your usual day. Cycle count alone is not a replacement deadline.

mainEntity.name: Can I trust third-party apps for battery stats?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use Settings on iPhone 15 or later, or a trusted desktop diagnostic tool on an older model. Avoid uploading analytics files to unfamiliar services.

mainEntity.name: How do I keep my iPhone battery health at 100%?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't keep battery health at 100% forever. Heat and charging habits affect battery ageing; see our guide to maintaining iPhone battery health for ways to slow it down.

title.rendered: How to see parts and service history on iPhone (iOS 27)

content.rendered:
When you send your iPhone for a repair or plan to buy a refurbished one, its service history is more important than most people realise. Apple’s Parts and Service History feature makes it easy to see whether key components like the screen, battery, display, camera, or Logic Board have been replaced.

In this guide, you’ll learn how to check Parts and Service History on your iPhone and understand what each label really means, so you can make smarter decisions with confidence.

What is parts and service history on iPhone?

Parts and Service History is a built-in iOS feature that logs any component that has been replaced or serviced. It indicates whether the part is genuine Apple hardware, an unknown third‑party component, or a used part that was previously installed in another device.

Apple introduced this feature to:

  • Improve repair transparency.
  • Protect users from poor-quality components.
  • Help buyers verify that the repair used genuine Apple parts.
  • Check the used or refurbished iPhone is original, avoiding scams.

Having genuine parts is important as they work better and last longer. Also, it helps keep up the resale value of your iPhone.

How Apple’s parts and service history works

Apple uses software and repair-calibration processes to identify and configure replaced components. When a supported repair is completed, Apple’s systems can verify the component and install the calibration data required for it to work correctly.

For supported repairs, Repair Assistant can finish the calibration process after a part is replaced. On supported devices, it can also calibrate a previously used part from another device of the same model.

The best part is:

  • You cannot edit or reset this section. If a component has been serviced more than once, only the most recent service appears.
  • Apple does not track personal data.
  • It is strictly read-only information.

Note: If your iPhone has never been repaired, the Parts and Service History section will not appear at all.

When you should check parts and service history

You should check this section in several situations:

  • Before buying a used or refurbished iPhone: Verify repair claims, confirm genuine parts, and avoid hidden issues.
  • After screen, battery, or camera replacement: Ensure the repair was completed correctly.
  • When troubleshooting performance issues like battery draining fast, Face ID or camera problems, or display issues.
  • Before selling or trading in your iPhone: Buyers may check it for genuine parts, which increases trust and value.

iPhone models that support parts and service history

Apple gradually rolled out this feature across models starting from iOS 15.2 and later:

If you have an iPhone 15 or later, you can also see if the replaced Apple hardware was previously used in another iPhone.

How to see parts and service history on iPhone (step by step)

Follow these simple steps:

  1. Open Settings and go to General.
  2. Tap About.
  3. If your iPhone has been repaired, you will see Parts and Service History.
  4. Tap it to see the list of replaced components like Display, Battery, Camera, etc.
  5. Each part shows a status label such as Genuine, Used, Unknown, and Unverified.
  6. Tap the component for more information about it, including the date of service. Ensure your iPhone is connected to the internet.

If the repair was not completed, it shows a Finish Repair message. It means the repair has not yet completed the required calibration process.

Understanding parts and service history labels

  • Genuine: Official Apple component properly paired and calibrated.
  • Used (iPhone 15 and Later): Genuine Apple part previously used in another iPhone. Still verified by Apple.
  • Unknown: Apple cannot verify the part. May be third-party or improperly installed.
  • Unverified: Logic Board was previously replaced as part of a repair. This may affect certain features, such as Apple Pay.
  • Finish Repair Message: If the setup or calibration was not done after the replacement, you will see it. You can’t use Face ID or Touch ID to unlock your device or to sign in to apps until it’s done.

To finish the repair, connect the iPhone to Wi-Fi and make sure the battery is above 20 per cent. Then open Settings > General > About > Parts & Service History. Tap Restart & Finish Repair. Finally, follow the on-screen instructions.

What genuine Apple part means

A Genuine Apple Part means the repair was completed using genuine Apple parts and Apple’s repair/calibration processes.

It does not necessarily mean the repair was performed only by Apple or an Apple Authorised Service Provider. Apple also provides genuine parts to Independent Repair Providers and, where supported, through Self Service Repair.

Benefits

  • Proper calibration and compatibility with supported iOS features.
  • Repairs meet Apple’s performance, security, privacy, and safety expectations.
  • A clearer repair record for buyers and trade-in providers.
  • Higher resale and trade-in value.
  • Safer long-term use.

What used part means

A Used label means the part was already used or installed in another iPhone.

On supported iPhone models, Repair Assistant can calibrate compatible reused parts from another device of the same model. A used part may function differently from a new part because of prior use or modification.

What unknown part or non-genuine part means

This label appears when Apple cannot verify the replacement part or its repair status. It can appear when a part is non-genuine, isn’t functioning as expected, hasn’t been verified and linked after the repair, or has been modified or otherwise cannot be verified.

An Unknown label does not automatically prove that a part is counterfeit or that the iPhone is unsafe. It means Apple could not verify the part or repair status. An Unknown part might affect the trade-in value of the device.

Possible downsides

  • Battery health issues.
  • Face ID or camera problems.
  • Lower resale value.
  • The part may not perform as expected.
  • Some repaired functions may require further diagnosis or calibration.
  • The Unknown label may affect trade-in value.

Messages about replaced parts or multiple repairs

To help you combat poor-quality servicing, your iPhone shows a notification the first time you unlock it after a repair and again in five days if an unknown part is found.

This indicates the replacement part:

  • Is non-genuine.
  • Isn’t functioning as expected.
  • Hasn’t been verified and linked to your iPhone after the repair was done.
  • Has been modified or can’t be verified.

You can contact the repair service provider about this.

For display and battery repairs, you may also see the message “Apple has updated the device information for this iPhone.” Apple says this indicates that it has updated device information maintained for safety analysis and to improve future products.

If a component problem significantly affects the device’s functionality and needs attention, your iPhone can show a one-time notification that remains in Parts and Service History until dismissed.

What to do if your iPhone shows unknown or unverified parts

You have a few options:

  • Visit Apple, an Apple Authorised Service Provider, or a reputable Independent Repair Provider with access to genuine Apple parts.
  • Ask the repair provider to diagnose the part and complete any required calibration.
  • Replace the part with a genuine Apple component. If the issue involves a previously used part, check whether it is protected by Activation Lock.
  • If buying a used iPhone, ask the seller about the repair and consider the potential effect of an Unknown part on trade-in value.

If buying a used iPhone, you may negotiate the price or consider returning the device to avoid future hassles and security issues.

Note that repairs performed by Independent Repair Providers are not covered by Apple’s warranty or AppleCare plans, although the provider may offer its own repair warranty.

Best Practices to Keep Service History Clean

  • Choose Apple, an Apple Authorised Service Provider, Apple’s Self Service Repair program, or an Independent Repair Provider with access to genuine Apple parts where supported.
  • Complete repairs properly and check everything before accepting the device.
  • If Finish Repair appears, complete the repair with Repair Assistant.
  • Check Parts & Service History after the repair.
  • Keep service receipts and repair documentation.
  • Before a trade-in, make sure there are no unfinished repairs and prepare the device using the current iOS 27 Ready for Repair or Trade In workflow when applicable.

Note: If you have multiple repairs for the same component, your iPhone will show the status of the most recent repair.

Final thoughts

Checking Parts and Service History on iPhone is simple but extremely powerful. It helps buyers avoid scams, owners verify repair quality, and sellers understand what a future buyer or trade-in provider may see.

For iOS 27, the feature is more useful than ever because Apple now distinguishes between Genuine, Used, Unknown, and Unverified parts and provides Repair Assistant for completing calibration on supported repairs.

If you are preparing an iPhone for repair or trade-in, iOS 27 also gives you a new Ready for Repair or Trade-In workflow through Find My, making the preparation process different from older iOS versions.

If you found this guide helpful, save it and share it with anyone buying or selling an iPhone.

FAQs

How do I see parts and service history on iPhone?

Go to Settings > General > About > Parts and Service History. It will only appear if your iPhone has been repaired before.

Is it safe to buy an iPhone with non-genuine parts?

An Unknown label means Apple could not verify the part or repair status. The phone may still work, but you should understand what was repaired and consider that the Unknown part might affect trade-in value.

Can I reset parts and service history?

No. This information cannot be erased or changed.

Do third-party repairs affect warranty?

Yes. Unauthorised repairs may void parts of your warranty.

Does service history affect resale value?

Yes. iPhones with genuine parts usually sell for more.

Can AppleCare+ be used with unknown parts?

Apple may require replacement with genuine parts before providing coverage; otherwise, the warranty may be void.

mainEntity.name: What if I don't see Cycle Count in my Settings?

mainEntity.name: Is a high cycle count always bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Check Maximum Capacity, any Service warning, and whether the battery lasts through your usual day. Cycle count alone is not a replacement deadline.

mainEntity.name: Can I trust third-party apps for battery stats?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use Settings on iPhone 15 or later, or a trusted desktop diagnostic tool on an older model. Avoid uploading analytics files to unfamiliar services.

mainEntity.name: Does service history affect resale value?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iPhones with genuine parts usually sell for more.

mainEntity.name: Can AppleCare+ be used with unknown parts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple may require replacement with genuine parts before providing coverage; otherwise, the warranty may be void.

@graph.name: How to See Parts and Service History on iPhone
@graph.description: Learn how to check if your iPhone has undergone any repairs and view the details of replaced parts like the display, battery, or camera.

step.name: Open Settings app
step.text: Unlock your iPhone and open the Settings app from your home screen.

itemListElement.text: Unlock your iPhone and tap on the Settings icon.

step.name: Go to General
step.text: Scroll down and tap on the General option to proceed.

itemListElement.text: Scroll and select the General menu in Settings.

step.name: Tap About
step.text: In the General menu, tap on About to view your device information.

itemListElement.text: Tap About to open your iPhone's basic details.

step.name: Check Parts and Service History
step.text: If your iPhone has been serviced, you’ll see a Parts and Service History section. Tap it to view more details.

itemListElement.text: Look for the Parts and Service History section and tap on it.

step.name: Review component details
step.text: You’ll see a list of replaced components with labels like Genuine, Used, or Unknown. Tap a component to get more info, including service date.

itemListElement.text: Tap any listed component to see more information and service details.

blockGraphs.question: How do I see parts and service history on iPhone?
blockGraphs.answer: Go to Settings > General > About > Parts and Service History. It will only appear if your iPhone has been repaired before.

blockGraphs.question: Is it safe to buy an iPhone with non-genuine parts?
blockGraphs.answer: An Unknown label means Apple could not verify the part or repair status. The phone may still work, but you should understand what was repaired and consider that the Unknown part might affect trade-in value.

blockGraphs.question: Can I reset parts and service history?
blockGraphs.answer: No. This information cannot be erased or changed.

blockGraphs.question: Do third-party repairs affect warranty?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes. Unauthorised repairs may void parts of your warranty.

blockGraphs.question: Does service history affect resale value?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes. iPhones with genuine parts usually sell for more.

blockGraphs.question: Can AppleCare+ be used with unknown parts?
blockGraphs.answer: Apple may require replacement with genuine parts before providing coverage; otherwise, the warranty may be void.
